projects.title: 做了个抖音运营助手 Chrome 扩展：推荐流挂机 + 关键词搜索 + AI 神评
projects.author: gybin02
projects.summary: 开发者自荐：我是波波抖音内容运营助手的开发者，下面讲怎么做、怎么用，不讲流量保证。 ### 1. 痛点：抖音日常运营，重复动作太多 做抖音号，每天都要刷推荐流、找对标视频、回评论、盯意向客户。动作本身不难，难在每天重复、耗时，而且人工一累就容易漏掉真正想买的人。 ### 2. 它是怎么做到的 - 跑在 Chrome / Edge 的抖音网页版里，不用输入抖音账号密码，也不用导 Cookie ，在你已登录的官方页面里执行。 - 推荐流挂机：自动浏览推荐流，模拟完播停留和点赞、收藏，停留时长和互动概率可以自己调。 - 关键词搜索获客：多关键词队列搜索，结合抖音官方排序和视频时长筛选，批量定位对标视频，自动记录已处理视频，不重复处理。 - 评论区截流：在视频评论区直接发表评论，或在同行视频的高意向评论下做楼中楼回复，带包含词 / 排除词过滤。 - 云端大模型 AI 神评：结合视频标题和前排热评生成评论，支持自定义 Prompt 和语气，也支持纯文本话术库。 - 拟人节奏：随机停留、随机互动概率，遇到验证码或频控提示会平稳暂停，不硬冲。 - 记录都在本地，可以导出 CSV 复盘。 ### 3. 四种预设模式 - 稳健养号：新号、提权防风控 - 智能获客：均衡高效，转化首选 - 爆客冲量：老号抢量 - 极速测试：快速验证策略 模式可以一键切换，里面的停留、互动、AI 风格也可以自己再调。 ### 4. 安装与价格 - 安装：官网下载离线安装包 ZIP ，解压后在浏览器扩展管理里开开发者模式，加载已解压的扩展程序。 - 试用版免费：单次最多处理 15 个视频、单次挂机限时 15 分钟、每日 20 次免费 AI 神评。 - 永久专业版：前 50 名早鸟 ¥19.9 终身买断，名额满后恢复 ¥19.9/月。支付宝直付，付款成功后页面显示激活码，一机一码，粘贴到扩展里激活。剩余名额官网没给实时数字，草稿不写还剩多少名。 ### 5. 限制，一定要先说清楚 - 不能保证零风险，也不能绕过平台审核和平台规则。 - 请遵守抖音社区公约，合理设置单日互动上限，不滥发引流广告，不在短时间内超大频次操作。 - 自动化工具仍有账号风险，节奏和数量要按自己账号的实际情况调，不要无脑拉满。 ### 6. 链接 官网： https://dy.tihub.com/

projects.title: [Dev-circuit-ultra]-自己做的比 OpenSpec 更少上下文、更少流程、更快交付的开发 loop
projects.author: iswalterwu
projects.summary: 这两天优化了自己在用的开发工作流，好处是比 OpenSpec 的上下文维护轻量得多，但不丢框架深度和交付细节。 经过测试，在较短的开发周期下，已经能体现较 OpenSpec 超过 -30% 的 token 成本、-48% 的 cache-read 以及 -51% 的文档维护。仓库里还放了一次单会话的开放任务 A/B，方向和这个一致（模型成本 −29.9%、输入+输出 tokens −36.2%、cache-read −48.6%、留存文档 −51.6%）。 同时，记账与开发完全分离，确保开发过程不会被过期设计或旧想法污染。 [项目地址]( https://github.com/iswalterwu/dev-circuit-ultra) [项目概览]( https://github.com/iswalterwu/dev-circuit-ultra/blob/main/assets/after-setup-en.svg) ## 它是什么 一套面向独立开发者的五步功能开发循环，以 skill 的形式加载到 Claude Code、Codex、pi、DeepSeek Harness 等编码 agent 里： 1. 设计澄清 + 意图卡 2. 单个能独立验收的端到端切片 3. 实现 + 验证 4. 独立审核（普通功能一次；框架级改动加一次结构审） 5. 验收 + 合并 和常见的规格驱动工具不同，它不维护 proposal / tasks / archive，仓库里只保留**现行设计**：设计变了就原地覆盖或删除，功能收尾就删卡。决策历史（包括被否掉的方案）写进项目之外的私有 git 账本；强隔离下，dev 容器没有账本挂载、没有路径、没有凭证，开发 agent 读不到。 这条边界是文件系统级的，不是 prompt 约定。README 里把隔离分成弱 / 中 / 强三档，明确写了只有容器方案才叫"保证"。 ## 最新 A/B：省在哪 同一个 records CLI 开放任务、每个 skill 一个会话、最终交付物盲评： | 相对 OpenSpec | Dev-circuit-ultra | OpenSpec | 差异 | | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | | 模型成本 | $0.0743 | $0.1060 | −29.9% | | 输入 + 输出 tokens | 72,308 | 113,337 | −36.2% | | 缓存读取 tokens | 1,891,968 | 3,678,333 | −48.6% | | assistant 轮次 | 39 | 50 | −22% | | 留存文档 | 2 文件 / 132 行 | 3 文件 / 273 行 | −51.6% | | 盲评总分（30） | 27 | 26 | +1 | 欢迎大家一起探讨，跟大家学习！

projects.title: 【工具自荐】UnimeType：不用来回切输入法，一个英文键盘连续写中/日/英混排句子的跨平台输入法与在线转换工具
projects.author: losdwind
projects.summary: UnimeType 是一个专为双语与多语言混输设计的跨平台输入法及在线转换工具。 平时在写技术文档、工作消息或日常聊天时，一句话里经常同时夹杂中文、英文单词、代码标识符或日文，用传统输入法每遇到一个英文词都要按 Shift / Caps Lock / Ctrl + Space 来回切模式，还会遇到拼音候选框吞掉英文单词的问题。 UnimeType 采用了「先用普通拉丁键盘一气呵成打完草稿，再按一下一键整句转换（Convert）」的交互方式： 免切换整句混输转换（Convert）：打字时没有候选框干扰，全程在标准英文键盘上连续输入拼音（中文）、罗马音（日文）、Hinglish（印地语）、Arabizi（阿拉伯语）或 Translit（俄语）与英文单词混合的句子（例如直接输入 wo gang push le new build, mingtian morning kan xia metrics 或 kyou wa Tokyo de meeting ga arimasu），写完按一次转换键（桌面端默认 Caps Lock，移动端点 Convert），自动将拼音/罗马音片段转为母语文字（我刚 push 了 new build，明天 morning 看下 metrics / 今日は Tokyo で meeting があります），句中的英文词汇、代码变量、URL 与数字原样保留。 输入框原位润色（Polish）与解释（Explain）：在当前聊天框或编辑器里直接润色双语草稿，或选中陌生缩写/习语弹出三行只读解释卡片，无需切去浏览器复制粘贴。 平时打字零网络请求 + 开源本地模型：普通按键输入完全在本地，仅在你主动触发 Convert / Polish / Explain 时发起请求；除了官方云端额度（注册即赠 1,000 体验积分）外，还支持免费接入自有 API Key，或在本地通过 LM Studio 离线运行我们在 Hugging Face 开源的专用微调转写模型（UnimeType/Transliteration-2.0-4B 与 0.8B）。 免安装网页在线体验与全平台下载： 官网首页： 免登录网页在线转换台（中英混输）： 免登录网页在线转换台（日英罗马音混输）： 全平台客户端下载（iOS / Android / macOS / Windows / Linux / ChromeOS）：

projects.title: [开源推荐] SnapOCR：深色界面截图也能准确取字的离线 OCR 工具
projects.author: q037180

github.name: q037180/SnapOCR
github.description: 离线截图 OCR / Offline screenshot OCR for dark IDEs & dark-mode pages — 自动反色增强，识别结果进本地可搜索历史。按一次热键框选即取字；批量 / PDF / 表格转 Excel / 长截图。识别全程在本机，不上传截图。Windows · MIT。

projects.summary: 按一次热键框选屏幕即完成识别并复制到剪贴板。针对深色 IDE 与暗色网页，识别前自动反色并做 CLAHE 对比度增强，解决低对比度文本整行漏检。结果进入本地可搜索历史，可导出 Excel；内置简体中文模型，默认全程离线、不上传截图。Windows 绿色包解压即用，MIT。 亮点 1. 把「深色截图识别不准」当成首要问题解决。 系统自带 OCR 处理白底黑字没问题，但深色主题截图（代码、报错栈、暗色文档）经常整行漏检。这里先按整体亮度判断是否需要反色，再用 CLAHE 提局部对比度，最后才送进识别模型。 2. 识别结果不是「复制完就没了」。 每次结果自动进本地历史，关键词即时过滤、双击重新复制、可批量导出 txt/docx/pdf/md/xlsx。查一周前识别过的一段报错是秒级的事。 3. 表格转 Excel 不会错列。 不少工具按「行内间隙中点」切列，遇到某行有空单元格就整行少一格、右侧列全部左移。这里改成把单元格的水平区段合并成全局列带，保证每行列数恒定，空格留空。 4. 长截图能扛住动态内容。 页面里有视频、滚动条、时钟时，模板匹配会被这些区域带偏、导致拼接断裂。这里用缩略粗搜 + 全分辨率细化 +「逐列差异中位数」判据 + 动态列自动屏蔽。 5. 完全离线。 内置简体中文 PP-OCR 模型，识别不联网、不上传截图；只有「截屏翻译」会把识别出的文本发给翻译服务，且可在设置里关掉。 6. 工程记录公开。 仓库里有一份 QA 报告，记录了 40 项测试审查修复的根因与实测数据（例如 docx 导出 10 万行从 419 秒降到 3.4 秒），可以当作「一个人怎么系统性自测桌面应用」的参考。 截图或演示视频 深色截图效果对比： 15 秒串联演示： 在线介绍页： 补充说明 这是自荐（本人项目）。MIT 许可，当前版本 v1.0.3；有 README / CHANGELOG / docs/QA-REPORT-2026-11-06.md 三份文档。Windows 10/11 x64 提供 7z / zip 绿色包，Linux / macOS 可从源码运行。

projects.title: Show HN: I asked HN about AI agentic setups, here are 750 of the comments mapped
projects.author: eggbrain
projects.summary: A few days back I posted here asking about how people were using AI / doing agentic coding (see: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50366117 ). Needless to say, I was overwhelmed by the response! The one challenge I found, however, was that the comments were almost impossible to parse: some users answered my questions in the format I provided, others answered in any order, but either way it was really hard to get a picture of who was using what from that thread alone. So, I spent last night building an interactive site out of people's answers. I used Claude to pull the tools, models and plans out of each comment, with every number linked back to the original comments it came from. projects.summary: Fun 是一款静态类型的自研编程语言，它直接转译（Transpile）为可读的 C 语言代码。该项目专注于提供极简的语言表面、强大的静态类型系统、实用的并发原语以及对编辑器极其友好的工具链（内置 FLS 语言服务器、格式化、诊断等）。 核心特性： 1. 高性能 C 转译： 编译产物为 C 语言，具备极佳的跨平台便携性、极低的运行时开销与零性能损耗的 C 语言互操作能力。 2. 混合并发模型： 同时支持 M:N 虚拟线程（通过 fork 实现轻量级 I/O 任务与异步资源加载）以及 1:1 系统原生 OS 线程（std.thread，用于固定高帧率的系统如渲染和物理引擎）。 3. 灵活的数值类型： 提供高层默认数值类型（num, dec）的同时，支持固定宽度标量类型（i32, u64）以及任意宽度的整数（iN, uN），极其适合游戏引擎底层与系统级开发。 4. 开箱即用的工具链： 内置代码格式化（fun -fmt）、静态分析（fun lint）与调试映射（fun -g）。

projects.author: yoavshmariahu
projects.summary: I’ve been doing a lot of solo development lately and found myself hitting Claude token limits halfway through the week constantly. Even with a Max plan, I’d have to switch over to Codex or Cursor, and it would be a bit difficult to get used to the nuances of each harness. It’s still a problem for me, but I finally built Thinker to save me some tokens and help me get a bit more out of my coding agent subscriptions. I started off a bit in the dark about how token billing works, and had to dig deeper to figure out what workflows ended up hurting my budget the most. By far, it was large context windows. Claude tries to help out on costs by offering prompt caching - which is sort of a bandage on the bigger problem: context bloat. I find that my context window gets bloated with unneeded tokens in two main ways: Tool outputs from subtasks that are long finished. File reads, Bash commands, MCP outputs, etc. Main idea is that the model finished the work but carries the weight of it for every subsequent call - translating to wasted token usage. CLAUDE.md / AGENTS.md getting way too big. Lots of content gets dumped into these files as your agents work in your repo. I found that it’s not clear what is actually useful to be included there. Every token here counts, because it will be paid for in every session, and its cost scales linearly with the duration of your session. Thinker addresses both of these issues. We have a proxy that wires in between your harness and model to cut out old context that we determine is no longer needed for your current task. Based on the provider you’re using, we determine the right time to batch enough context to cut that justifies the cache re-write cost, which gets paid off after X subsequent calls. We also analyze your sessions and figure out which parts of your instruction files don’t really get used - and send you suggestions to cut or compress those sections. Thinker will kick off a subagent to do that work for you and open a PR you can review. Finally, we use your sessions to record knowledge notes by distilling your sessions with a cheap model (Haiku, Luna). These notes are then served at prompt time via a cross-encoder, also on your machine, that decides whether a note is relevant to the user’s prompt. Here are some data points to show how exactly Thinker saves you coding agent costs: https://thinker.sh/see-the-data If you’re hitting problems at all with usage limits, it’d be great to hear how you’ve been trying to mitigate it. Our open-source repo here (MIT License): https://github.com/yoavshmariahu/thinker

projects.summary: 自荐一个开源的 Mac 看图软件 Flipic，解决的是拍完照之后的"挑片"这一步。 拍完一场活动，几百上千张照片拷进电脑，先得把能用的挑出来。Mac 自带的「预览」一次只能开一张；开 Lightroom 又得先建图库、等导入，还没开始挑就先花几分钟。Flipic 干的就是中间这一步：双击文件夹里随便一张照片，它直接读这个文件夹——不导入、不建库、不要账号，左右方向键往下翻，4800 万像素的 RAW 按住方向键连翻也跟得上。看不清焦点的话，鼠标停在眼睛上按 0，立刻放大到 100%；连拍拿不准留哪张，按 C 两张并排比。 挑中的照片按 1–5 打星，星级按 XMP 标准写进文件元数据（JPEG/HEIC 写进文件本身，相机 RAW 写在同名 .xmp 边车文件里，RAW 一个字节不动），之后在 Lightroom、Bridge、Capture One 里都能直接读到，换软件不用重打一遍。要留的按 P 标记，存成访达标签，不开 Flipic 在访达里也能找到。活动照片几百张的场景还有个清理模式（⇧⌘K）：用系统自带的 Vision 框架在本机把相似连拍、完全重复、闭眼、糊掉的照片分出来并推荐保留哪张，删不删、删哪些由你决定，⌘Z 可撤销。 几条设计上的坚持：默认完全联网功能为零（不收集任何数据），清理检测全部在本机跑，照片不上传；安装包不到 4 MB，Developer ID 签名并通过 Apple 公证；支持 JPEG/PNG/HEIC/WebP/GIF/TIFF/AVIF/JPEG XL/PSD/OpenEXR 和常见相机 RAW（ARW、CR2、CR3、NEF、RAF、DNG 等），界面有 14 种语言，macOS 13 起 Apple 芯片和 Intel 都能用。Swift + AppKit 手写，零第三方依赖。 完全免费且开源（MIT），看图、打星、标记、筛选、清理模式都在免费范围里；另有一个 ¥68 买断的 Pro，是大批量挑片的一些增强功能（按人比闭眼、修图前后对比之类），免费版已经够大多数人用。 安装包和更多截图见官网，也支持从源码构建。现在用它的基本都是摄影师，很多功能是他们提的，欢迎试用提意见。

projects.author: lssvip
projects.summary: 嗨，大家好，最近又做了一个小东西。这次没有选择做网站，而是做了一款微信小程序。 受一句话影响：如果你想快速验证你的想法能不能行，就是收费。如果有人愿意付费，那就说明你的这个项目创意是可以的，如果没有，就要及时止损，停止开发，果断放弃。 正巧又看到微信文章说个人开发者可以开通虚拟支付通道。这就是把所有链路都打通了，就等着验证你的想法了。 想法来源：最近自己不是用 AI 做了一些小网站吗？经常有些小文本需要经常的复制粘贴，比如网站统计代码，我的网站只有前端，没有后端，每次新增页面都是 AI 给写好了，手动添加统计代码的。需要经常用到这个代码，每次用我就登录一次网站获取统计代码，后来我就保存在了 TXT ，每次复制还是麻烦，于是就有了这个保存在小程序里。可以快速的复制，然后去黏贴。 就这样，这个重复的动作在一次一次的优化下，越来越简单，链路越来越少，到最后直接 0 链路了，解决的方法就是不在添加新页面了。 网站不添加新页面了，但是想法不能停。于是就做了这个小程序-LiteNoteGo,已经上架好几天。主打短文本记录，本地存储。想邀请大家体验一下的。 谢谢。 我的账号里还有点铜板。

github.name: jingchengyin/codex-kanban-plugin
github.description: A Kanban board for Codex power users to manage concurrent chats, tasks, and usage history. 专为 Codex 重度使用者设计，看板模式管理并发对话，组织对话合集

projects.summary: 产品截图 1: 产品截图 2: 插件使用场景一 插件设计之初是为我自己的需求服务，应该很多人和我一样是 Codex 重度用户，而且会同时开很多个会话，经常是这个会话在出方案、另一个会话在 worktree 写代码、其他还开了一堆的会话在排查线上问题，同时要并行处理很多事情。 当然并行处理并不是阻塞点，毕竟是 AI 处理，阻塞点在于每一个对话结束后都要我们一个一个去 check 才行，这就导致经常会忘记 check，或者不想现在就 check，那随着处理的东西越来越多，之前没有立即 check 的对话，很可能会被漏掉，几十几百个会话里面，漏看一两个是常有的事情，我经常是隔了几天发现这个问题还没被处理，然后来 Codex 根据关键字搜对话，这个时候我又得花时间重新回想一遍这个问题的背景。 甚至有时候会出现你隔了很久来 check 的时候，发现 Codex 竟然需要你输入补充信息，这就更难受了。。。 插件使用场景二 上面我们重点聊的是并行处理的问题，我经常还会遇到的一个场景是，开多个对话分模块来处理同一个需求，然后这个模块的所有内容我都会在同一个对话里进行，这样做的目的是啥呢，就是保证不同的模块的上下文都是连贯的，一个对话专注处理一个模块，拥有我关于这个模块的所有输入。如果需求开发的时间跨度比较长，就经常会忘记某个模块。如果没有这个插件的话，我目前的解法是统一重命名 + 置顶。 再举个例子，就是我们日常工作中还存在很多调研性的需求，这类工作不一定要及时处理，只是先调研，可能到后面某一天的时候来会拿出来，到时候要找的话，要么是关键字搜索，要么就是把这些对话先置顶。这类需求一多，管理起来就越来越麻烦 插件使用场景三 我目前的开发流程基本都是写让 Codex 写方案文档/设计稿 -> Goal 模式实现 -> 出验收文档 -> 推送 MR，对我来说要 check 的就 3 个东西： 1. 方案文档 2. 验收文档 3. MR 链接 所以需要不管我在这个对话中聊了多少轮，这三个东西我都能快速的找到，但现在做不到，我经常需要翻上下文来找 插件介绍 以上，便是这个插件要解决的问题。 Codex-Kanban-Plugin：A Kanban board for Codex power users to manage concurrent chats, tasks, and usage history. 专为 Codex 重度使用者设计，看板模式管理并发对话，组织对话合集 GitHub jingchengyin/codex-kanban-plugin 看板 看板按状态分列： 需要你处理 正在运行 未读（对话已完成但还未读） 空闲（对话已完成且已经完成） 执行异常（比如模型失败，排队超时等等） 看板上展示的信息包括： 所属文件夹 使用的分支/worktree 模型和思考强度 计划模式 目标模式 最近一次的用户输入 最近一次 Codex 处理所花费的 token 和时间 自动解析出来的成果（目前包括 MR 链接 + 计划文档 + 飞书文档） 所属合集 支持自定义配置成果解析 URL： 如果存在需要用户输入的会话，看板卡片会直接展示待确认卡片，可直接在插件内操作，无需跳转会话 合集 对应上述场景二，合集支持把多条对话关联起来，统一管理说明、进度、成果和验收清单。 事项有四个状态：待开始、进行中、待验收、已验收，状态由你手动更新。 看板页面也可以快速加入合集： 合集 icon 和颜色支持自定义： 关于安全性 插件只读访问本机 Codex 对话数据，所有数据均保存在 CODEXHOME/kanban/workspace.sqlite。没设置 CODEXHOME 时，默认位置是 ~/.codex/kanban/workspace.sqlite。 快速安装 目前只支持 MacOS，Windows 暂未适配，欢迎 PR 👏 把下面这段话发给 Codex，让它帮你安装： 请帮我安装 Codex-Kanban-Plugin： 从 main 分支添加插件市场，安装 codex-kanban-plugin@codex-kanban-plugin，并检查安装结果。

projects.title: Show HN: KeepPlain – ask your coding agent why a line of code exists
projects.author: kagen
projects.summary: My code is written by agents now. Git blame shows me the commit and my own name, but the reason for the code is in a session I closed weeks ago. KeepPlain saves your agent sessions. It uses git blame to find the session that corresponds to a file, line, or commit. Then it shows the original request and the reasoning behind the change. It also finds commits made by the user after the agent session and links them to the session. I also try to use the mistakes the agent makes over and over to turn them into rules for new sessions. It works with Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Pi and Antigravity. Your sessions are uploaded to my server and are kept private to you. All secrets are redacted on your machine before the upload. I’m sure there will be lots of questions about this. The plugin is MIT licensed and open source. The server is not. Teams can run their own Postgres database to store their data. KeepPlain is free for personal use and teams will pay for it. I am a solo developer and this is early on in development so please let me know where it breaks.

projects.title: Show HN: Cerea – yet another self-hosted LLM chat front end
projects.author: pviviani
projects.summary: Here is Cerea, a self-hostable, open-source (Apache 2.0) chat+agent frontend for LLMs. It works alone with any OpenAI-compatible inference provider, but it's way better when coupled with the model gateway I'm also developing, Pystino ( https://github.com/paoloviviani/Pystino ). I came to this after struggling to find a hosted chat interface that was truly open source, that I really enjoyed to use, and that was simple enough to be shared and used by family. In particular, I was looking for something that could provide the smooth and integrated user experience of commercial products for the tasks needed by family (e.g., document editing, form filling, notes and knowledge management), but backed by open models hosted wherever I decide. Then it became richer, now supporting: remote coding agents (wrapping Opencode), delegation and coordination between agents, integration between chat/projects and code agents (this one to me is a pain point for Claude, which I use at work), projects, RAG, rich artifacts support, schedules, and more. You can try it yourself, either cloning the full repo and head to Cerea/kit, or just the deploy kit with a script ( https://github.com/paoloviviani/Cerea#quick-start ). It's just a docker compose with a ./configure script that helps to generate a sensible .env for the specific scenario. It works in the browser and as a PWA on mobile. I hope you'll enjoy, feel free to reach out for questions.

projects.summary: 自荐一个自己开发的开源项目：EPUB Reading Edition（MIT）。本人是项目作者。 这是一个供 AI 编程助手使用的 EPUB 阅读与文档处理工具（AI Agent Skill），用于将用户有权处理的 EPUB 整理为带阅读导读的 Word 文档和离线 HTML 阅读器。 主要功能： EPUB 结构解析：依据 OPF manifest、spine、目录和文档结构识别阅读顺序与阅读单元，保存结构化 JSON。 AI 阅读辅助：由助手阅读全文及相关图表，撰写中文「背景」与「作者观点」两段导读。 多格式输出：生成 Word、可直接打开的单文件 HTML，以及静态网站 ZIP。 阅读标记：支持黄色高亮、部分取消和按原文顺序复制高亮；标记保存在当前浏览器本地。 AI Agent 负责阅读理解与导读，Python 负责提取、数据校验和文档/HTML 生成；脚本不内置模型 API，不能仅运行 Python 就自动完成 AI 阅读。 项目最初来自我个人改善 The Economist EPUB 精读体验的需求，之后整理成可复用工作流。目前仍保留部分专用解析规则，已用原创合成 EPUB 验证解析、Word/HTML 导出与高亮功能，不宣称兼容所有 EPUB；具体限制见 README。 仓库仅提供工具代码、模板和原创合成测试素材，不提供原刊文件或下载服务。使用者需确认输入、AI 处理和输出分享的相应权限；持有文件或订阅不自动等于获得这些许可。项目与 The Economist 没有官方合作、授权或隶属关系。

With the cli you can do a `zenith publish` and get a spot on the marketplace and a cut of the revenue. Your users can then deploy a fully managed instance. Want to test emails with SMTP? You can spin up an identical preview deployment with `zenith up` and it just works. On the roadmap is Resend and Twillio compatible email, SMS APIs, Sign in with ChatGPT, Google account connections, GPUs, sitewide notifications (mobile app maybe?) projects.title: Show HN: teletap – Your remote coding agents ask you when stuck
projects.author: megalomanu
projects.summary: Hi HN! I'm Manuel, CTO of Tandem. Most of our PRs are now written by custom coding agents on remote hosts. But we had a recurring problem: they sometimes lacked product context and consequently guessed too much. This resulted in some PRs coming back a bit off, with some wrong choices. We ended up spending more time fixing the PRs than if we had made them ourselves. So we built teletap, first for ourselves, and now for everyone. How it works: when an agent is stuck on something it can't find itself, it asks a person on the team. It picks the best person to help it, based on a short "when to ask" description each developer specifies, like "pricing owner", or AGENTS.md instructions. The question pops up on that engineer's computer. They answer it, and it goes straight back into the agent's session, which is now unblocked and can continue. If the engineer doesn't know, they just have to say so, and the agent will ask someone else. Many teams use Slack for this. We tried it too. But we didn't find it productive enough. The agent had to keep checking a thread. An idle session never saw the reply. With teletap, the answer is delivered directly into the session, even if it's idle. It works with Claude Code, Codex, Gemini, Hermes and Pi. Just install it on a device (your computer, a VM, a Docker container, a VPS...), and it finds all the installed agents and plugs into them. We were inspired by Tailscale, which we love. Devices talk peer-to-peer, encrypted end to end, and fall back to our relay only when a direct path is impossible (the relay never sees the content). It's very minimal: you don't have to live in another interface. In case you're wondering, we wrote it in Rust and everything runs over QUIC, on a single UDP socket. The most fun part of the project was the integration with agents, figuring out how to put the answer into a live session. For instance, Claude Code has an internal messaging socket (CLAUDE_CODE_MESSAGING_SOCKET), while the messaging for Codex works through its app-server. For pi, we developed a plugin (how surprising). Short video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=z224uyyxuYQ Website with install instructions: https://teletap.dev We'd love your feedback, especially from teams that run agents in the cloud.

projects.summary: Hi HN, k8sman is a native lighter-weight Kubernetes IDE. It’s a Flutter GUI on top of a Go backend that works with client-go and your existing kubeconfig. Nothing installed in the cluster and no telemetry whatsoever. Just some of the features I think are unique: - Low footprint (~ 50% RSS compared to Lens on the same cluster) - Inspector panels for 30+ kinds that explain what's wrong (a crash-looping pod shows its exit code, termination message and a link to the previous instance's logs) - Customisable views with a compact query language (status!=Running restarts>3 age<1h), with sortable, resizable and reorderable columns that persist per kind - Streamed logs with searching, pod terminals, alerts, port-forwards that persist across pod restarts, and local shell with kubectl that follows the cluster you look at - Helm history with diffs between revisions, rollbacks and dry-run upgrades - Read-only mode per context (enabled by default for everything that looks like prod) - Integrated with Argo CD, Prometheus, Trivy image scanning (but works just as well without!) Builds for macOS, Windows and Linux. Apache 2.0.

projects.title: Show HN: I paid Claude US$1,070 to read the worst reviews of 30k places to stay
projects.author: orifito
projects.summary: Hi HN, I'm Oriol, a solo developer in Barcelona. Before booking anything, I used to do the same thing every time: find a place with a great rating, open the lowest-rated reviews and read them one by one. Broken AC, thin walls, a bed as hard as a board, a shower that barely works. Very often the deal-breaker was right there, written by guest after guest, under a lovely 8.9 global score. OKstays does that reading for you. It scores 33,000+ places to stay in 95 destinations on how well you'll actually sleep and stay there, and ranks them for how you travel (light sleeper, remote work, family...). This month I re-scored 30,500 places from what guests wrote. For each one, Claude reads its newest and lowest-rated reviews, then a second search collects what about 7 other review and booking sites say. It scores 67 comfort signals from 0 to 10, each with a short reason you can read on the place's page. If a deal-breaker (dirty rooms, an uncomfortable bed, a poor shower, bugs) ends up at 6.0 or below, the place is left out of every ranking. One angry guest can't do that alone: it has to be a pattern. What came out (method and charts: https://okstays.com/stats/deal-breakers ): - 1 in 39 places to stay has a deal-breaker guests keep reporting. - Half of them come down to a poor shower (51%). Bugs are next (35%). - 92% of them still have a guest rating of 8+. Across all places, it's 97%. - Under US$100 a night, deal-breakers are nearly 4.5x as common as at US$400+. - Among hotels: about 1 in 5 in New Delhi, 1 in 19 in Mexico City, and 1 of 698 in Tokyo. The cost, because HN always asks: about US$1,070 in API calls, US$3.7 cents a place, all batched (first search ~US$1.3c, second search ~US$1.2c, scoring ~US$1.2c). Before spending it, I tested methods against places I had researched in depth. My old scores were off by about 1.1 points on average; reading reviews brought that to about 0.5 (on a different, larger reference set, so read it as a direction, not a precise gain). It's free, no sign-up, and it also works inside ChatGPT, Claude and Grok as a connector (okstays.com/mcp). It earns booking commissions, and hotels can't pay to rank or to be removed. Last month it earned its first US$8.81, 18 months after I started. That was also the first money I ever made online. Two things I'd love from you: pick a city you know well and tell me if the top 5 feels right. Thank you!

projects.title: 做了个 Pi-Work：让 AI 真正操作工具，并把整个工作环境打包带走
projects.author: pphboy
projects.summary: 大家好，我是 pphboy https://github.com/pphboy, 一名独立开发者，之前主要做 NAS 、Linux Infra 相关的开发。 这段时间一直在做一个自己的项目：**Pi-Work**。目前 MVP 已经跑通，也录制了 Demo ，今天第一次在 V2EX 分享，希望能找到第一批愿意尝试的用户。 本人录制的使用 Demo https://www.bilibili.com/video/BV1Uxx16VEYR/?spm_id_from=333.1387.homepage.video_card.click 官网目前的 Demos: https://pphboy.github.io/piwork/demos/ ### 为什么做 Pi-Work ？ 现在 AI 已经能够写代码、执行命令、调用各种工具了。 但我一直在思考一个问题： **如果 AI 不只是一个聊天窗口，而是真正拥有一套可以操作、保存、迁移和分享的工作环境，会怎么样？** 目前很多 AI Agent 依然依赖宿主机的运行环境。换一台电脑，可能又要重新安装依赖、配置工具、处理环境问题。 我希望把这些复杂性尽可能隐藏起来。 ### Pi-Work 是什么？ Pi-Work 是一个基于 MicroVM 的 AI 工作环境。 它不是单纯给大模型套一个聊天界面，而是尝试把 AI 的工具执行能力与独立的工作环境结合起来。 目前主要实现了几个方向： - **独立运行环境**：通过 MicroVM 为 AI 提供可以实际执行命令、操作文件和使用工具的环境。 - **AI 直接操作工具**：用户通过自然语言提出需求，由 AI 在工作环境中执行任务。 - **工作环境打包与迁移**：支持将工作环境导出为 `.work` 文件，在其他机器上导入和继续使用。 - **降低使用门槛**：提供 GUI 和一键安装流程，尽可能减少用户手动配置虚拟机、依赖和开发环境的成本。 我希望未来用户不需要懂 Docker 、Linux 或各种复杂的环境配置，也能直接使用 AI 完成实际工作。 ### 技术实现 底层使用 QEMU MicroVM ，主要围绕 KVM / WHPX 等虚拟化能力构建。 选择 MicroVM ，是希望在环境隔离、运行效率和可迁移性之间取得平衡。 当前主要面向 x86-64 环境，后续也考虑支持 macOS / Apple Silicon 。 ### 当前进度 目前已经完成了核心 MVP ，包括 AI 操作环境、运行环境管理以及跨机器导入导出的基本闭环。 不过产品还处于早期，UI 、兼容性和使用体验都有需要继续完善的地方。 我不打算等所有功能都完美之后再发布，而是希望开始公开构建，让真实用户的反馈推动后续迭代。 ### 项目地址 https://pphboy.github.io/piwork/ ### 最后 Pi-Work 的长期目标，是让 AI 不仅能够回答问题，还能真正使用工具完成工作，并且让这些工作环境可以被重复使用和分享。 我个人非常看好 AI Agent ，但也觉得在 Agent 之外，运行环境、工具管理、环境迁移等基础设施同样值得投入。 这也是我选择做 Pi-Work 的原因。 目前最想听到大家的反馈： 1. 你有没有遇到过 AI Agent 环境配置、迁移、复用方面的问题？ 2. 你认为这种可以打包分享的 AI 工作环境，有哪些实际使用场景？ 3. 如果你愿意尝试 Pi-Work ，目前有哪些问题会阻碍你使用？ 欢迎大家提建议，也欢迎直接指出产品设计和技术方案中的问题。 我会继续独立开发、公开构建这个项目。 **Just for fun.**

projects.title: Show HN: Firenook – Firebase emulators in Rust: 40× faster writes, 10× less RAM
projects.author: sanjevirau
projects.summary: Hi HN. I build with Firebase almost every day and keep the local emulators running all day, and two things wore me down. The suite is really heavy. Java is required, a heap that grew past 22 GiB on our app, out-of-memory crashes, and data gone at every stop unless you export it. It had become almost unusable and was slowing us down. It's also hard to see what your app is doing. The Emulator UI is incomplete, with no page for Functions, Pub/Sub, Cloud Tasks or Eventarc, only a log. Firenook replaces the emulators for Firestore, Auth, Storage, Functions, Extensions, and many other services with native Rust services. It's a drop-in replacement, so simply install one npm package, no Java, change `firebase emulators:start` to `firenook emulators:start`, and your firebase.json, ports, SDKs, rules and Functions code stay as they are. We tested it heavily. On two hours of a real app's traffic, Firenook peaked at 2.11 GiB against 22.57 GiB on official emulator and answered writes in 5.1 ms against 208 ms at the median. On an idle emulator a write is only 1.5× faster and 40× is under load. With --keep-data, millions of documents come back in about 0.5s. Results are here: https://firenook.dev/benchmarks The console sits on the Emulator UI's port. It shows every function call with its logs and stack, and you can run a failed one again. It shows your rules beside each decision, with the line that decided it, and an inbox of the emails and codes Auth would have sent. Screenshots: https://firenook.dev/console . Honestly, I built the console from scratch as the one the emulators should have had from the start. It's fast, clean, full of the detail you need while developing, and still able to browse and edit millions of documents. The terminal shows a start-up card, then one line per function call with its outcome and, when it fails, the stack. And `npx firenook mcp add` gives Claude Code, Cursor or VS Code tools over the running emulators, so an agent can read the logs or ask the rules why a request was denied, without touching production. It's still new and I'm sure it misses things, so if you use the Firebase emulators, I'd love for you to try it on your project. `npx firenook init --adopt --dry-run` checks your project without changing anything. If something behaves differently from the official emulator, please tell me here or open an issue. That's the most useful feedback I can get.

projects.summary: 这是一次自荐。rightcommit 是一个可视化的 AI 智能体工作流编排工具：在画布上设计工作流，或用自然语言描述需求，由 Project Manager 助手自动生成可编辑的工作流草稿。每个步骤可分配给 Claude Code、Codex 或 Pi，并加入测试、智能体审查和人工审批等质量门禁。不仅用于写代码，也适用于研究、文档分析和报告生成。工作流还能发布为兼容 A2A 的智能体。Rust 编写，Apache-2.0，自托管。 亮点 本人为项目作者（Lorenzo Toscano / ltoscano），此次为自荐。 可视化画布 + Project Manager 助手：用自然语言描述要自动化的任务，Project Manager 助手生成可编辑的工作流草稿，在画布上检查、调整后即可运行。也可以从预置工作流开始，例如 Spec Kit 的规范 → 计划 → 任务 → 实现。 多智能体协作：同一工作流中，不同步骤可分别交给 Claude Code、Codex 或 Pi。 质量门禁与人工审批：检查任务是否关闭、运行服务端测试、智能体审查、人工审批通过后才提交；文件在测试后若有变化会重新验证。支持交互、辅助和无人值守模式，可暂停等待人工决策后继续。 连接与集成：GitHub、Azure DevOps、ServiceNow，以及通过 Atlassian CLI 接入的 Jira、Confluence 和 Bitbucket；支持 MCP，工作流可发布为兼容 A2A 的智能体。 FinOps：按智能体、模型和执行查看成本与 Token 用量。 自托管：默认绑定 localhost，使用自己的密钥；可用 Docker Compose 或 macOS 上的 Homebrew 安装。仓库提供简体中文 README（READMEzh-CN.md）。

projects.title: Show HN: Thousand Suns, a nuclear war sandbox
projects.author: gxd
projects.summary: Hi HN, I'm the author of Thousand Suns (1KS). This has been my full-time project for the past six months and is now available as freeware for Windows, Linux and macOS (experimental) on itch.io. It started as a game but slowly turned into a serious simulation as I educated myself on nuclear war. I'm a stay-at-home dad, previously a Big Tech software engineer, and not a nuclear war expert. But I spent an enormous amount of time learning about the subject from original and derived sources, such as the well-known site NUKEMAP. It goes beyond existing free projects by simulating full conflicts on top of single detonations. The conflicts are “all out” and meant to be a demonstration of the power of present-day arsenals rather than a depiction of nuclear war escalation. This was made with Godot/C# and I spent a good amount of time hand-optimizing the code... Not because it was needed, but because it was fun! I'm not using any external libraries with the exception of Godot itself. It was all custom-made and the nuclear calculations were derived from the amazing 1977 book "The Effects of Nuclear Weapons" by Glasstone and Dolan. I decided to make it free because I think it's important to raise visibility on what is, perhaps, the most dangerous threat to our survival. Without minimizing the many other risks we face, it is the one way civilization as we know it could end tonight. Feel free to ask any questions and I hope 1KS is useful for you!

projects.title: 做微信小游戏踩的坑--详细版
projects.author: DearFox
projects.summary: 想起什么说什么,基本是要做微信小游戏就需要了解的. iOS 上微信小游戏能用的内存有上限：整个微信进程内存和显存共用大约 1G 到 1.4G(具体看手机内存)，超过就会被系统杀掉；另外 5 秒内收到两次内存警告，微信也会直接销毁小游戏。 别以为你游戏资源包只有几百 MB 就没事。PNG 、JPG 只是文件小，进显存要解开成原始像素，每个像素 4 字节，小游戏占用只看分辨率：一张 2048×2048 的图不管文件多小，都占 16MB ，开了 mipmap 还要再多约 1/3 。要是你的游戏资源几百 M,基本玩着玩着就必崩溃. 解决办法是用 ASTC 压缩纹理：显卡能直接读压缩后的数据，4×4 块的显存是原来的 1/4 ，6×6 约 1/9 ，代价是画质略有损失(我自己测试看不出分别)；再配合用完及时卸载资源，就能把峰值压下来。拿我游戏来说，战斗峰值从约 1G 降到了 200MB. ASTC 压缩还有个问题,可能会把某个类型的图片变成洋红色,真机才会出现,所以一定要测试好. 用户手机发热可以在小游戏网页后台给你的游戏接入高性能模式,能大幅度降低发热问题,其他也有能优化的,腾讯这点好在每个文档里面都有一键复制,直接给你的 AI 看,完美接入. 网页后台显示 100 用户就可以开启流量主,手机看要 1000,这里以网页后台为主. 任何游戏,一定要弄新手教程,用户进来几秒不知道干啥,绝对就退了,想象你自己玩小游戏,有那么耐心吗? 游戏版本审核的时候,只要你的资源需要额外下载,审核界面一定要选择联网,而不是单机,这里不是看你游戏的类型,只要有云上资源,就要联网,不然审核员用不能联网的环境审核失败,会直接打回. 加载云上资源的时候,游戏一定要显示具体的大小或者文件进度,我买的腾讯 cdn,按理来说网络肯定可以,但是几次遇到下不动的情况,如果你的游戏没有详细说明,用户可能会以为卡死,直接就退了. 第一次版本审核成功,后台会建议你用他们的代码加固插件,用的时候代码混淆选中等就行,高选项会直接让主包大于 4M. 接入好友排行功能,要在后台开启这个功能,不然游戏不保报错,但是也不显示内容,会让用户疑惑. 每个游戏可以开启新游种子,基本会给量让你开启流量主,一定要把版本弄好再开启,不像我,新手引导都没有就开启了,浪费了... 就说这么多吧,哎,不做游戏看别的游戏都是垃圾,一做才发现真的难啊,总是有一些问题出现,更难受的是辛辛苦苦做完,没有流量 现在小游戏不花钱推,基本都没入尘烟了 我的游戏是割草类游戏,就是各种技能搭配,纯爽游,感兴趣的朋友微信搜:站桩修仙

projects.title: Show HN: Pots – Open-source Grok Bot alternative, used by 6 startups for a month
projects.author: Crokily
projects.summary: Hi HN, I'm Crokily. Pots is an AI coworker that lives in the chat your team already uses: Slack, Discord, Telegram, or any channel with a Chat SDK adapter. It is MIT-licensed and runs on a machine you give it, with the model you choose. To be honest, the first time I used Grok Bot, its design really impressed me. Unlike OpenClaw before it, it was not just Claude Code connected to a chat app. It truly cared about how it works with people. It felt like a living AI assistant, and working with it was painless. That is the idea I kept learning from the whole time I built Pots: it is not an agent hooked up to a chat channel. It should be a coworker that feels alive and is comfortable to work with. But Grok Bot is only Grok's bot. Which model you get depends on your X subscription, your data and your machine are all in the cloud, and most of all, it is a standalone app, and most of its features serve that app. Pots is a bit different. In Sydney I have talked with quite a few founders. Grok Bot is good, and it helps them a lot with their personal tasks. But when I asked who had actually put Grok Bot into their company's work to make their startup team faster, nobody had. So I think Pots is in a different place from Grok Bot, and from most open-source Grok Bot alternatives: it grew out of what real startup teams need. Before I open-sourced it, 6 small startups I met at startup events had been using it with me for over a month. Pots is built first for the channels startup teams already work in, not for an app of its own, so most of what it does serves the places where you actually work. The teams use Pots as a middle layer: a CEO talks ideas through with the team in chat, Pots listens, and then it builds a prototype that both sides can check. They use Pots for competitor research: because Pots runs inside their channels, it knows their product well. Not only the GitHub repo, but the team's daily discussions and what the team cares about. Pots has been listening quietly the whole time, so it knows the product with no setup at all. It also works well with each channel: it talks to people with the channel's own controls, like Slack and Discord buttons and cards, and when it hands over something complex, it deploys a page with its built-in server so everyone sees it in a better form. So Pots is different from Grok Bot and from most open-source alternatives. It came out of what real startup teams need. Its channel features start from what each company's work needs, and it can join your real work setup with no setup and still do well, instead of being one more app that nobody uses and that is hard to start with. And it ran in real business for a while before I cleaned it up and open-sourced it. The difference from Grok Bot is also exactly why I made Pots an open-source Grok Bot alternative. I have OpenAI and Claude subscriptions with plenty of quota, and my own servers, so I don't want an X subscription to limit me. I want to use whatever model I want and do whatever I want. I can even switch to an open model, and none of my data goes into anyone's pocket. Try it (Node 24+, macOS, Linux or Windows): the easiest way is to ask your coding agent (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor) to read docs/for-agents.md in the repo and set up Pots for you. 01 谁要买什么，大家自己填 群友自己添加物品、认领份数；发起人可以配置常购清单，群友也可以添加自己的常购物品 大份商品支持拆分后拼单，比如一盒瑞士卷，可以拆成几份，大家选择自己要的份数，页面会实时显示还差多少没拼满 ![拆分商品和认领份数]( https://blog.scond.me/img/article-studio/2026-11-09-%E4%B8%BA%E4%BA%86%E5%92%8C%E9%82%BB%E5%B1%85%E6%8B%BC%E5%B1%B1%E5%A7%86-%E6%88%91%E7%94%A8-AI-%E5%81%9A%E4%BA%86%E4%B8%AA%E5%B0%8F%E7%A8%8B%E5%BA%8F-2-0/02-08baac22b1eb715566c5997ab91a3e066f2e33d0f7d596feb85b4ac44e213a83-e64610dc.png) 拆成几份，大家各自认领｜旧版界面示意 遇到限购商品，发起人可以按实际限制，在首页「常购物品」里设置限购件数 比如给小码鸡蛋、大码鸡蛋各设「限购 2 件」，配置一次，之后自己发起的拼单继续使用 群友仍能自由添加，同款商品在整单里共用限购额度，小码、大码分别计算 ## 02 每个人该付多少，自动算清楚 认领时能看到自己买了什么、商品合计多少；生成账单后，再看包含费用和优惠的最终应付金额 运费和包装费，可以选择怎么分。发起人填好运费、包装费，可以按购买人数均摊，也可以按购买金额比例分 ![个人账单示例]( https://blog.scond.me/img/article-studio/2026-11-09-%E4%B8%BA%E4%BA%86%E5%92%8C%E9%82%BB%E5%B1%85%E6%8B%BC%E5%B1%B1%E5%A7%86-%E6%88%91%E7%94%A8-AI-%E5%81%9A%E4%BA%86%E4%B8%AA%E5%B0%8F%E7%A8%8B%E5%BA%8F-2-0/03-48a8791ffacbe1f0f264b08fa7c336d6aefc5fcab3474f0b5686280284879758-3d0b8fad.png) 个人账单示例｜旧版界面 ## 03 谁的钱到了，一眼看清 谁的钱到了、谁还差着，首页卡片上直接写。待收金额和未付人数一目了然，发起人不用再点两层才看得到 小程序只负责计算和记录，大家自行转账，发起人核实到账后，再在小程序里确认 ![实际收款记录]( https://blog.scond.me/img/article-studio/2026-11-09-%E4%B8%BA%E4%BA%86%E5%92%8C%E9%82%BB%E5%B1%85%E6%8B%BC%E5%B1%B1%E5%A7%86-%E6%88%91%E7%94%A8-AI-%E5%81%9A%E4%BA%86%E4%B8%AA%E5%B0%8F%E7%A8%8B%E5%BA%8F-2-0/04-42015c9d107985d59d2b84fb1b67686f4ef85171bd529adb1dede028621a3a7d-79cad550.png) 收款管理：这单已经收齐 ## 04 货到了，一键喊人 支持群友订阅通知，订阅过提醒的群友会收到微信通知；没订阅的人，详情页上也一直挂着取货时间和地点 ![实际到货提醒]( https://blog.scond.me/img/article-studio/2026-11-09-%E4%B8%BA%E4%BA%86%E5%92%8C%E9%82%BB%E5%B1%85%E6%8B%BC%E5%B1%B1%E5%A7%86-%E6%88%91%E7%94%A8-AI-%E5%81%9A%E4%BA%86%E4%B8%AA%E5%B0%8F%E7%A8%8B%E5%BA%8F-2-0/05-a293df22ecde18260a020da56e905c0dfaeb00af536f65a758fb22279f1b0487-90a6ad16.png) 群友收到的到货提醒 --- 从有这个想法，到学习小程序开发、上架流程，再到测试上线，前后花了大概一个星期，主要时间花在等小程序备案 费用主要是 30 元的小程序认证费，消耗的 token 没有统计 如果你也经常和邻居、朋友拼单，欢迎体验使用～ ![拼拼账单小程序码]( https://blog.scond.me/img/article-studio/2026-11-09-%E4%B8%BA%E4%BA%86%E5%92%8C%E9%82%BB%E5%B1%85%E6%8B%BC%E5%B1%B1%E5%A7%86-%E6%88%91%E7%94%A8-AI-%E5%81%9A%E4%BA%86%E4%B8%AA%E5%B0%8F%E7%A8%8B%E5%BA%8F-2-0/06-64f34a965fac958b2bdaf30900069d836fb5cb0028dab846cf914268bef13b32-bbee2bb0.png) 长按识别，打开拼拼账单 --- **关于我** 旅行、跑步、看书，也喜欢 AI 和数码 🌍 30+ 国家 · 🏅 半马 1h36 ｜ 全马 3h58 [主页 scond.me]( https://scond.me/) 原文： https://mp.weixin.qq.com/s/BI0j5pprqS27tmTkEGmKbA

projects.title: Show HN: DBDelve – Open-Source DB Client Made with Rust and GPUI
projects.author: shayan_abbas
projects.summary: Hi HN, I’m Shayan and a few months ago I started building a DB Client DBDelve with a focus on performance and just making something that feels good to use (in the spirit of Zed, Ghostty, and other tools that just feel pleasant to use). For my workflow I’ve always looked for performance, especially since some time ago I had a really outdated machine and any kind of bloat was really noticeable, I remember using DBeaver and it just crashing on me multiple times, I also had to use postGIS which just made it worse. I migrated all my essential dev tools to use the ones with performance in mind (Zed, Ghostty etc) but the only thing that was missing was DB Client. The main choices everyone has are DBeaver which is a memory hog and an overkill for most of the tasks imo. The other options like Datagrid, Beekeeper, TablePlus are either electron based so bloated and memory hogs or paid and closed-source. DBDelve 0.3.6 against DBeaver 25.3.1 on the same Postgres table, median of 5 runs each (2026-10-11, M1 Pro, 32 GB). Times are from the action to the rows rendered. DBDelve DBeaver Launch 1.1 s 5.2 s Idle memory 133 MB 606 MB 1,000-row query 0.21 s 1.96 s 1M rows, time 56 s 208 s 1M rows, memory [1] 4.9 GB 17 GB [1] The whole 1M-row, 100-column table pulled into memory on purpose, with the row limit off. Not a normal use case; DBeaver's heap limit had to be raised manually for the benchmark. Scrolling perf with 1 million rows loaded with 100 columns each: https://youtu.be/V2MOhJYFqIE It has most of the features most devs would need for 90% of their workflow plus some more I thought would be a nice touch: Readonly, read-write and Full Access modes Glass themes (If you’re into them, I am) Keyboard focused with every keybinding customizable Organization of connections into projects Me and some other folks have been daily driving it for more than a month now and most good feedback comes on it having a really simple UI to navigate, very stable for its age and the performance of course. I’m also sharing here because those people tell me this has potential to grow so I’m trying my hand at distributing it. Just want to give a huge shoutout here to the Zed team for GPUI, it's a breeze to work with if you just get through them not updating the crate officially on crates.io but the community has found the solutions for it, you just have to dig deep for it. It performs extremely well and just the HTML-like structure of it, makes it easy to understand for someone from a web dev background and agents are very good at writing it too. GPUI component also solves a lot of problems with having a good component library we can use. I think for anyone starting a GPUI project now, GPUI-kit makes a lot of sense, it just bundles GPUI, GPUI-component together and has some optimizations adding retained mode which is experimental but could provide a lot of benefit, so think all things considered it should be the default way. The major optimization I did was just lowering the memory overhead by using packed rows which reduced the memory usage by 40% on large datasets (8.1GB to 4.9GB on a 4GB table loaded in app), everything else came bundled in with Rust and GPUI mostly or they just made it very easy. Limitations: It's not signed and notarized, identity verification from apple's side has been a nightmare but it should be signed soon. Don’t expect feature parity with more mature clients for now, the general direction of this right now is the zed way of adding features in but after making sure the core workflows are done with a high quality. Do give it a try, you can import your connections from dbeaver and tableplus. https://github.com/ShayanAbbas1/dbdelve

projects.title: Show HN: Clikr – Virtual laser pointer that follows where you point your phone
projects.author: abelw
projects.summary: After installing the web extension and clicking its icon it shows a QR code that is scanned by a phone which opens the web app in the browser. When the WebRTC connection has been set up between the devices you can steer a dot on the computer web page by holding a button and pointing the phone. The app also has other presentation clicker features like switching slides, drawing, presenter notes, and can also be used for remote controlling some videos (tested on YouTube and Plex). Firefox extension: https://addons.mozilla.org/sv-SE/firefox/addon/clikr/ Chrome extension: https://chromewebstore.google.com/detail/clikr/oalndbmcbpchb... Home page: https://www.clikr.app/ I've always been fascinated in how much the web can do. This project started as a fun small POC many years ago when some of these native app-like functions were less common. I got the idea to see if I could make my phone control a "laser dot" on my computer just by tilting the phone like a real laser pointer. Being a web guy I went with web extension + web app. Surprisingly I think I got the basics working in an afternoon or two, having some experience with web extensions from before. Getting the user experience smooth and stable and adding other presentation features in various online tools took more time... It uses RTCPeerConnection for the communication, Metered for TURN, and a small protocol for the commands (point, switch slides, etc.). The deviceorientation event is used for getting the orientation (which has to be explicitly allowed on some devices). One issue here is that the angle values don't actually mean anything without a reference. Therefore the first pair of angles received in the extension becomes the origin for that "pointing". The origin on the screen is the middle of the viewport and additional received angles move the dot with those origin values as reference. I.e. it will always start in the middle. This is of course not as good as a real laser pointer but I think it works quite well when you've tried it a bit. Distance to the screen and its size will matter for how much to move the dot which is why there is also a calibration tool. I like the other features too but I think the laser pointer is the fun one. There are some paid features (one-time payment, no subscription) but the laser pointer, basic presentation features, and video remote are free and doesn't require an account. It has some users but it's hard to get them to give feedback so honestly I don't yet know much about how it's performing in real situations. If anyone here tries it out please tell me what you think.

projects.title: Show HN: View Markdown like you would on GitHub/Obsidian, right in your terminal
projects.author: qu8n
projects.summary: Hi HN! I (for better or worse) live in the terminal and look at Markdown files a lot for work. To read Markdown, it seems like we have two choices: (1) use a GUI like VS Code and Obsidian to preview them, which takes me away from the terminal, or (2) use a terminal Markdown viewer like glow and leaf, which doesn't render them in their true form. So I made mddog (inspired by mdcat!). It basically works by building out the Markdown into its real format using macOS built-in engines like CoreText and CoreGraphics, then send the outputs to the terminal as images. The result is that we can view real Markdown format right in the terminal. I spent a month learning basic Rust, another two weeks using AI to iterate on the design and test different approaches for the best performance, then another two weeks on the final build. I hired a human designer to create the dog logo. His name is Spike, named after the dog in my favorite cartoon growing up, Tom & Jerry. Give mddog a try and let me know what you think!

projects.title: Show HN: QueenMQ – slow LLM calls blocked our Kafka partitions, so we built it
projects.author: aliceviola
projects.summary: Hi HN, I'm Alice. Over the last year, at Smartness, the company where I work, we built a new message broker, open source under Apache 2.0. During this year it has replaced Kafka almost completely for us. I would like to show it to you and try to explain what is different about it. First, long story short: in 2025 we launched a new product in our suite. Like all the others it used Kafka for messaging, and like many other companies we were using Kafka as a message queue, wrongly and knowingly. In this product head-of-line blocking hurt a lot: an LLM call takes seconds to minutes, and it blocked every other chat in the same partition. We first built a hack: we saved the Kafka messages in Postgres, ordered by the entity we needed (a chat_id, for example), processed them, and sent them back to Kafka. Then we decided to build a real broker on that idea. It took a year, from C++ plus Postgres to, today, a single Rust binary with data replicated on disk by Raft. I designed this system, so I am biased. Still, I believe QueenMQ holds a new paradigm that turns a message broker into something more powerful, while staying simple. What QueenMQ is, compared to what you already know: Like Kafka, it has partitions, but in QueenMQ they are dynamic (not preallocated) and you can use a lot of them (tested up to 10 million). Like Kafka it is a log, but there is one Raft leader per tenant, so all of a tenant's writes go through one node, which allows transactions without 2PC. Head-of-line blocking can only happen inside one partition, which is one business entity, like a customer or a chat. If you need a plain queue, you can use a different partition for every message. Like RabbitMQ, it has ACK, NACK, retries and a DLQ: this makes it a message queue. It has no routing on push and no exchanges, though. Like a database: thanks to its etcd-like design, it runs transactions that include ACKs, pushes to other queues, KV writes and timers, and it has atomic locks. The KV store is replicated by Raft and keeps the application's state. It is linearizable. It also has strong streaming features: the SDKs can receive one single log with all the messages of all the queues, with one clock and one order. On top of it there are the classic streaming features, like windows, and some less common ones. Clients talk to it over HTTP (the clients are thin, the intelligence is in the broker), and it is Kafka-compatible (although that way you cannot use all of its strengths). The idea underneath is the change from seeing a message broker as a pure "handler" of messages to one where you can offload a lot of application logic that you would otherwise write yourself. In our company it let us remove outbox tables, cron jobs and many other things. On three beefy machines (24 vCPU, NVMe, 88 GB of RAM), QueenMQ sustains 3M msg/s of 256-byte messages, up to 10M partitions, with p99 latency around 20 ms and every write fsynced on two nodes. Of course, with a single leader per tenant, it does not scale by adding more machines. We tested it hard: 226 tests of our own, written with the Jepsen library, on up to 5 nodes. It is changing the way we design the systems and products of our company. I believe in this project and I believe in open source, and I am really glad that Smartness thinks the same way. It is hard to find the time and the money to build something like this without a company behind you. I would love to get questions, the harsh ones too (like how many times this thing crashed production), and feedback. docker run -p 6632:6632 ghcr.io/queen-mq/queen:2.8.0

projects.title: Show HN: Negs (Spektrafilm) brings spectral film simulations to the browser
projects.author: haasisnoah
projects.summary: Hi HN, I'm Noah. Negs runs spektrafilm, Andrea Volpato's physically based film simulation, in your browser (it's completely rewritten in Rust and using WebGPU). Drop in a photo (JPEG, PNG, TIFF or a RAW), pick a film and a print paper, and drag the sliders. The picture updates as you drag, and nothing is uploaded: it all runs on your machine. Try it: https://getnegs.com/try/ Code (GPLv3): https://github.com/noahhaasis/negs There are also native apps on the same engine: SwiftUI on macOS, GTK4 on Linux, and Windows. Spektrafilm (it started life as agx-emulsion) isn't a LUT or a preset. It simulates the whole analog chain, negative and then print, using only the manufacturers' published datasheets. Andrea's original write-up on discuss.pixls.us is worth reading in full: https://discuss.pixls.us/t/spectral-film-simulations-from-sc... . Roughly, it goes like this: - Your RGB image is turned back into a light spectrum and exposed onto the film's three dye layers through their published spectral sensitivity curves. - Each layer builds up density along its characteristic curve. Datasheet curves are measured with densitometers that see all three dyes at once, so they're first separated into a curve for each layer. - DIR couplers: where one layer develops a lot of density, it releases inhibitors that hold back development nearby, in the same layer and the ones next to it. This is where film's saturation and its edge sharpness come from. - Grain is simulated per layer, with fast and slow sub-layers, as random silver halide particles that become dye clouds. It depends on the density at each spot instead of being laid over the image. - Halation: light passes through the emulsion, bounces off the film base and exposes the red layer again (it's at the back), which gives the red glow around highlights. - The negative's dye spectra are then projected through a virtual enlarger with Y/M filtration onto print paper, which has its own sensitivities and curves, and the print is scanned back to RGB. Because it's a model, the controls are physical: camera exposure, print exposure, enlarger filters, how much DIR coupling, grain particle size, halation strength. Push them too far and the image breaks the way film does, with colour crossovers when it's badly over- or underexposed. And you can experimentw with each control. There are about 50 stocks: Portra, Ektar, Gold, Pro 400H, Superia, Kodachrome, Velvia and Provia slide film, Aerochrome and some B&W (HP5, FP4...). There are 9 papers and print films too, such as Endura, Crystal Archive and Vision 2383. The paper choice has a huge impact on the final look. Negs implements the entire chain and is orders of magnitudes faster than the original python Spektrafilm implementation, so you can play around with sliders and get live feedback. Feedback is very welcome, especially from people who have actually shot these stocks: tell me which ones look wrong to you.

projects.title: Show HN: A visualization map of the funding of public companies
projects.author: feearent
projects.summary: I made this webapp (vibecoded) with Meta's AI models during the Meta AI hackathon that just ended (Oct 26-Nov 4). So far it contains public 33,000 companies, and 100k+ 'flows'. A company X has a flow to another company Y if X funds Y or owns its shares, or vice versa. It collects business data from SEC's EDGAR (Electronic Data Gathering, Analysis, and Retrieval), Wikidata company lists, and other regional company indices of Europe and Asia to build a database of companies to display on the map. SEC provides financial information liberally, while for the European counterpart I didn't find an equivalent yet. I geocoded the business addresses using OpenStreetMap's Nominatim (hopefully that doesn't break their terms somehow; I love OSM). But it was slow... (1 API call = 1 address translation per second; I did not have the time/space to download the whole Nominatim database.) There's also this amazing database from OpenAlex, where you can see billions of connections between funders and research institutions, authors, and OpenAccess papers. It's a continuation of Microsoft Academic Graph, which was discontinued in 2021. It's a goldmine for studying study financing / grants, and their API allowances are great, and very clear. I made that a part of the app too (just on a small scale). You can increase the sliders on the top right to increase the scope of data shown. It needs to be raised to show the university grant data (will fix it soon, AI kept failing on this). It was pretty fun building it. There are amazing APIs for this type of work online (free), like from the SEC, Wikidata, some European company indices, though seemingly the hardest part was getting AI to read the API terms and rate limit the API calls interestingly. I think the most fun I had was because I used a non-Claude(?) model, I had to continuously reprompt things that it did not get right intuitively on its own, but I had the sense to know what was broken, so it felt like the fun of programming. I'd say this is my first vibecoded project so maybe that fun dies away soon after. I want to incorporate private company information, donations , or big individual share holders' data into the charts too. projects.title: Show HN: You can now train your own LLMs with less memory, on your consumer GPUs
projects.author: gladia-solaria
projects.summary: *TL;DR: You can train your own 27B model on a 3090 with 24GB VRAM, though you would have to go through hundreds of billions of tokens for it to be good. I am working on conversion of existing models. Check repos for code and the paper if you are interested in more. I have a 40.4GB Qwen Flash* N*ext GGUF* Hi, I do AI research. I have been working on an optimizer that doesn't need the \~16 bytes of VRAM per weight to train a model that AdamW does. I focused on training ternary networks bcs BitNet (Ma et al.) shows they match full precision quality in large scales. The problem is BitNet also keeps the full precision weights during training which means you still need to use the same amount of memory. I got this down from 16 bytes to 1 byte or even less per weight. For you, this means, you can train your own 10-20B parameter models on your consumer GPUs. I fitted 27B model training on a single 24GB 3090 and a 23B model on a 16GB GPU. The trained model costs \~1.6 bits per weight (\~6GB at 27B), 10x smaller than 16bit, and 5x smaller than Q8. I have also been working on converting existing models and training them. This is harder and I am still working on it but I have some promising results. I quantized and trained a Qwen3.8 27B though the file I published below has adapters which are about 2GBs, pushing the file size to 8GB. I am also making a no-adapter version right now. It scores GSM8K 0.895, the same as full precision, HumanEval 0.84 vs 0.93 and runs on a 12 GB GPU at \~2*3* tok/s on my crippled 12GB laptop 4080, though this number can heavily be improved with custom kernels, engineering, etc. I will leave it to you guys to help me with that too. I also quantized and trained Qwen Flash Next down to 40.4 GBs including its n-gram table (at 8GB). It largely retains the skills of the network (scores equivalent on GSM8K benchmark, a little behind on HumanEval, I unfortunately don't have compute for the larger benchmarks such as TerminalBench2.1 but perhaps some of you can help me out) but forgets facts. It mostly works fine if you give it web search as far as my experience goes but this is not strictly measured. I am still doing work on this and I will keep working on it, perhaps even for many years. The code is open for non-commercial use. Check out: The core repo for training: https://github.com/oguzeldereli/ttf-ternary The repo for conversion: https://github.com/oguzeldereli/ttf-conversion Repo for running models trained by ttf: https://github.com/oguzeldereli/ttf-home GGUF for a converted Qwen 3.8 27B with adapters (around 8 GB): https://huggingface.co/oguzeldereli/ttf-Qwen3.8-27B-GGUF GGUF for a converted Qwen 3.8 Flash Next (around 40.4GB): https://huggingface.co/oguzeldereli/ttf-Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-G... GGUF for a converted Qwen 3.8 27B without adapters (around 6 GB): Currently in conversion and will drop soon. I will convert a Qwen 4 27B instance when it drops. Full paper: https://github.com/oguzeldereli/ttf-ternary/blob/main/paper/... Also, I would appreciate github stars if you like the project.

projects.author: jscalo
projects.summary: Hey HN, I’m John. I’m excited to share something I’ve been working on for a long time and releasing today: AppTraction, a native Mac app for Apple’s App Store Connect. I spent 10 years as an engineer at Apple working on macOS and iOS, and the last 8 as an indie developer with 20+ apps on the App Store for myself and clients. AppTraction is the tool I wish I’d had when I started building my own apps. Most iOS and Mac devs that I talk to agree that Apple’s App Store Connect website is slow, confusing, and buggy. There’s a lot of useful data there, but the clunky site makes it really hard to make sense of. AppTraction brings your sales, analytics, ratings, and reviews to your Mac, and then tells you what matters. I won’t get into all the app features here, you can find those on the website, but it has some interesting capabilities so please check them out. Some background on the development process: AppTraction started as a straight port of the App Store Connect website to a native Mac app, and for about two months that’s all it was. Having the analytics data cached and instant was fantastic, but it still required a lot of time and expertise to interpret. At that point I tried connecting Claude directly to the structured data via MCP, and the results were pretty astonishing. Right away it caught that Apple had featured my apps in Australia and the UK, which I’d been totally oblivious to. It also explained that my bread baking app’s sales decline (which I knew about) wasn’t a problem with the app at all, but a recurring seasonal slump, which is evidently typical for baking apps in the summer. That’s when the Insights tab, which now looks for things like these automatically, became the main view of the app. The AI runs on your existing Claude Code or Codex subscription (or OpenRouter). AppTraction uses the CLI you already have, so there are no API fees and no API keys to expose. A bundled, read-only MCP server lets the AI query your data with real tools rather than a pasted dump, and you can point your own AI at it. Privacy: AppTraction was designed with privacy in mind from day 0 so there’s no account, no ads, and your App Store data is stored only on your Mac. projects.title: ChatGPT / Codex 防封号指南 2026｜最新封号潮底层逻辑与我亲测的纯净网络破局方案
projects.author: AtomicBeyondChaos28595
projects.summary: 一、我扒到的风控底牌：触发 OpenAI 封杀的 6 大高危红线 要想防封，必须先搞清楚官方在查什么。根据最近这波封号和之前的案例，绝大多数账号阵亡都是踩了这些雷： 底层网络环境污染（最高频死因）：用廉价共享机场、超售节点或机房IP，短时间内频繁切换节点，同一出口IP下请求量异常，直接触发连坐。中转/反代在这轮清洗里被重点盯上。 支付卡与设备硬限额（新增高危）：同一张卡或同一台设备关联太多付费订阅（Go、Plus、Pro 100/200/500都算），会直接弹出“Too many subscriptions associated with this card or device”或“Device limit reached”。低价区订阅、一卡多号、多设备叠号，这波死伤最惨。 API 违规分发与模型蒸馏：把个人订阅转成API共享或二次售卖（比如sub2api那种），或者拿输出来做蒸馏，风险极高。11月20日起，第三方模型路由/AI网关还得提前拿到官方书面审批。 支付链路异常：虚拟卡、一次性卡，或者支付地区和登录IP严重对不上。 非人类的自动化并发：请求间隔太规律、短时间超高并发，把个人订阅当生产后端用，很容易被识别成脚本滥用。 设备指纹与登录异常：同一设备高频切多个账号，或者短时间多地登录，再跟已封账号产生关联，基本就交代了。 二、我目前的破局核心：彻底抛弃廉价节点，上高纯净专线 防封最底层的逻辑其实就一条：让系统觉得你是个网络稳定、行为正常、没有共享订阅的真实个人用户。 网络环境绝对是重中之重。 我之前也用过各种低价机场，结果IP污染严重、出口老跳、并发一高就卡，后来直接被连坐。那种“万人骑”的节点，等于主动往风控枪口上撞。 正确的做法是建立低复用、高稳定性的IEPL专线。 我自己实测下来，目前用得最稳、口碑也最好的是 TAG 机场。它能成为我现在的主力，主要靠这三点： IEPL内网专线防断流：彻底不用公网中转，断流和IP跳变少很多，ChatGPT长对话和Codex长时间写代码都稳。 物理级价格壁垒和低复用：全球90+国家和地区节点，方便我固定常用出口，不乱跳。套餐门槛相对高，设备数限制也严，把大量低端脚本和羊毛党挡在外面，单节点污染概率低很多。 原生多客户端支持：Clash、Shadowrocket都能直接用，分流规则好配，DNS泄露基本能杜绝。 如果你现在还在用容易连坐的廉价共享机场，我强烈建议尽快换。可以直接去 TAG 机场官网 购买尝试，我自己日常主力是Bronze套餐，重度用的话Silver、轻度用的话Special也够。 三、行为伪装：我给自己定的“真人画像”规则 网络干净了还不够，使用习惯也得像正常人： 循序渐进：刚订阅别立刻拉满并发或通宵跑脚本，保持合理间隔，别7×24小时不间断。 固守阵地：我基本就固定1到2个常用出口，坚决不无意义跨国乱跳。 私产私用：个人订阅只自己用，绝对不共享，更不会做成API对外提供。 底子干净：尽量用真实支付方式，避开虚拟卡和一卡多号。不买来路不明的成品号。API Key一旦泄露立刻撤销重生成。 数据自保：重要聊天记录和Codex项目我会定期导出到本地，云端数据被停用后可能一时半会拿不回来。 另外提醒一下，12月开始Plus/Pro/Business的ChatGPT和Codex会共享Token额度，使用节奏要提前规划好。 四、手机验证码接码：我现在用的纯净平台 注册或登录ChatGPT经常要手机验证码，国内号很容易被识别异常，那些乱七八糟的虚拟号平台更是雷区。 我目前用得比较稳的是 DogeSMS。多国真实号段，接码速度和成功率都不错，专门适合ChatGPT这类需要手机验证的场景。比那些容易被风控标记的廉价虚拟号靠谱太多。 需要的话直接去 DogeSMS官网 购买就行。 五、我总结的挽救与避坑FAQ 已经被封了怎么办？ 马上保存邮件、错误提示和订单信息，走官方申诉入口，强调是个人正常使用、没共享、出口相对稳定。千万别立刻用同一污染网络批量开新号，申诉期间也尽量别用高风险方式登录。明显转售或滥用的，申诉基本没戏。 固定美国IP就能绝对防封吗？ 不能。固定干净出口只能降低IP跳变和共享出口的风险，账号共享、自动化滥用、支付异常照样能封你。 提示额度用尽就是被封了吗？ 不一定，很多时候只是触发了5小时或周额度限制。真正封号会有明确的暂停或停用通知。 用sub2api中转会被封吗？ 风险极高。个人订阅转API分享官方明确不支持，11月20日后第三方网关还得审批。用官方客户端或支持Sign in with ChatGPT的工具会安全很多。 老邮箱/苹果内购能提升权重吗？ 目前没看到公开证据，核心还是真实资料和正常使用习惯。 出现Device limit reached / Too many subscriptions怎么办？ 这是卡/设备硬限额，买Credits或重置额度没用。可以试试切到其他已允许的账号，或者取消订阅申请退款。 亮点 总结 2026年想稳着用ChatGPT和Codex，我自己的核心就三点： 1. 网络要干净稳定：远离廉价共享节点，优先上IEPL专线并固定出口。我目前主力就是 TAG 机场。 2. 使用要像真人：控制节奏，绝不共享或转API分发。 3. 资料要真实：支付信息一致，避免批量操作。手机验证码我现在用的是 DogeSMS。 网络环境永远是第一优先级。还在用廉价共享节点的，我建议尽快迁到更干净的专线，不然封号风险会一直挂着。把这三点做好，配合 TAG 机场 这种高纯净专线 + DogeSMS 接码，目前来看已经能避开绝大多数风控。

projects.summary: 配置了 Claude Code hook，却不确定它有没有执行？HookProbe 将配置读取、单个脚本模拟测试和临时真实会话探针分开检查，输出 PASS、FAIL 或 UNKNOWN 及对应证据。它用 Go 编写，构建后的程序无需第三方运行依赖，提供中英文说明、示例配置和离线 Demo，适合排查 command hooks，也适合学习子进程管理与事件协议测试。 亮点 区分“配置能读取”“脚本能执行”和“观察到运行时回调”，避免把一个模拟测试通过误当成原有 hook 已注册。 提供 JSON 报告和明确退出码；证据不足时返回 UNKNOWN。真实探针依赖回调记录与文件副作用，不采信模型回复中的成功描述。 demo 可离线体验，不启动 Claude、不消耗模型额度、不修改现有配置。 MIT 许可；公开 CI 已在 macOS、Ubuntu 运行 race 测试、go vet、构建和离线 适用范围：同步 command hooks 的 SessionStart、PreToolUse、PostToolUse。真实 Claude 会话尚未实测；自动化传输测试使用明确标记的替身。probe 仅验证本次临时注入的 canary，不证明已有 hook 在原配置位置已注册。真实探针需要已有 Claude 登录与额度。

projects.title: 【工具自荐】GIFGenerator.ai：通过文字或图片，使用 AI 生成 GIF 动图
projects.author: gifgenerator
projects.summary: GIFGenerator.ai：让静态图片动起来的 AI GIF 生成工具 大家好，最近开发并上线了一个 AI GIF 动图生成工具 —— GIFGenerator.ai。 项目的想法来源于一个很简单的问题：现在 AI 已经能够生成各种精美的图片，但如果想让这些图片动起来，制作成可以循环播放的 GIF 动图，往往还需要额外的动画工具和编辑流程。 传统制作 GIF 的方式通常需要准备多张图片、制作逐帧动画，或者先生成视频，再通过其他工具转换为 GIF。对于只想快速制作一个表情包、动态插画、网站动画素材的普通用户来说，这个过程有些繁琐。 因此，我做了 AI GIF Generator，希望把 GIF 动画的创作过程简化为：输入描述或上传图片 → AI 生成动画 → 获取 GIF 动图。 不需要学习 Photoshop、After Effects 等专业软件，也不需要手动绘制每一帧，就可以尝试把一个简单的创意转换成动态内容。 ✨ 主要功能 1. Text to GIF：通过文字描述生成 GIF 只需要用自然语言描述自己想要的动画内容，AI 就可以根据描述生成相应的 GIF 动图。 例如： 一只橘猫坐在窗边，慢慢摇晃尾巴。 一个像素风格的小机器人在草地上行走。 一颗卡通爱心有节奏地跳动，形成循环动画。 一只戴着墨镜的柴犬踩着滑板向前滑行。 一个可爱的 3D 卡通角色向镜头挥手。 对于没有动画制作经验的用户来说，只需要描述场景、角色、动作和风格，就能够快速尝试不同的动画创意。 2. Image to GIF：让静态图片变成动态 GIF 除了文字生成，还支持通过上传图片来创建动画。 比如你已经有一张 AI 生成的插画、宠物照片、卡通角色或者 Logo，可以直接上传图片，并通过文字描述希望添加的运动效果。 一些典型的使用方式： 照片动画化：让照片中的猫咪眨眼、转头，或做出简单的动作。 插画动画化：让插画中的人物挥手、微笑，或者让画面中的元素产生动态效果。 Logo 动画：让静态品牌 Logo 旋转、缩放、移动或产生简单的循环效果。 角色动画：让原创卡通人物跳跃、行走、挥手，制作动态角色素材。 表情包制作：将一张有趣的图片转换成适合聊天分享的动态 GIF。 这种方式比较适合已经有现成图片，希望在保留原始视觉元素的基础上增加动画效果的用户。 3. 支持不同风格的 GIF 动画创作 GIF 不只是传统的聊天表情包，也可以用于 UI 动画、视觉设计、创意展示和网站内容。 GIFGenerator.ai 可以用于尝试不同类型的动画，例如： Pixel Art GIF：复古像素风格动画，适合游戏角色、像素场景和怀旧风格内容。 Cartoon GIF：卡通角色、可爱表情和轻松有趣的动画。 3D Animation GIF：3D 卡通人物、玩具风格角色以及简单的动态展示。 Anime GIF：动漫插画风格的动态创作。 Looping GIF：适合在网页、社交媒体和聊天工具中重复播放的循环动画。 通过描述不同的视觉风格、动作和场景，可以快速探索不同的动画效果。 4. 使用自然语言控制动画效果 除了描述画面内容，还可以在提示词中指定动画的运动方式。 例如： 一只手绘风格的猫头鹰站在树枝上，缓慢眨眼并轻轻歪头。镜头保持固定，背景不变，动作自然，最后回到初始姿势，形成平滑循环。 相比手动制作关键帧，这种方式降低了动画创作的门槛。 对于有明确需求的创作者，还可以在描述中添加运动方向、动作节奏、视觉风格和循环效果等细节。 需要说明的是，AI 生成结果存在一定的随机性，复杂动作和精确的循环衔接可能需要多次调整提示词。 🎯 适合哪些使用场景？ 1. 社交媒体和表情包创作 可以用来制作聊天表情包、社交平台动态图片、趣味角色动画等，让原本静态的内容更加生动。 2. 网站和产品设计 开发者和设计师可以尝试使用 AI GIF 制作网站上的简单动态插画、产品展示素材、加载动画或其他视觉元素。 3. 独立开发者的产品宣传 对于没有专职设计师的独立开发者，可以通过简单的文字描述，为自己的 SaaS 产品、应用介绍或社交媒体宣传制作动态素材。 4. 插画师和内容创作者 已有插画作品的创作者，可以尝试让静态作品增加眨眼、挥手、头发飘动等简单动画效果，探索新的内容展示方式。 5. 宠物和生活照片创作 上传宠物照片或其他有趣的图片，通过 AI 添加动作，制作适合分享给朋友的个性化 GIF。 🚀 如何使用？ 整个使用流程比较简单： 1. 打开 GIFGenerator.ai 网站。 2. 选择文字生成 GIF，或者上传一张想要制作动画的图片。 3. 输入动画描述，说明角色应该如何运动、希望呈现什么风格。 4. 提交生成任务，等待 AI 处理。 5. 预览生成结果，并获取需要的 GIF 动图。 例如，上传一张原创卡通角色图片，输入： 让这个角色开心地跳起来，双手举高，落地后轻轻弹跳，镜头固定，背景保持不变，制作成流畅的循环 GIF。 就可以尝试把静态角色转换成动态形象。 🌐 项目地址 英文首页：GIFGenerator.ai - AI GIF Generator 中文首页：AI GIF 生成器 - 在线制作 GIF 动图 💡 为什么做这个项目？ 现在 AI 图片生成工具已经很多，但是制作 GIF 动画仍然有一些使用门槛。 有些工具偏向专业的视频生成，操作复杂；有些工具只能把已有视频转换成 GIF，并不能直接根据文字或图片生成动画。 我希望 GIFGenerator.ai 能够更专注于 GIF 动图这个使用场景，让用户不必为了制作一个几秒钟的动画，去学习复杂的软件或者经过多个工具的转换流程。 项目目前仍在持续完善中，后续也希望根据实际反馈改善动画生成效果、创作流程以及 GIF 的使用体验。 如果大家平时有制作 GIF 表情包、网站动态素材、角色动画的需求，欢迎体验并提出建议。 也很想了解大家在实际使用 AI 生成 GIF 时遇到的问题，例如角色一致性、动作自然度、循环衔接效果等。 感谢阮老师和《科技爱好者周刊》提供分享项目的平台！

projects.title: Show HN: Open-source customer-facing agents
projects.author: zualas
projects.summary: Hi, Dmitri from Radioso here, an open-source platform to design AI agents for customers and visitors in any channel, in the style of Fin/Ada/Decagon. The repo is https://github.com/radioso-ai/radioso and our website is https://radioso.ai Today, your choices are: 1. Buy a very expensive service for your vertical (usually starting with $$ five figures monthly) 2. Get a cheap off-the-shelf chatbot that mostly answers FAQs 3. Build your own, and then also build the inbox, human handoff, audit trail and integrations around it At Radioso we wanted an open-source option that combines the best of all 3. You can integrate it with your own software via API/SDK or your CRM, or run it standalone, either self-hosted or in our cloud. The engine runs multi-step interactions and takes actions: calling your APIs, updating records, booking things. Maybe you’ve tried Parlant; Radioso is the alternative “with batteries included”: RAG, audit trail, customer service inbox, and integrations like Slack and email. Under the hood it’s plain TypeScript + PostgreSQL, works with OpenAI/Anthropic/other models, and is licensed under Apache 2.0 which includes all features (The only thing we keep under EE license is the multi-tenant layer we use to run our own cloud). We have existing customers running it for technical Q&A, course booking, online product recommendations and goods returns, among others, some reaching 92% of conversations automated. We’re currently working on voice support so we can offer a call center. Our ambition is to be “the WordPress of customer-facing AI” :), where people can contribute their favorite plugins and benefit from the ecosystem. Longer term, we think browsing the web will mostly mean talking to your own agent, and when you need a service or a purchase, your agent will talk to the vendor’s agent to get things done. For this, Radioso already publishes an A2A Agent Card and we’re working on the rest. Your Radioso services are also callable over MCP, for customers who already use it. Thanks for your attention. We’d especially love to hear which integrations you’d want, whether you’d self-host it, and what’s stopped you from deploying a customer-facing AI agent so far. Tell us what you think.

projects.summary: 这是一个运行在 Android 手机上的 AI 智能体，用一句话描述任务（比如“打开设置，告诉我电量”），它就会截图读屏，自己点击、滑动、输入，直到完成。不需要电脑和 adb，只有调用大模型时联网，支持 OpenAI 兼容、Anthropic 和本地 Ollama 模型。适合用来学习手机 GUI 智能体的原理和 Android 无障碍服务开发。 亮点 完全在手机上运行：通过无障碍服务截图、读取界面元素并执行操作，不依赖电脑或 adb 连接。 定位方式稳：优先按界面元素编号点击，找不到时再用 0-1000 归一化坐标，兼容自绘界面。 过程透明：悬浮球实时显示每一步，任务记录保存每一步的截图、动作、推理、耗时和 tokens，还有每步耗时图。 注重隐私：API Key 用 Android Keystore 加密，Base URL 默认隐藏，报错信息里的服务器地址也会脱敏。 中英文界面，可选离线语音唤醒（说“你好阿特”）。 参考 Google 开源的 ARTEMIS 设计，用 Java 移植到手机端，代码适合学习研究。

github.name: ImpossibleComputing/jacq
github.description: Jacq inference compiler and CUDA kernel DSL

projects.summary: I was working (with agents) on testing out various attention algorithm ideas I had, and I found that the existing infrastructure/libraries made it more difficult than it should be. So I created Jacq, a DSL and compiler. A jacq file describes a model’s configuration, weights, layers, and pipeline. Jacq turns it into a standalone CUDA inference runtime and a Python weight exporter. Kernel descriptions can also generate CUDA harnesses. The easiest way to try it is the TinyLlama example in the README. Building, validating, visualizing, and generating CUDA only require Rust. Of course, running inference does require an NVIDIA GPU, CUDA, Python dependencies, and weights. Jacq doesn't support other GPU vendors (AMD, etc) or Metal, yet (PR's welcome!) There's also an experimental vLLM patch to compile and patch your jacq file into a vLLM build, as well. Feedback very welcome!

projects.title: X/twitter 运营必用 Skill, 可以审查发帖, 也可以问问题
projects.author: liyu7352
projects.summary: 前段时间研究了一轮 X / Twitter 的公开推荐代码，整理成了文章。后来发现，这些内容更适合做成一个可以随时提问的工具：碰到具体问题，直接查对应的代码和适用条件。 于是做了 **For You Skills**，给 Claude Code 、Codex 、Cursor 等支持 Skills 的工具使用。 项目：[github.com/alexliyu7352/for-you-skills]( https://github.com/alexliyu7352/for-you-skills) 如果你也在经营 X ，可能纠结过这些问题： - 今天已经发了一篇，另一篇要不要等到明天？ - 一篇长文，应该发普通 Post 、Thread ，还是 Article ？ - 网上说“第二篇曝光打六折”，这个说法到底从哪来的？ - 草稿写好了，开头、长度和配图有什么具体问题？ 这些都可以直接问它。 我比较在意的是**回答的依据能不能查到**。所以除了研究结论，也把对应的原始代码链接、适用条件和未解决的问题整理进了知识库。回答时会查相关条目，再给建议；公开证据不足的地方，也要说明白。 比如“第二篇打六折”这个案例，重点就是查清楚代码里的“第二篇”到底在数什么，以及分数倍率能不能直接理解成曝光比例。演示里保留了这次问答和对应源码，可以自己核对。 有草稿的话，也可以让它审稿。它会检查实际开头、统计长度、考虑首图和后续配图、判断内容更适合哪种发布形式，并给出具体修改。目前一共 8 个技能，通过一个总入口按问题选择工作流。 安装先用这一条： ```bash npx skills add alexliyu7352/for-you-skills --skill x-assistant ``` 装好后，可以在对应工具里试着问： > 使用 x-assistant：我今天上午已经发了一篇 X 帖子，下午还有一篇不同主题的内容。该今天发还是明天发？请给建议，并说明相关源码支持什么、不能证明什么。 也说明一下边界：知识库基于特定版本的公开源码研究，不能据此确认全部线上配置，也不能保证涨粉或曝光。模型、联网和生图等能力由你使用的工具提供。 这里有 [78 秒案例演示及完整记录]( https://github.com/alexliyu7352/for-you-skills/tree/main/docs/demo)，之前的 [中文研究文章]( https://blog.go5.si/posts/zh/x-algorithm-teardown/) 也保留着。 想找一些本身就在用 AI 工具、也有 X 发帖需求的人试试。尤其欢迎拿你真正纠结过的问题，或者一篇准备发布的草稿来测试。 如果试了，最想听到的是：**它有没有帮你做出一个具体决定？哪一段回答仍然空泛，或者证据对不上？**

projects.title: 【资源自荐】从 microGPT 到唐诗 GPT：中文动手课，包含训练、生成和失败实验
projects.author: OakcoderX

github.name: OakcoderX/TangShiGPT-Course
github.description: 从 microGPT 到唐诗 GPT：原始《全唐诗》、可运行代码、HTML 与 PPT 教案，以及真实的李白风格实验。

projects.summary: 自荐一套面向会一点 Python 的初学者的中文动手课：从 microGPT 到唐诗 GPT。 课程受 Karpathy 的 microgpt 启发，采用独立的 PyTorch 教学实现，带学习者把《全唐诗》JSON 整理成字符序列，训练、保存、加载一个小 GPT，再观察它怎样生成五言、七言形式的草稿。 学习路径包括： 先做“下一字频数”基线，再训练模型，比较统计规律与模型输出。 从小规模短跑开始，练习保存权重和继续训练。 用真实的李白风格实验学习设计对照、匿名比较输出和判断失败。当前模型能生成唐诗形式的草稿，但李白风格仍不能稳定复现。 完整学习包提供 HTML 自学教案、可编辑 PPTX、代码、语料、权重和实验记录。下载解压后，用浏览器打开 docs/index.html 阅读教案；运行代码需要 Python 3.10 以上和项目依赖，支持 CPU，亦可尝试 CUDA 或 Apple MPS。 这是公开免费学习项目，不是 Karpathy 的官方课程。自有代码、教案和权重目前没有附开源许可证，上游数据许可已在包内保留。欢迎反馈最难跟上的步骤。

projects.title: Show HN: stardelt.io – a self-hosted lakehouse on k8s (pre-alpha)
projects.author: schwarztrinker
projects.summary: I am pretty honest: there are a ton of vibecoded projects around, and I made another one... great huh? I'm working as a data platform engineer in Germany. My day job is basically spinning up & running lakehouse platforms on US hyperscalers for SMB and some DAX companies. I mean, data engineers like to work on these platforms but since some time I really have ethical concerns about it - like: - vendor lock-in - high costs (because of cloud costs - and in most cases you are not able to connect your own metal if you have one) - non-EU vendors... - other open-source solutions have high license costs for LDAP etc. pp. That's why is started to build my own opinionated data lakehouse platform in my spare time (tbh I also started learning agentic engineering and what harnesses are..), only curated from open source projects already available. The building blocks are pretty straightforward imo: - Iceberg tables on whatever S3 storage you already have - Trino for SQL and Spark Connect for jobs - Airflow for schedules, plus notebooks, Kafka streams and dashboards - One web UI and one API over all of it - stuff around like OIDC, secrets management etc. It's fully pre-alpha. But I want to use it as an internal pitch project at my current employer to push agentic engineering & the idea of creating our own data platform for our non-hyperscaler customers. Site: https://stardelt.io Code: https://github.com/stardelt I'm happy to hear what you think about it :) Cheers, Martin

projects.title: Herdr 的终端界面能把事情做好。Shepi 让你在 Mac 上用得更愉快。
projects.author: wisteen
projects.summary: 同时让几个 AI 编程 agent 做事，难点不只在于怎么给任务。一个在本机改接口，一个在检查测试，服务器上还有一个处理数据。你得不断切回终端，确认谁还在工作，谁正等着你。 我做的 [Shepi]( https://shepi.app/?v=20261107)，是 Herdr 的原生 Mac 客户端，与 Herdr TUI 实时共享同一套工作空间、标签页和 agents ，并支持简体中文、英文和日文。它不是另建一份桌面会话，也不需要你迁移现有工作。Herdr 负责维持 AI 编程 agent 的终端会话，Shepi 提供桌面入口，让任务、进度、产物和需要你参与的时刻，都有清楚的位置。 ## 01 · 现有的终端会话，打开就在那里 Shepi 和 Herdr TUI 连接同一个 Herdr server ，实时共享同一套工作空间、标签页和 agents 。在终端启动的会话，会直接出现在 Shepi ；从 Shepi 启动的，也能在终端里看到。两端可以同时使用，不用迁移，不是复制一份，也不会为桌面界面另开一套独立会话。 Claude Code 、Codex 、OpenCode 、Gemini CLI 、Cursor 、Copilot CLI ，仍然运行在完整的真实终端里。旋转标记表示工作中，空心圆表示空闲，状态也有文字；当前输入的窗格是更浅的卡片。想用桌面窗口就打开，想回 TUI 就回去，接着做的是同一份工作。 ![Shepi 窗口：左侧是工作区和 agent 的边栏，顶部是标签页，中间是三个窗格，底部是状态栏。]( https://shepi.app/guide/img/zh/window.webp) *工作区、agent 状态和真实终端，在同一个窗口里。（指南原图）* ## 02 · 需要你时，不必靠反复巡视发现 当 agent 停下来请求确认，例如准备部署、删除或安装时，侧栏、窗格标题和状态栏会亮起琥珀色； agent 提供操作信息时，也能看见它要执行什么。收起侧栏仍有横幅，切到其他应用会收到 macOS 通知，知道谁停了、工作了多久，点击查看就能回去。声音沿用 Herdr 的提醒时机，远程机器也一样。我希望你能专心做别的事，而不是守着输出等待。 [查看演示视频]( https://shepi.app/guide/img/zh/needs.mp4) ## 03 · 把背景和选项讲清楚，再请你决定 在你要求时，agent 可以发来带背景、选项及各自后果的提问卡。你从任何窗格都能点选，或写自己的回答，答案直接回给对应 agent 。它也能打开网页、在名称下报告进度，或在自身上下左右打开测试和日志窗格，标明归属而不抢键盘焦点；远程 agent 同样可用。这些动作让确认与检查留在工作旁边，不必从长段输出里寻找入口。 ![claude 问 “Deploy to staging?”，卡片位于窗口右上角，写明了情况，有三个回答，每个都说明会做什么，Deploy 标为“建议”，还有一个可以自己写回答的输入框； claude 窗格泛着琥珀色光。]( https://shepi.app/guide/img/zh/ask.webp) *先了解情况，再选择下一步；也可以直接写自己的回答。（指南原图）* ## 04 · 一项工作结束，把下一项交接清楚 有些任务适合分段完成。前一个 agent 做完后，可以留下交接提示，结束当前窗格，再由一个新的 agent 在同一位置接手。也可以安排稍后开始，或等另一个 agent 完成后再执行。安排在机器上运行，关闭 Shepi 也会继续；需要你介入时，仍然停下来等待。我想提供的是清楚的接续位置，而不是假设开发过程不再需要人判断。 ## 05 · 回来时，知道它进行到哪一步 一句“还在工作”，不足以解释任务的进展。Agent 可以把计划放在 Shepi 里，当前步骤显示在名称下面，状态旁有累计工作时长。把指针停在步骤上或点击，就能展开全部步骤、进度条、当前项与每一步的耗时。关掉窗口再打开，这些进度仍然保留。回来时可以先读清位置，再决定是否需要翻完整输出。 ![边栏：带分支和 agent 徽标的工作区，以及显示标志、已工作时长和当前步骤的 agent ；其中一个 agent 的任务卡片在旁边打开，进行到第 3 步（共 4 步）。]( https://shepi.app/guide/img/zh/agents.webp) *当前步骤留在侧栏，完整计划和耗时可以展开查看。（指南原图）* ## 06 · 不只听“完成了”，也看看实际改动 检查结果时，我希望能顺手对照代码，而不只是读 agent 的总结。Shepi 可以查看本机和远程项目自上次提交以来的未提交变更。通过状态栏，或 prefix 后按 d 打开 diff ，按习惯选择并排或单列阅读；看完按 Esc ，就回到原来的窗格。这里做的是查看，不负责暂存或编辑代码，把后续操作留给你自己的工作流程。 ![差异视图：左侧是更改的文件，右侧是更改内容。]( https://shepi.app/guide/img/zh/diff.webp) *把 agent 的说明与实际变更对照着看。（指南原图）* ## 07 · 远程机器，加入同一个工作视野 如果任务跑在服务器上，可以直接在 Shepi 内添加 SSH 机器，使用已有的密钥。输入主机后，由 Herdr 连接；机器会以自己的标题加入侧栏，下面是它的工作区和 agents 。每个工作区都有需介入、工作中、完成和空闲的数量。本机改页面、远程处理数据时，不必把机器边界变成另一套窗口管理负担。 ![窗口上方的“添加机器”表单。]( https://shepi.app/guide/img/zh/machines.webp) *从应用内添加 SSH 机器，和本机任务一起查看。（指南原图）* ## 08 · 在 agent 旁边，留一个能动手的 shell Agent 改完接口，你可能想自己跑一次测试；排查异常时，也可能需要持续看日志。Shepi 可以向旁边或下方拆分真实 shell ，让这些操作紧邻当前任务：跑测试、追踪日志，或用命令打开 PR 。新窗格在原布局中展开，不必另找一个终端窗口，也不用把自己的检查命令塞进 agent 的输入流。协作不只有观看，随时动手也应当方便。 [查看演示视频]( https://shepi.app/guide/img/zh/split.mp4) ## 09 · 输入之前，清楚自己正对着谁 几个 agent 并排时，发错位置比少看一条输出更让人分心。Shepi 用更浅的卡片标出当前输入窗格，只有这里有闪烁光标，标题也写着 agent 的名字。其他窗格保持完整亮度，不会因为失去焦点就暗下去，仍然方便对照输出。可以点击切换，也能用 prefix 加 h 、j 、k 、l 移到相邻窗格，让注意力和键盘去向保持一致。 ## 10 · 布局变零碎，一次把空间分匀 工作过程中不断拆分、拖动，窗格难免变得有大有小。有时你并不需要精确设计比例，只想让每个任务重新获得差不多的阅读空间。prefix 加 = 会让当前标签页里的窗格均分空间，无论此前怎样拆分或调整，都能把布局收拾齐整。我希望整理窗口是一个随手动作，不必在真正的任务之外，再花时间经营一套布局。 ## 11 · 把当前问题看大，也保留原来的位置 读一段长日志，或专心看一个 agent 的结果时，可以用 prefix 加 z 把当前窗格放大到整个窗口，文字保持原位。其他窗格只是留在后面，并没有被关闭；角标、标签页和窗格标题会提醒你正在缩放。再按同一个键，或点击还原，就能回到原布局。临时专注不需要先拆散工作现场，看完也不用重新排列其他任务。 [查看演示视频]( https://shepi.app/guide/img/zh/zoom.mp4) ## 12 · 重复输入，交给知道等待的宏 切换模型、重启开发服务器，或顺序输入几条命令，可以收进一个宏。它不只是连续敲字符，也能等前一步的内容出现在屏幕上再继续：例如等待模型菜单出现，再移动和确认。可以让当前 agent 编写、试运行并告诉你按键，也能让它修改、列出或删除；愿意自己写，就在 Settings 里完成。本机和远程都能用，把明确重复的动作收起来，留出判断的精力。 [查看演示视频]( https://shepi.app/guide/img/zh/macro.mp4) ## 13 · 它做出的页面，就放在旁边检查 让 agent 展示页面，网页就能在旁边打开，本机开发服务和远程服务器提供的页面都可以。你能直接点击交互，也有后退、前进、刷新和在外部浏览器打开的入口。即便光标落在网页输入框里，Shepi 的 prefix 仍然有效，按 Esc 可以把键盘操作交还窗口。检查页面和继续终端工作，不必来回寻找各自藏在哪个应用里。 ![一个 agent 在旁边的窗格中打开了它的开发服务器页面。]( https://shepi.app/guide/img/zh/web.webp) *开发服务器与页面并排，方便检查刚完成的结果。（指南原图）* ## 14 · 相关内容放近，终端继续运行 日志应该靠近正在排查问题的 agent ，测试也可以移到更方便对照的位置。拖住窗格标题，松手前就能预览布局：交换两个窗格，或放到另一个的上、下、左、右。拖到其他标签页可以跨 tab 移动，悬停后还能精确选择落点；放到加号上，就单独建立一个标签页。位置改变时，终端始终继续运行，整理现场不必打断工作。 [查看演示视频]( https://shepi.app/guide/img/zh/move.mp4) ## 15 · 记住一点线索，就能找回任务 不一定每次都记得任务在哪台机器、哪个工作区里。Shepi 的统一搜索覆盖机器、工作区、agents 、窗格和最近输出，本机与 SSH 机器都在同一个入口。输入一两个词，可以组合查询，也不必遵守固定词序，找到结果后按 Return 就能进入。无论记住的是任务名字，还是刚看过的一段输出，都可以从线索回到工作位置。 ![打开的查找，输入了查询，结果按类型分组。]( https://shepi.app/guide/img/zh/find.webp) *同一个搜索入口，同时找任务位置和输出中的线索。（指南原图）* ## 16 · 刚才的位置，不用再找一遍 有时并不需要完整搜索，只是切出去看了一眼，想回到刚才的窗格。Cmd E 会列出跨机器最近使用的位置，按最近顺序排列，并默认选中刚离开的那一个。再按 Return ，就回去了。列表也支持输入文字查找，和搜索一样使用。处理几个交错的任务时，这样的小入口能让临时切换更直接，不必每次都重新辨认侧栏和标签页。 [查看演示视频]( https://shepi.app/guide/img/zh/recent.mp4) ## 17 · 错过的事情，留在收件箱里 Shepi 开着而你离开时，不是每条通知都会当场看到。期间 agent 完成任务、需要介入或发来问题的事件，会留在查找旁边的收件箱里，Dock 也显示数量。点击其中一条，可以直达对应窗格；查看那个窗格之后，提醒才会清掉。我希望回来之后有迹可循，先接住等待处理的事情，而不是重新巡视所有终端，猜测离开时发生了什么。 ![托盘按钮下方的收件箱，列出在你没在看时需要你处理或已完成的 agent 。]( https://shepi.app/guide/img/zh/inbox.webp) *错过的事件留在这里，回来接着处理。（指南原图）* ## 18 · 关掉窗口，工作仍有自己的位置 退出 Shepi 、关掉窗口，或关闭 Herdr TUI ，都不会停止底层 server 中的 agents 。远程服务器上的任务，在这台 Mac 睡眠时也继续运行。重新打开 Shepi ，可以回到原来的工作位置；如果中间断开连接，状态栏还会告诉你有多少窗格发生了变化。窗口是入口，不是任务存在的前提，可以离开，也能在回来时接着做。 Shepi 继承 Herdr 的 prefix 和键位，默认是 Control-B ，也支持鼠标。我希望保留终端的直接，同时把多任务、远程连接与需要人参与的环节讲清楚。如果你经常同时使用几个 AI 编程 agent ，或在 Mac 与服务器之间切换，这就是我想照顾的工作场景。 整个应用支持简体中文、英文和日文，可以跟随 Mac 的语言，也可以在设置里切换，立即生效，不用重启。菜单、设置、提问卡、提示消息和通知等界面内容都有对应翻译；终端里的 agent 、命令和输出则保留原样。网站和用户指南也提供这三种语言，阅读说明与实际操作可以用同一种界面语言。 Shepi 适用于 macOS 15 及以上，支持 Apple silicon 和 Intel Mac ，需要 Herdr 0.9.3 及以上。它是我独立开发的产品，非 Herdr 官方应用。

projects.title: 【资源自荐】三组 AI 结果核对练习：交接、资料来源与代码变更
projects.author: m8500321
projects.summary: 分享三组免费的中文练习，练习给 AI 交任务后怎么核对结果。每组都有完整模拟材料、提示词和参考核对点： 任务交接：分清内部预览和对外发布，保留未确认的负责人、预算。 资料来源：不同样本、平均数与中位数为什么不能直接合并。 代码变更：需求只改按钮文案，提交却顺带改了金额舍入，应该怎样验收。 无需注册，可复制、改写和用于教学；可以人工完成，也可用自己已有的 AI 工具，模型服务费用另计。下面可直接展开一组完整练习。 由 CC-Brichy777 / CCHello 项目方使用 AI 辅助制作，全部是模拟资料，尚无人类讲师审定或课堂实测。外链页面有项目方署名、CCHello 付费第三方桌面服务说明及官网入口；练习不要求使用或推荐产品。 直接试做：把讨论整理成可交接的任务 先读下面六条模拟讨论，分清已经决定的事、暂定安排和仍需追问的问题。 材料 N01：周一讨论，演示页暂定周五发。设计同学小林先出两版首页，周三前给大家看。 N02：周二补充，周五只是内部预览，不是对外发布。公开发布日期需要等隐私说明和测试一起过。 N03：测试负责人阿青说周四可以检查登录流程；支付流程还没有安排测试负责人。 N04：大家提到预算先按2000元准备，小周追问能否提高到3000元。会上没有确认。 N05：小林说首页只保留一个主要按钮，按钮文案还没定。两版稿都不代表最终方案。 N06：会议结束前确认，内部预览前要隐藏演示数据中的邮箱和订单号。没有分配执行人。 给 AI 的任务 请只根据以上模拟材料整理交接清单。每行给出事项、状态（已确认／暂定／待确认）、材料明确写出的负责人、时间和来源编号。没有写出的信息填“未确认”，不要替参与者决定预算、日期或负责人。最后列出最先需要追问的三个问题。 拿到结果后，逐项回看原文 周五是内部预览，没有推断出公开发布日期。回看 N01、N02。 支付测试与脱敏的执行人仍待确认。回看 N03、N06。 没有把3000元写成获批预算，保留2000元准备口径与3000元提问。回看 N04。 周三前提供两版首页；最终方案和按钮文案没有确认。回看 N01、N05。 关键结论有来源编号，没有把追问写成既定事实。 保留第一版结果，再写下“已核实、需修正、待追问”各一项。这些核对点是供人工检查的参考，不是自动评分，也不保证穷尽所有问题。
