projects.title: Show HN: Yogurt – Free, private, open-source alternative to Granola
projects.author: brownrout
projects.summary: Hey HN, I’m Eric and I want to share an OSS project that I’ve been building in my free time. Yogurt is a free, MIT licensed desktop app that uses on-device AI models to transcribe, summarize, and chat with your meetings. Similar to Granola, Yogurt runs in the background and does not join your calls. But unlike Granola, Yogurt is open-source, free to use, and private. Your meeting transcripts, call recordings, and summaries never leave your computer. As small OSS models have gotten faster and more powerful, Yogurt seemed like a pretty obvious win for privacy and cost conscious folks. You do not need a frontier model to summarize meeting notes or answer questions about them. And if you want to make your notes available to a frontier model, you can just share it with Anthropic, OpenAI, etc. directly via Yogurt’s local MCP server. There’s no need to use a paid cloud service as a middleman. I tried some of the most popular OSS note taking tools, and most were missing features like calendar integration, MCP server, etc. or required you to connect or create an account. And more than that, they didn’t feel polished enough for it to be something I actually wanted to use daily, and so I built Yogurt to scratch that itch. I spent a lot of time fine-tuning every UI interaction/animation and optimizing the model calls to get the most out of your hardware + make it snappy. To support Windows/Mac/Linux, I decided to go with Electron. I use whisper.cpp for transcription and Apple’s on-device SpeechAnalyzer if your system supports it. For call summaries and questions, I use a local open weight LLM that automatically gets downloaded and set up based on what your hardware can handle without your cooling fans firing off like crazy (this part uses llama.cpp). I’ve spent a lot of time working on details like echo detection/reduction, global/folder/local level search respectively, and auto-end recordings. Hope this is useful for any of you who have held out on using AI note tools for privacy or cost reasons, or for folks using cloud tools who want to switch to something free and open source that still feels great to use. Would love to hear what you think about the onboarding and note taking experience :)

projects.title: 【开源自荐】DockPilot：让 macOS 程序坞自动跟随当前屏幕
projects.author: LiMingHuaGit

github.name: LiMingHuaGit/DockPilot
github.description: Move the macOS Dock to the display you're actually using — auto-follow the cursor or pin it to one screen. A tiny menu-bar app.

projects.summary: 下载地址： 多显示器使用 Mac 时，Dock 通常停留在主显示器，需要把光标推到另一块屏幕底部才能唤过去。DockPilot 常驻菜单栏，提供两种工作模式： 自动跟随光标：光标在某块屏幕停留一小段时间后，Dock 自动移动过去；切换延迟可调，避免路过屏幕时误触发。 手动固定屏幕：把 Dock 固定到指定显示器，并记住显示器标识，睡眠或重新连接后仍可恢复。 其他特点： 不需要辅助功能等系统权限 菜单栏应用，没有主窗口和 Dock 图标 支持开机启动 Swift 6 开发，MIT 开源 支持 macOS 14+、Apple Silicon macOS 没有公开接口可以只移动 Dock，因此 DockPilot 的实现方式是通过 CoreGraphics 将目标屏幕设为主显示器，Dock 和菜单栏会一起移动。这是当前实现明确保留的取舍。 目前版本为 v1.0.1，提供 DMG 下载。应用已经签名但尚未经过 Apple 公证，首次启动需要右键选择“打开”，开发者也可以直接从源码构建。欢迎试用和反馈，谢谢！

projects.summary: Helmp 是我用 Rust 写的 macOS 启动器，名字读起来像 "help me"。按 ⌥Space 唤起一个面板，可以搜应用、文件和系统设置，也能在里面直接做几件日常小事： 应用搜索支持拼音和首字母（输入 wx 找到微信），名字里有空格、连字符也不影响匹配。 剪贴板历史：单击看详情，双击复制。 截图（⇧⌘1）先冻结屏幕再框选，选区可以调整，右下角可以保存、复制、钉在桌面上。截图识字（⇧⌘2）松开鼠标就出结果，文字自动复制，用的是系统自带的 Vision，离线识别。 翻译：接你自己的模型 API Key，Key 存在系统钥匙串里。 插件：用一个 plugin.json 声明命令（打开链接、调用 HTTP 接口、运行脚本），比如几行配置就能把文字发到 flomo。有插件中心，也可以让 Claude Code 直接帮你写插件。 自带 MCP 服务：Claude Code 等 coding agent 可以调用 Helmp 的功能，有副作用的操作会先在面板里请你确认。 项目以 MIT 协议开源，免费使用。安装包已签名并通过 Apple 公证，支持 macOS 15 及以上。内置自动更新，国内从七牛下载，不需要翻墙。 主页：

projects.title: Show HN: Mimzie, an agent-neutral alternative to the Claude Suite/Claude Cowork
projects.author: kyleandruczk
projects.summary: hi HN! I built Mimzie, an agent neutral AI workspace inspired by the Claude Suite (Docs, Sheets, Slides) and Cowork. It's a free desktop app that runs ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, and Grok in their native CLI harnesses. Think T3 Code or Conductor but for knowledge work. It's basically a GUI for managing knowledge work agents in various form factors. One of those form factors is Bots, akin to Grok Bot or Dots. The original idea for mimzie was simple: I pay for Claude and ChatGPT, and a lot of my day-to-day work lives in .xlsx, .pptx and .docx files. Moreover, I was sick and tired of losing context between AI platforms. I didn't want to bet the house on one AI lab's product, be it the ChatGPT or the Claude Desktop app. So I built an AI desktop app that was agent neutral. The goal of mimzie is to bring the kind of agent workflows that devs have had with codex and claude code into the hands of everyone. And to have a friendly GUI to do it. I've found that the personal agents, hermes and openclaw, are intimidating to set up and confusing to the average non-technical person. some of the core principles of mimzie: - your file stays your file: edits are done locally and .docx, .pptx, .xlsx, and .md and synced to the cloud after - every change is reviewable: edits show up as tracked diffs that you accept or reject, at the smallest unit that makes sense (e.g. a sentence in .docx) - free, and no new subscription needed: bring whichever AI plan or plans you already have. You shouldn't have to pay twice for the same inference, and you SHOULD take advantage of the insane subsidization in the current ChatGPT and Claude plans. - Bots with any AI: I love the concept of grok bot, not so much its limited choice of models. I strongly believe that long-standing "ai teammates" should be agent neutral and in your control Try mimzie out: it's a free beta at mimzie.com it's early, lots of rough edges, but I've had the time of my life developing it. I'd love to answer questions and hear any and all feedback.

projects.title: 【开源自荐】ArcMD：纯 Go 原生打造的 Arc / Zen 风格富文本 Markdown 编辑器
projects.author: Ciao1019

github.name: Ciao1019/ArcMD
github.description: A fresh take on Markdown: a fast, native rich-text editor built in Go with MyGo. Inspired by Arc, with colorful spaces, split views, and local-first notes.

projects.summary: ArcMD 是一款将 Markdown 写作习惯与富文本编辑相结合的新概念文档编辑器。 项目交互与美学灵感源自 Arc / Zen 浏览器：竖向侧边栏、多彩色 Space、全局收藏、资料库视图以及安静克制的呼吸感。整个应用完全使用 Go + MyGo 原生绘制，没有 Electron、没有 WebView、不依赖 cgo。v0.0.2 的 macOS .dmg 安装包约为 7.9 MB（Apple Silicon）/ 8.8 MB（Intel）。在项目公开的百万字符文档基准测试中，CPU 场景构建耗时的 P95 低于 1.2 ms。 起源与初衷 在 The Browser Company 宣布 Arc 步入维护模式后，社区很多喜欢其审美与手感的人都感到十分惋惜。作为一个 Arc 的忠实拥趸，我非常留恋彻底改变了我工作流的竖向侧栏、多色彩 Space 与全局收藏。既然 Arc 停下了脚步，我们便尝试用纯 Go 与原生 UI，在文档编辑的世界里把它延续下去——献给依然相信「软件应该有审美与触感」的创作者。 核心亮点 1. 纯 Go 原生绘制，轻量与性能 基于 MyGo Native UI 纯 Go 绘制，使用原生窗口、GPU 绘制、字形排版与系统输入接口； 自研文档引擎与富文本编辑器，无需捆绑浏览器运行时；v0.0.2 的 macOS 安装包约 7.9–8.8 MB； 在包含 100 万字符、500 张表格的混合文档基准测试中，输入、退格和滚动时的 CPU 场景构建耗时 P95 分别为 1.105 / 1.002 / 1.136 ms。 测试环境为 Apple M5 / 24 GiB、macOS 26.5.1，测量日期为 2026 年 11 月 8 日；数值为三轮独立测试各轮 P95 的中位数。该指标不包含输入事件分发、光栅化、GPU 呈现及显示延迟，不代表端到端输入响应时间。测量方法与原始数据见性能报告。 2. Arc / Zen 式的多空间（Space）工作流 多色彩 Space：每个空间对应一个本地文件夹，可独立定制 1–3 种主题色、渐变、颗粒质感与图标； 空间切换：触控板双指横向轻扫跟手翻页，支持快捷键（⌃1–⌃9）快速切换； 收藏与置顶：全局跨空间共享 Favorites 磁贴，空间内独立 Pinned 置顶； 资料库（Library）与悬浮侧栏：macOS 上用快捷键 ⇧⌘L 一览所有空间卡片；⌘\ 收起侧栏，光标靠近窗口左缘时平滑浮出。 3. 丰富但自然的富文本表达 浮动格式工具栏、/ 斜杠插入、嵌套任务列表、代码高亮、支持合并单元格的表格、TeX 公式与双栏布局； 目录大纲导航、可折叠的标题与列表、自定义文档封面图 / 渐变封面。 4. 知识连接与专注机制 支持 [[双链]] 与 #标签，重命名文档时自动更新指向它的链接； 打字机滚动、专注模式段落淡化、最多 4 分屏独立编辑。 5. 本地优先（Local-First） 采用带版本号的 .arcmd JSON 格式存储完整富文本结构，文档与附件保存在本地文件夹； 支持导入 / 导出 .md 文件；Markdown 无法完整保留文字颜色、部分表格格式及合并单元格结构，.arcmd 文件保留完整内容； 支持版本历史对比、外部修改感知以及保留 30 天的「最近删除」。 项目目前处于早期预览阶段（v0.0.2），欢迎大家体验尝鲜、提 Issue 和参与交流！

projects.title: 【开源自荐】AgentHome：把 Claude Code / Codex / Gemini 的会话收进本机归档，并查看 token 用量、成本与剩余额度
projects.author: PeterChen1997

github.name: longbridge/gpui-kit
github.description: Rust GUI components for building fantastic cross-platform desktop application by using GPUI.

projects.summary: 阮老师好，自荐一个自己写的 macOS 应用，我是作者。 AgentHome：把 Claude Code、Codex、Gemini CLI 的会话收进本机归档，在同一块仪表盘上查看 token 用量、估算成本和剩余订阅额度。 做它有三个原因： 1. Claude Code 默认 30 天后删除会话记录，几个月前解决某个难题的那次对话，到时候就找不回来了。 2. 长会话每一轮都会从缓存重读一遍上下文，token 数字大得吓人，却和实际花费对不上。 3. 各家的 5 小时 / 7 天额度窗口分散在不同地方。 比 agent 清理活得久的归档：每份会话记录入库前先逐字节拷贝（zstd 压缩）到 ~/AgentHome/raw/，agent 删掉自己的文件后，副本还在。只拷贝，不改动 agent 的目录。 成本算得清：直接从会话记录里算 token，按模型、缓存档位分别计价，分项目、分模型统计，有 30 / 90 天趋势。 额度一眼看到：Claude 额度通过官方 claude CLI 的 /usage 读取，Codex 额度读它自己写进会话文件的快照。不读任何凭据，不调私有接口。 全文搜索：⌘K 跨全部消息搜索，支持中文子串，回车直接跳到那条消息。 菜单栏面板：点菜单栏的像素小屋，不用开主窗口就能看到今日成本、各家剩余额度和重置倒计时。 像素栖息地：左栏小屋里住着 Claude（狐狸）、Codex（企鹅）、Gemini（猫），会随真实的活动和额度工作、思考、疲惫或睡觉。 实时同步、中英双语界面，另附命令行工具；没有统计上报，数据不离开本机。 | 归档 | 会话详情 | |---|---| | | | 技术栈：Rust + GPUI Kit（Zed 编辑器的 GPUI 框架），原生 macOS 应用，Apache-2.0 许可证。

projects.title: MuteHint
projects.summary: MuteHint is a desktop app for macOS and Windows that listens to your call and shows a short suggested reply in a floating window on your own screen, for sales calls, meetings and interviews. You use your own Google Gemini API key.

projects.title: GoTerm

projects.title: LLMRouter
projects.summary: LLMRouter gives developers access to 400+ AI models through OpenAI- and Anthropic-compatible APIs, including GPT, Claude, Gemini, DeepSeek and Qwen. Browse model pricing and follow integration guides for desktop clients and developer tools.

projects.title: Shoji
projects.summary: A macOS menu bar app that lays a soft, realistic paper texture over everything on your screen.

projects.title: Levo
projects.summary: Levo lives in your menubar and watches disk, memory, CPU and GPU. When space runs low, your own AI agent (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor or any CLI) checks what's filling your Mac, even System Data. You tick what goes, and Levo cleans it up.

projects.title: Ravkit Desktop
projects.summary: Free desktop app for compressing, converting and merging video, working with PDFs and images, adding subtitles and removing personal details from files.

projects.title: Keyquill
projects.summary: Typethx and get the whole reply in Gmail, help desks, CRMs, chat widgets and any other text box. Unlimited snippets and folders free, a search palette, dates, clipboard and cursor placeholders, daily backups and import/export. Snippets stay in your browser: no account, no AI, no ads, no tracking. Pro adds fill-in forms and nested snippets. Chrome, Edge and Firefox.

projects.title: 【工具自荐】Split：拖一条分隔线，两个 Mac 窗口一起调整大小
projects.author: LukeParker-A
projects.summary: 我想自荐一个自己做的 Mac 菜单栏小工具，叫 Split。 两个窗口并排的时候，中间那条边往往要两边分别去拖。Split 会把两个窗口配成一对，中间给出一条共享分隔线。拖这条线，左右或上下两边会一起变大变小。点一下分隔线，两边对调。 也可以先在菜单里选好比例，再用菜单或快捷键把当前窗口放过去，这个比例下次还在。窗口拖到屏幕边缘或角落，会先预览落点，松手再就位。同一侧还可以叠几个窗口，点旁边的数字就能切换。 它不管 Spaces 或多桌面，摆的是当前这块屏幕上的窗口。支持中文界面。 闭源软件，$4.99 一次性买断，不是订阅。需要 macOS 13 Ventura 或更高版本，Apple 芯片和 Intel 都可以。第一次用要在「系统设置 → 隐私与安全性 → 辅助功能」里给 Split 开权限，不然它动不了窗口。

projects.title: DUPY
projects.summary: DUPY is a desktop app that helps creators turn raw ideas into structured, engaging video scripts. Organize your thoughts, build your narrative step by step, and shape your ideas into content designed to capture attention. With AI assistance and a visual workflow, DUPY helps you go from a rough concept to a ready-to-refine script, without the chaos of a blank page.

projects.title: Junk

projects.title: APX
projects.summary: APX is a free, open-source desktop app that runs your own team of AI agents on your machine. Organize specialists by project, delegate tasks, schedule routines, and connect your models and channels. Connected models and services may have separate costs.

projects.title: Earmix
projects.summary: Turn Spotify down, the Zoom call up and that autoplay tab off. Earmix is a menu bar mixer that gives every Mac app and browser tab its own volume (up to 400%), EQ and output. Plus call ducking, call recording and an iPhone remote. Runs locally.

projects.title: Oxide
projects.summary: Oxide is a lightweight, open-source desktop tool written in Rust for taking notes and screenshots without interrupting your flow. It stays out of the way (invisible when you need it to be), launches fast, and uses minimal memory. - Quick notes, always one shortcut away - Instant screenshots - Invisible mode that stays out of sight - Native Rust performance, small footprint - Open source: contribute on GitHub

projects.title: Reset Rune
projects.summary: Codex banked resets expire, and you can only redeem when remaining usage is under 80%. Reset Rune is an open-source macOS menu bar app that watches expiry and can try to redeem before it disappears. It doesn’t bypass Codex’s rules; auto-use is off by default.

projects.title: ASIS
projects.summary: Take a screenshot, draw directly on it, copy it to your clipboard, or pin it to your screen.

projects.title: Clamshell
projects.summary: Clamshell keeps an Apple Silicon MacBook awake with the lid closed, with no external display, sudo or admin setup. Version 2.0 adds 30+ optional modules: see what Claude Code and Codex are doing from the menu bar, get a notification when an agent needs you, let your agents finish and then let the Mac sleep, or sleep through a usage limit and wake when it resets. 7-day free trial, then $9.99 once.

projects.title: ShotJar
projects.summary: ShotJar keeps recent screenshots on a shelf in your Mac's menu bar. Open it, grab a thumbnail, and drag the file into another app. Keep taking screenshots with macOS, CleanShot X or Shottr. Search by the text inside when you need it. Text recognition runs on your Mac.

projects.title: TypeCrux
projects.summary: Most text expanders sync everything you type to their cloud. TypeCrux does the opposite: your snippet library lives in your browser's storage, on your device. No account, no sign-up, no servers, no tracking — it even works fully offline. Type a shortcut, pick your delimiter, and your full text appears — emails, replies, forms, code, anything you write twice. Folders, data tables, export/import, 16 languages. Free: 25 snippets, 5 tables. Pro: unlimited — $2.99/month, $29/year or $59 lifetime.

projects.title: Dots
projects.summary: Glide into your notch to instantly surface active applications, target windows, web spaces, and custom workflow shortcuts.

projects.title: LabelIt
projects.summary: A small macOS menu bar app that turns Screenshot 2026-11-08 at 10.41.07.png and IMG_4821.HEIC into names you can find later. The AI runs entirely on your Mac.

projects.title: Macbrow
projects.summary: Macbrow turns your Mac's notch into a shelf for files, a heads-up before meetings, a music player with calendar, and your clipboard history. Try everything free for 14 days. Pro is €7.99, one payment.

projects.title: Zonewell
projects.summary: Menu bar window manager for Mac. Draw your own zones, then drag a window or press a shortcut to snap it in. Separate layouts per display. FancyZones for macOS. A$14.99 once, 14-day free trial.

projects.title: Tributary
projects.summary: An open-source workbench for Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode and local models. Keep agent chats, real files, team workflows and Git review together in a desktop app, VS Code companion and CLI.

projects.title: Mostly Daily: Habit Calendar
projects.summary: Mostly Daily is a habit tracker for iPhone that measures consistency, not perfection. Instead of a streak, every habit has a level: Starting, Sometimes, Often, Mostly. One miss never resets anything, and rest days count as rest. Check in with one tap from widgets, the Lock Screen, Siri or Shortcuts; let Apple Health check habits off for you; track what you want less of with Limit habits. No account, no ads: your data stays on your devices and in your private iCloud.

projects.title: DeskPile
projects.summary: Group the windows you use together (VS Code + Chrome + Terminal, Slack + Mail) and press one shortcut: the whole group comes to the front, tiled by layout and framed in its colour. The same window can sit in several groups. Works with Spaces and multiple displays. Native Swift, ~3 MB, no account, no telemetry. Free for 2 groups; $15 one-time unlocks 9 groups, unlimited windows and custom shortcuts.

projects.title: Opaline for Mac
projects.summary: Opaline is a menu bar app for screenshots and screen recording on Mac. Capture an area, a window or a whole scrolling page, mark it up with arrows and blur, record to MP4 or GIF, and copy text from anything on screen. Everything stays on your Mac.

projects.title: MB Viewer
projects.summary: MB Viewer is a free, offline-first desktop application for previewing and editing technical files. Preview TSX/JSX React components without setting up a development environment. Work with Markdown, KaTeX mathematical expressions, Mermaid diagrams, and multiple files in split or quad views. Built for developers, technical writers, researchers, and AI-assisted coding workflows. No account. No cloud dependency. Just open your files and work. Available for Windows, macOS, and Linux.

projects.title: Awake (beta)
projects.summary: Awake is an API client built for seamless team collaboration through Git. No cloud, no subscription, no analytics: your data is yours. Open a workspace, design the contract, commit it, push, all from a fast native desktop client. - Git-native API management: workspaces, versions, history, push/PR workflows. - Local and shared environment and request parameters to avoid conflicts - Claude Code & Open Code integration - Native performance with Go Beta is open. Your API deserves Git superpowers. ⚡️

projects.title: RestocksAIO
projects.summary: RestocksAIO is a desktop app (Windows and macOS) for high-volume sneaker and streetwear resellers. It holds the inventory, lists to 12 authenticated resale marketplaces (StockX, Alias, Sneak.eu and 9 more) plus eBay, Shopify, Vinted and Wallapop, reprices with Bricker Mode, confirms sales and prints invoices and shipping labels. It never buys for you. Built by Reactive Systems SL in Ibiza. From EUR 15/month with a 7-day trial.

projects.title: Show HN: MyBox – Isolate your projects in a Linux box
projects.author: janpmz
projects.summary: Hi HN, I’ve built MyBox to isolate my development projects in Linux containers. Installing npm modules on my machine didn’t feel right anymore. MyBox is built on a fork of apple/container. - Each box has its own Linux kernel. - Project files get copied into the box (no folder mounts). - Packet filtering blocks access to the Mac and local network (internet access from the box is allowed). - Mac apps cannot reach into the box (a dedicated macOS account owns the runtime and virtual disks). - Touch ID or a password is required to access the box (e.g. opening a shell, importing & exporting files). I started with a CLI tool, but for convenience I’ve built a desktop app around it. https://github.com/janpmz/mybox

projects.title: Lumadio
projects.summary: Lumadio puts external monitor controls and per-app audio in your Mac menu bar. Dim each display on its own, change resolution, or boost XDR brightness. Mute or turn down one app, solo another, and duck music in meetings. Save setups as scenes. (Pro 4.99$ forever)

projects.title: SnipText
projects.summary: Turn text in screenshots, PDFs, videos, and webpages into editable text. Open SnipText from your Mac’s menu bar, select an area, and paste wherever you need it. Recognition runs locally. Pro adds optional local MLX recognition and searchable clipboard history.

projects.title: Show HN: emcee – macOS Stage Manager alternative
projects.author: campfireshuffle
projects.summary: I am one of the (dozens!) of users of Stage Manager, but I don't like some of its UX choices. For example, it moves newly opened windows into a new stage, which breaks my focus. I spent some time trying to see if I could modify SkyLight and Window Manager to tweak Stage Manager behaviors, but this required me to turn off SIP and the experience was janky. So I built a full replacement that still feels great to use. You can make as many stages as you want, reorder them, and drag windows and apps between them. IMO all the drag-and-drop behaviors work the way you’d expect. Like several recent window managers, emcee hides windows in an invisible Space (I learned this from yabai), and it works with SIP on. There were lots of little edge cases to get right, e.g: - Keeping the strip’s previews fresh without hammering Screen Recording - Cmd-Tab switching to the right stage and putting focus somewhere sensible. - "Save dialogs", listening for app quit events, etc. Happy to answer any questions!

projects.title: emcee
projects.summary: Make room for what you’re doing on cramped screens with emcee. As intuitive as Apple's own Stage Manager, but with more sensible defaults and new features. Create an unlimited number of stages, one for each activity (e.g. gaming, work or study), and drag-drop windows between stages freely. The interface is fluid, and is more approachable than tiling window managers that require memorization of complicated keyboard shortcuts.

projects.title: Online Counter
projects.summary: Online Counter is a free, no-sign-up counter that runs entirely in your browser. Tally, click, number, digital, button and counting-machine counters for attendance, reps, laps, votes, inventory and events — with keyboard shortcuts, undo, count-by steps and counts that save on your device. Open it and start counting in two seconds. No account, no download, no tracking of your counts.

projects.title: ToDo for Google
projects.summary: Google Tasks has no official desktop app. ToDo for Google brings it to your Mac or Windows computer with a full-screen three-column view, filters for today, tomorrow and overdue tasks, full-text search, and a global shortcut to add a task while you work in another app. Everything syncs with your Google account, and there is a browser version too. Try every feature free for 7 days with no automatic charge, then keep using it with a one-time Full License, not a subscription.

projects.title: [开源分享] MemDock：Claude Code 和 Codex 的双助手工作台，支持会话互转、记忆和 Skills 管理
projects.author: LingyiChen-AI

github.name: LingyiChen-AI/MemDock
github.description: Desktop app to manage Claude Code and Codex memories, skills, sessions and usage

projects.summary: 用 Claude Code 和 Codex 久了，我常遇到两件事。测试命令早就换了，新会话还在按旧规则跑。想更新一个 Skill，又要先翻目录，确认当初装在了哪个工具里。我做了 MemDock，把这些散在不同地方的记忆和 Skill 放到一个桌面工作台里。 规则散在哪，先找得着 在「记忆总览」里，可以按全局或项目搜索 CLAUDE.md、AGENTS.md 和 Claude Code 的自动记忆，也能浏览只读的 Codex 记忆库。规则文件支持分栏编辑和版本回滚。想知道一条规则从哪来，可以在项目记忆图谱中查看关联并跳回来源。 每周翻一遍，有依据再更新 比如项目已经换了测试命令，你在对话里纠正过助手，规则文件却还写着旧命令。可以设成每周提取一次，让 MemDock 从近期对话里找出值得补充的经验和需要修订的规则。也可以每天定时提取，或者手动运行。 提取结果先进入「待审核记忆」。你可以对照旧内容、新建议和原对话，再决定采纳、改完再采纳，或者驳回。采纳后才写回文件。 我到底装了哪些 Skill？ 「Skill 管理」会列出 Claude Code 和 Codex 已装的 Skill，区分全局和项目范围，也能看来源和文件。Superpowers 这类插件会按包展示。可以从 GitHub、本地目录或 ZIP 安装，在两个工具之间复制，也可以检查更新、批量更新或从备份恢复。 换台电脑，规则和清单一起带走 旧电脑可以把记忆和 Skill 安装清单同步到自己的 GitHub 私有仓库。新电脑登录同一个账号，从同一个仓库拉取记忆，再按清单补装缺少的 Skill。有冲突时可以逐块处理，外观和记忆提取等偏好也能单独恢复。 平时写代码，还能用到这些 对话和终端。按项目查看两边的历史会话，支持 Claude Code 与 Codex 双向转换。可以切换图形聊天和原生命令行，也可以开独立的分屏终端。 代码和并行开发。在对话旁搜索、编辑文件和查看 Git 差异。多条任务可以各开一个 Git Worktree，分别开发，做完再合并。 用量和额度。查看两个工具的 Token、估算费用和活跃热力图，支持导出 CSV，也可以选择开启实时额度查询。 飞书连接。用自建机器人在飞书里调用本机助手，按项目和使用者控制访问权限。 桌面设置。检测或安装助手 CLI，设置语言、主题和开机自启，安装版支持自动检查更新。 MemDock 支持 macOS 和 Windows。可以先打开一个常用项目，看看有哪些规则还在用、哪些 Skill 已经装了。

projects.title: Glassline
projects.summary: A menu bar, a dock, Launchpad and Search for Windows 11, with screenshots in one drag. Glassline replaces the taskbar and Start menu, and gives them back whenever you quit.

projects.title: Tarca
projects.summary: Tarca keeps projects, customers, documents, and next steps connected—from the first idea or inquiry through delivery. Plan tasks, manage CRM and sales, create and sign documents, build forms, review designs, publish web pages, and automate workflows. AI Meeting Notes provides transcripts, summaries, and action items you can turn into tasks. Use Tarca in your browser or download the Mac and Windows desktop application. Take a moment to explore the public demo at https://tarca.app/demo

projects.title: 【开源自荐】Mac Selection Clipper：在任意 Mac App 里划词，一键摘录到 Markdown / Obsidian
projects.author: Mylszd

github.name: Mylszd/mac-selection-clipper
github.description: Select text in any Mac app, preview it, and append it to one Markdown file (e.g. an Obsidian inbox). Native Swift/AppKit, no network.

projects.summary: Mac Selection Clipper：一个原生 macOS 划词摘录工具。在任意 App 里用鼠标划选文字，屏幕底部的小横条就显示预览，点「保存」，这段文字连同来源（App、窗口标题、网址）追加到一个 Markdown 文件里，比如 Obsidian 的 Inbox。适合边读边摘，攒够了再统一整理，或者交给 AI 归类。 不用快捷键，也不用先复制，划完就有 能读 ChatGPT 桌面版、微信、Chrome 网页、Terminal 等 App 里的选中文字：优先走系统辅助功能接口，读不到再自动点该 App 的「拷贝」菜单取词，读完恢复原来的剪贴板 所有摘录追加到同一个文件，只追加不改写，整理完删掉已处理的条目即可 不联网，只监听鼠标，不记录键盘、不截图、不 OCR；密码框和安全输入自动跳过 技术栈：Swift + AppKit，无第三方依赖，MIT 许可证。Release 里有编译好的通用版（Apple Silicon + Intel），未经苹果公证，首次打开需要在「隐私与安全性」里点一次「仍要打开」；也可以从源码构建。

projects.title: Cliptrace
projects.summary: Cliptrace is a clipboard history for Windows that finds what you copied when you can only remember what it was about. You copy dozens of things a day and the Windows clipboard keeps almost none of it. Cliptrace saves your copies on your own PC and lets you describe one to get it back.

projects.title: Systematica.app

Mobile App (PWA): Self-hosted CRM into an installable mobile app with custom navigation, shortcuts, and push notifications. projects.title: Tessera
projects.summary: Tessera is a small menu bar app for macOS. Save your layouts, press ⌃⌥1, and your windows tile. Drag one window onto another to swap them, or stack them as tabs.

projects.title: 做了个菜单栏小工具：听写的时候把音乐静音
projects.author: zhigang1992
projects.summary: 用豆包输入法听写的时候，音乐还在响，每次都要自己去按暂停。做了个菜单栏小工具 Autopause：麦克风在用的时候，把正在放的音乐静音或暂停，说完再回来。 两种方式： - 静音：歌继续放，系统音量淡下去，说完再淡回来。 - 暂停：停掉 Music 、Spotify ，以及当前正在播放的内容。只有它自己暂停的才会再播放。中途按了播放，它就不再插手。 默认再等 1.5 秒才恢复，两句话之间音乐不会弹一下。也可以只让指定的 App 触发，开会、打电话就不会把歌停掉。 不录音，不打开麦克风，不申请麦克风权限，没有账号。macOS 14 或更新，Developer ID 签名并公证，不在 App Store 。 https://autopause.reily.app https://github.com/zhigang1992/autopause/releases/download/v1.1.1/Autopause-1.1.1.zip https://github.com/zhigang1992/autopause#这是做什么的

projects.title: Nova
projects.summary: Nova turns your MacBook's notch into a sleek, pure-black Dynamic Island. Hover to expand it, move away and it disappears. 🎵 Music controls, album art & live lyrics 🤖 AI assistant: Apple Intelligence, OpenAI, Gemini, Claude or Groq 📅 Calendar with one-click meeting join 🌤 Weather at a glance ⏱ Pomodoro focus sessions 🗂 File shelf for drag & drop 📋 Clipboard history 🔔 Volume, brightness, AirPods & battery alerts Works on Macs without a notch too. Native Swift, 6 languages.

projects.title: FelixCal
projects.summary: Click the date in your menu bar: month grid, what's up next, reminders. Type "Lunch tomorrow 1pm" to add events, join Zoom/Meet/Teams in one click, edit in place. No account, no analytics, no subscription. $6.99 once, 3 Macs.

projects.title: Cursor Flow
projects.summary: Cursor Flow is for introverts who need to write at work without talking to a laptop. Speak softly into your phone, or type on it silently, and the text appears at the PC cursor. Your phone can also send files and clipboard text, scan a document, press Enter, and use Flow AI. It is built for Windows and Android, for shared offices where free dictation still does not help if you cannot speak out loud.

projects.title: Clipmonger
projects.summary: Clipmonger is a cross-platform clipboard history manager written in Rust. It remembers everything you copy (text, images and file lists), opens a popup on a global hotkey and pastes the clip you pick straight into the window you came from. projects.title: Deskbun

projects.summary: 这是一款用 Rust 开发的 macOS 菜单栏语音输入工具：按住 fn 说话，松开后文字直接出现在任何应用的光标处。可以在线用 Groq 或 OpenAI（自备 API Key），也可以完全离线用 Whisper 或 NVIDIA Parakeet 在本机识别，网络断开时本地模型自动接手。界面有简体和繁体中文，适合想用说话代替打字、又在意隐私的人。需要 macOS 14 及以上。 亮点 中文开箱即用：菜单和对话框有简体和繁体中文，跟随系统语言切换；Whisper 和 GPT Transcribe 都能识别中文，词汇表帮你写对人名和术语 在线还是离线由你决定：在线直连 Groq 或 OpenAI，中间没有服务器；离线时声音不离开你的 Mac 快：开始说话时就预先建立连接，用 Groq 时松开 fn 约 0.4 秒出字 小而原生：Rust 直接调用 AppKit，没有 Electron，应用约 17 MB，在线模式内存约 45 MB 想学用 Rust 写原生 Mac 应用的人，可以参考它通过 objc2 调用 AppKit、CoreML 和 Core Audio 的做法 目前的限制：Parakeet 不支持中文；OpenAI 和 Groq 在部分地区可能无法访问，这时只能用本地模型

projects.title: 【开源自荐】Firefly-Agent：融合 Live2D 桌面伴侣与多智能体工作台的本地 AI 助手
projects.author: Serendipity-wu02

github.name: Firefly-0423/Firefly-Agent
github.description: ✨ Firefly lives on your Windows desktop: chat with her, or let her and 12 partners read files, write code and run commands, with your OK on every step.

projects.summary: 阮老师好，自荐一个我开源的桌面端 AI 项目：Firefly-Agent 为什么做这个项目？ 市面上现有的桌面宠物大多只能简单闲聊，聊几句就容易“失忆”；而真正能读写文件、改代码、跑终端的 Agent 工具，往往又只是一个冷冰冰的命令行或聊天框。 我想尝试打破这层割裂：把「有温度的 Live2D 角色陪伴」和「有严格安全边界的本地多智能体工作台」真正融合进同一个桌面窗口里。 核心工程设计与亮点 1. Chat / Work / Code 三态同窗与克制陪伴 右下角常驻 Live2D 模型，但拒绝做“烦人的弹窗机器”：调用底层工具干活时，她会自动切换成认真的「工作表情」；内置主动关心话题，但如果检测到你在忙未回复，绝不会连续打扰。 切入 Work 与 Code 模式后，可直接接入本地文件系统、Git、LSP 以及 Obsidian 知识库。 2. 主从式多 Agent 并行委派（1+12 ）协同 面对复杂的多步骤任务（如同时统计代码函数、检索多篇本地笔记并交叉比对），主代理（流萤）不再单线程死磕，而是按需从内置的 12 个角色子代理中委派帮手开启子会话并行处理，最后由主代理对照原文做统一核对与汇总。每个子代理均可独立绑定不同的大模型服务。 3. 本地三层加密记忆链与 d3-force 记忆星图 为了解决桌宠“聊完就忘”和“胡乱幻觉”的问题，所有上下文与事实全部加密落盘在本机 SQLite 中，拆分为 S（近期语境）/ M（核心事实）/ H（历史检索） 三层记忆配合 RAG 检索。 在设置页中，系统会将她记住的关于你的事实，实时渲染成一张以“你”为中心的 d3-force 动态记忆关系星图。 4. “动手之前先问你”：自研 Harness 循环与安全沙箱 底层基于 TypeScript 与 Rust 原生辅助模块（app.rs）构建，原生支持 MCP 协议（stdio / SSE / Streamable HTTP）与插件扩展。 所有的文件写入、命令执行、内置浏览器操作均受控于权限拦截器（支持命令审批卡片、目录隔离与 TUN 模式下的 fake-ip 拦截）。执行完毕后，繁琐的调用日志会自动折叠为一行干净的时间线摘要。 5. 零门槛的在线交互预览 为了让不想立刻下载安装包的朋友也能直观感受交互逻辑，我复用同一套前端代码构建了免安装的在线体验网页，点开即玩。 相关

projects.title: 做了一个开源的 YouTube 桌面客户端 Lumtub：原生播放，推荐在本地跑，支持 Windows / Linux / macOS
projects.author: benedict00
projects.summary: # Lumtub：免费开源的 YouTube 桌面客户端 大家好！分享一个我做的开源软件 **Lumtub**。它是一个 YouTube 桌面客户端，支持 Windows、macOS 和 Linux，**免费、没有付费版，基于 GPL-3.0 完全开源**。 ![Lumtub 播放页]( https://raw.githubusercontent.com/0x696c757a696f/lumtub/main/docs/screenshots/watch.png) 🎞️ **一分钟宣传片**： https://github.com/0x696c757a696f/lumtub/raw/main/docs/promo/promo-en.mp4 --- ## 为什么做它 我每天在 YouTube 上看很多视频，但有三件事一直让我不舒服： 1. **浏览器播放 4K 视频时风扇狂转**； 2. **首页推荐越看越窄**，而且不知道为什么会推荐这些； 3. **看外语视频时**，为了双语字幕得装一堆浏览器扩展。 所以我做了 Lumtub：**不用浏览器内核，改用 mpv 原生播放，推荐算法完全在你自己的电脑上运行。** ![Lumtub 功能演示]( https://raw.githubusercontent.com/0x696c757a696f/lumtub/main/docs/screenshots/tour.gif) --- ## 核心特性 ### 播放 * **原生 mpv 播放**：最高 8K，自动选择电脑能硬解的编码（H.264 / VP9 / AV1），画质按钮直接标出 1080P60 这样的帧率。 * **播放控制**：迷你播放器、画中画、关灯模式、A-B 循环、倍速、逐帧和一键截图。 * **高画质直播**：直播支持 1080p 以上画质，直播聊天和聊天回放**可以显示成弹幕**。 * **投屏**：投到电视（Chromecast / DLNA），最高 4K，可选 8K。 * **内置下载**：下载完成后可以直接在应用里播放。 ### 推荐与隐私 * **本地推荐**：首页推荐在本机计算，**每张卡片都写明推荐理由**，可以标记“不感兴趣”。 * **数据只在本机**：观看历史、搜索记录和统计**只存在你的电脑上，不上传**。 * **不登录也能用**：不会擅自读取浏览器的 Cookie 或配置；只有你主动选择“用浏览器登录”时才会用到。 * **频道管理**：可以彻底屏蔽频道，也可以只设为“不再推荐”。 * **屏蔽 AI 视频（可选）**：开启后会隐藏标注为 AI 生成的视频，以及社区整理的 AI 垃圾频道名单里的频道。 * **频道管理**：可以彻底屏蔽频道，也可以只设为“不再推荐”。 * **专注模式**：隐藏首页推荐、评论和相关视频，只看想看的。 ### 字幕与语言 * **双语字幕**：第二字幕翻译第一字幕，**逐句对齐**。 * **沉浸式翻译**：标题、简介和评论都能翻译，可接多家翻译服务。 * **语音转字幕**：没有字幕的视频也能自动生成字幕（需自备 Key）。 * **AI 总结**：根据字幕先总结视频内容，再决定要不要花 40 分钟看完（需自备 Key）。 * **72 种界面语言**。 ### 登录（可选） * **Google 登录**：订阅、播放列表、点赞、评论，还能保存到 YouTube 播放列表。 * **电视码或浏览器登录**：社区动态、投票、给评论点赞，以及你有权限看的**会员专属视频**。 * **直播里发弹幕**：登录后可以在直播聊天里发言。 * **登录信息加密存本机**：浏览器登录会开一个单独的临时窗口，只保留 YouTube 的 Cookie 并加密保存，其他全部删除；观看记录默认不同步到 YouTube。 ### 发现与频道 * **分区探索**：像 B 站一样按分区和子分区浏览，可按为你推荐、热门、最新、冷门宝藏、新人创作者、长视频排序，也能自建分区。 * **按真实语言筛选**：会检查音轨和字幕，选“意大利语”就真的是在讲意大利语的视频。 * **频道页**：视频、Shorts、直播、播放列表、播客和社区动态都有，还能在频道内搜索。 * **订阅分组**：订阅可以分组，正在直播的频道会标出来。 * **按频道记住倍速和音量**：播客 1.5 倍、音乐 1 倍，自动切换。 ### 更多功能 * **内置插件**：SponsorBlock、Return YouTube Dislike、DeArrow（默认关闭，按需开启）。 * **外观**：浅色/深色、10 套配色、护眼暖光，还有紧凑模式和低占用模式。 * **系统集成**：关闭或最小化到托盘，接入系统媒体控制。 * **自动更新**：应用本体、yt-dlp 和 libmpv 都会自动更新，每个更新包都有**签名校验**。 ![搜索]( https://raw.githubusercontent.com/0x696c757a696f/lumtub/main/docs/screenshots/search.png) ![设置]( https://raw.githubusercontent.com/0x696c757a696f/lumtub/main/docs/screenshots/settings.png) --- ## 三个平台 **Windows** ![Windows 版]( https://raw.githubusercontent.com/0x696c757a696f/lumtub/main/docs/screenshots/windows.png) **macOS** ![macOS 版]( https://raw.githubusercontent.com/0x696c757a696f/lumtub/main/docs/screenshots/macos.png) **Linux** ![Linux 版]( https://raw.githubusercontent.com/0x696c757a696f/lumtub/main/docs/screenshots/linux.png) --- ## 技术栈 * **界面**：Flutter * **核心**：Rust * **播放**：libmpv * **解析**：yt-dlp --- ## 下载与安装 项目还在早期阶段，最新版本在 GitHub Releases： 🔗 **[下载 Lumtub]( https://github.com/0x696c757a696f/lumtub/releases/latest)**· **[项目主页]( https://github.com/0x696c757a696f/lumtub)** | 平台 | 说明 | | :--- | :--- | | **Windows** | 安装版或便携版，**不需要管理员权限**。 | | **Linux** | AppImage（x64 / arm64），需要 Debian 12、Ubuntu 24.04、Fedora 37 或更新的系统。 | | **macOS** | Apple 芯片和 Intel 芯片各一个版本。暂未做苹果公证，第一次打开请按 README 的说明解除隔离。 | --- ## 最后 欢迎下载试用、提 Issue。如果觉得有用，**给项目点个 Star 🌟 和捐赠就是对我最大的支持！**

github.description: 离线截图 OCR / Offline screenshot OCR for dark IDEs & dark-mode pages — 自动反色增强，识别结果进本地可搜索历史。按一次热键框选即取字；批量 / PDF / 表格转 Excel / 长截图。识别全程在本机，不上传截图。Windows · MIT。

projects.summary: 按一次热键框选屏幕即完成识别并复制到剪贴板。针对深色 IDE 与暗色网页，识别前自动反色并做 CLAHE 对比度增强，解决低对比度文本整行漏检。结果进入本地可搜索历史，可导出 Excel；内置简体中文模型，默认全程离线、不上传截图。Windows 绿色包解压即用，MIT。 亮点 1. 把「深色截图识别不准」当成首要问题解决。 系统自带 OCR 处理白底黑字没问题，但深色主题截图（代码、报错栈、暗色文档）经常整行漏检。这里先按整体亮度判断是否需要反色，再用 CLAHE 提局部对比度，最后才送进识别模型。 2. 识别结果不是「复制完就没了」。 每次结果自动进本地历史，关键词即时过滤、双击重新复制、可批量导出 txt/docx/pdf/md/xlsx。查一周前识别过的一段报错是秒级的事。 3. 表格转 Excel 不会错列。 不少工具按「行内间隙中点」切列，遇到某行有空单元格就整行少一格、右侧列全部左移。这里改成把单元格的水平区段合并成全局列带，保证每行列数恒定，空格留空。 4. 长截图能扛住动态内容。 页面里有视频、滚动条、时钟时，模板匹配会被这些区域带偏、导致拼接断裂。这里用缩略粗搜 + 全分辨率细化 +「逐列差异中位数」判据 + 动态列自动屏蔽。 5. 完全离线。 内置简体中文 PP-OCR 模型，识别不联网、不上传截图；只有「截屏翻译」会把识别出的文本发给翻译服务，且可在设置里关掉。 6. 工程记录公开。 仓库里有一份 QA 报告，记录了 40 项测试审查修复的根因与实测数据（例如 docx 导出 10 万行从 419 秒降到 3.4 秒），可以当作「一个人怎么系统性自测桌面应用」的参考。 截图或演示视频 深色截图效果对比： 15 秒串联演示： 在线介绍页： 补充说明 这是自荐（本人项目）。MIT 许可，当前版本 v1.0.3；有 README / CHANGELOG / docs/QA-REPORT-2026-11-06.md 三份文档。Windows 10/11 x64 提供 7z / zip 绿色包，Linux / macOS 可从源码运行。

projects.title: Show HN: GitHub-like reply with "R" for Basecamp and Slack
projects.author: nashbridges
projects.summary: Hello HN! I wrote a browser extension (also available as a userscript) that allows to insert quotes into site's reply message box using selected text + hitting 'r' (as it's done on Github). It targets only specific sites (basecamp.com, slack.com), because that's what we use at our company daily. The idea came out of my boss (who's also a good friend of mine) frustration. He always complained that Basecamp's replies are so inconvenient compared to Github's way. You have to select the quote, copy it into clipboard, then scroll to the reply box, paste it, then select the text again, and finally format it as a quote using editor's toolbar. That's 6 steps vs 2 on Github! Last summer Basecamp rolled out a new facelift featuring a heavy usage of keyboard shortcuts. But "reply with r" was still missing, so another rant from my boss followed :) At that time I was toying with an old browser extension written long time ago as a learning project. I was rewriting it against the new extension API to see what changed/improved. Being immersed into the topic, it was obvious that a thought about "fixing" Basecamp with a browser extension came into my head. So I started working on the Dial R for Reply project during my spare time. I had two clear motivations: 1. I knew it would make someone's life better (myself included). 2. I would learn something new along the way. During the process I realised I could also "fix" Slack replies. It was a bit of trial and error (I didn't use any LLMs for reasons stated above). The hardest part was to dig into each editor's public and private APIs (Basecamp uses lexical, Slack uses Quill). I had to resort to using internals, so be warned -- it might break when site owners decided to update those libraries. On the other hand, hacking a site with an extension is a risky operation anyway (anything may be changed at any time). Key takeaways: 1. browser extensions are cool! Compared to native apps and electron wrappers, you as a customer have such a powerful tool to amend a web application as you like. 2. if you are a library writer, if possible, keep your private state and/or functions accessible to the outside world. Yes, you should clearly mark them as a private, so there's a clear boundary drawn between what can be used safely and what's not. But being able to peek into private state was the only option for me to debug and hack into the application.

projects.title: Show HN: Ferry, a highly customizable and feature-rich file manager for macOS
projects.author: jailbirdBD
projects.summary: I am the main developer of Ferry. The team I am part of began on the demoscene in the mid-90s, but for a long while we are mainly just an indie development studio. Ferry started with me being forced to use macOS at my current workplace, which suddenly replaced a working environment I'd been using during professional career as a programmer: Windows for around 10 years, then Debian/KDE for the last 15 years. Over that time, I'd grown very accustomed to Total Commander on Windows, and later Dolphin on Linux as a file manager, plus a collection of small but very useful tools I'd written for myself on Linux. Moving to macOS was quite an adjustment. I really struggled with Finder and the rather fragmented ecosystem of apps, especially when I couldn't find tools that covered the things I was used to having at my fingertips. Having already written a few internal tools in Swift at work, I started to get familiar with the language while trying out several file managers for macOS without finding one that really suited all of my needs... So one thing led to another, and I eventually decided to build my own version of a better Finder (that's probably how most of the macOS file managers started their journey). Obviously, the first versions were essentially a combination of a slightly improved dual-pane Finder spiced up with basic features from TC, but t'was more than good enough for me. Once I started sharing it with coworkers and friends they began suggesting features I hadn't even considered initially, many of which turned out to be genuinely useful. I know there are quite a lot of file managers out there, so a "what makes Ferry different?" is a totally valid question. Well, Ferry first and foremost tries to be as less opinionated and as much customizable as it's possible, so I have included A LOT of options for personalization. Eg. the layout, the UI, the menus, or the shortcuts are adjustable in many ways, you could even put together something which more or less resembles an old-school Norton Commander-style file manager with a modern toolset if that's your thing. The app also includes a rather big collection of handy tools and tidbits which probably don't seem too interesting up until the point you run into a specific trivial task, and then you realize you have to search and install a tool for it. Main features list: https://ferry.indus3.org/#ftrs Another aspect that's important to me is how the app is made. Having been really involved in the demoscene, I wanted to handcraft as much code as possible and keep AI involvement to a minimum, while still using it to improve quality. Most of Ferry is still written manually, AI mainly helps with the boring parts: proofreading and translations, debugging, tests, temporary tools, code reviews and the site. LLMs have become so advanced that I'm honestly not sure whether this is a good or bad thing for software quality. My skills probably aren't quite on par with a modern LLM agent, but hopefully I can still build something useful and pragmatic by doing most of the work myself. Licensing follows TC's approach: there's a reminder, but you can keep using the app for as long as you like (or until the reminder gets too annoying). Hopefully that's reasonable enough. But if I eventually become really happy with the codebase, I'll most likely release the source code too. At this point, since there are plenty of features, I'm becoming much less interested in adding even more of them and rather focused on getting the existing ones as good as possible: size, stability, performance, memory consumption and above all, bugfixes and code quality. Of course I still listen to users, and if someone suggests a feature which is practical and it improves the UX, I try to include it into a future release. Feel free to contact us, as suggestion and criticism is always welcome!

projects.summary: 阮老师好，自荐一个我独立开发的开源自托管工具 Xiaomi Album Syncer（GPL-3.0）。 小米云服务一直没有官方的相册批量导出入口，想把自己云端的相册拿回本地，只能手动在桌面客户端选中下载。这个项目就是解决这件事：登录账号后，它把小米云端的相册（录音）完整拉到本地硬盘或 NAS，之后可以定时跑增量同步，已下载过的文件自动跳过。除小米云服务外也支持 Apple iCloud 照片，多个账号可以放在一个实例里统一管理。 主要功能： 全量 / 增量：用 Cron 表达式设定时，增量只拉新增资产，跑一遍大相册也只要几秒 自动维护凭据：小米支持手机扫码登录，iCloud 走账号密码 + 2FA，凭据过期自动刷新或者通知 照片时间线：下载时回填照片视频的 Exif 拍摄时间和文件系统修改时间，导入 Immich 等本地相册后按拍摄日期归档 按相册归档：每个云端相册存成独立目录，下载路径支持表达式插值自定义（比如按账号/相册/年月） Web UI 与 MCP Server：扫码、建任务、看下载记录都在浏览器里完成（支持 Passkey 和 HTTPS）；也可以把实例挂给 AI 助手，用自然语言查进度、触发任务 部署是典型自托管方案：Docker 一键拉起，或者直接下载单文件可执行程序，Linux / macOS / Windows 全平台含 arm64，面向 NAS 常驻。后端 Kotlin + Solon，前端 Vue 3。 bash docker run -d \ p 8232:8080 \ v ~/xiaomi-album-syncer/download:/app/download \ v ~/xiaomi-album-syncer/db:/app/db \ coolfan1024/xiaomi-album-syncer:latest

projects.summary: 一款像素风的 macOS 菜单栏桌宠，用《列子·汤问》里愚公移山的故事显示 Claude Code 和 Codex 的用量额度：背篓代表 5 小时额度，装满就坐下打盹并倒计时到重置；挖土速度跟着本机 token 流速变化；你用掉的全部 token 会让大山一点点变矮。只读取官方限额，数据只保存在本机，无遥测。 亮点 1. 不是又一个进度条：额度、速度、累计用量都变成了愚公、背篓和大山，瞟一眼就懂。 2. 故事完整：额度用完时智叟来嘲笑，愚公用"子子孙孙无穷匮也"回他；搬完一座山，夸娥氏二子来把山背走；用量越多，解锁的称号和场景道具越多。 3. 只读官方数据：Claude Code 通过 status line 交给本机脚本的 ratelimits，Codex 读本机会话日志；没有数据就说"不知道"，从不估算。 4. 原生 Swift，Apple 芯片和 Intel 通用；支持 Homebrew 安装（brew install --cask s3onghyun/tap/token-yugong）；界面支持简体中文、English、日本語、한국어。 5. 代码 MIT；像素美术以代码逐像素绘制（见 assets/PROVENANCE.md）。本项目在 AI 编程助手协助下完成，我是作者。

projects.title: Show HN: Zeus – Claude Code for AI voice agents
projects.author: kolchinski
projects.summary: Hey, Alex here, I'm one of the founders. We've built phone agents for enterprise customers for two years and kept seeing the same failure: agents that mishear callers and then do something confidently wrong. We're announcing two things in this launch. #1 is the stack: instead of one transcription model → one LLM → one TTS, most conversation turns runs through several transcription models and LLMs (a fast and a slow LLM in the same call, models switched per turn, audio sent straight to an LLM alongside transcripts). That gets us 99.4% on Big Bench Audio. That's the second-highest published score; the only model above us takes almost 9 seconds to start talking as far as we've measured, which doesn't work on a phone call. Eval set and transcripts are on Hugging Face - http://huggingface.co/datasets/kolchinski/bba-storm-eval #2 is Zeus, an agent that configures our voice AI stack per use case and per conversation. We tried doing this with Claude Code and Codex and they were bad at it: they can't run simulated calls out of the box, don't do well with audio input and spotting problems in calls, and tend to blindly believe vendor marketing about which model is best vs actually trying the models. Zeus has evals on real calls, can simulate calls in hard situations, and listens to production calls to find problems, so it can check its own work the way a coding agent runs tests to make sure the code it wrote actually works. Pricing is cost-plus (vendor prices + hosting + a 17–25% margin), no subscription. Zeus is free for now. You can try it with a free $10 credit. Happy to answer questions.

projects.title: Show HN: EarthData – find places to visit or live that match what you care about
projects.author: 11thEarlOfMar
projects.summary: Hi HN, A few years ago, I was trying to find the place on Earth that had the optimal combination of attributes to vacation to or live. I couldn't find anything that wasn't a marketing funnel or was limited in geography. So I built EarthData essentially for myself, but others might find it useful. There are two modes: "visit" for a trip (travel month, length of stay, things to do) and "live" for relocation or retirement (housing, healthcare, day-to-day fit). The way it operates is to allow the user to sculpt the attributes they care about in where they visit on vacation or live. Rate and rank what matters to you. And it will returns 10 initial places, down to specific towns, with a written explanation of why each one fits. From there, the user can expand on places that look interesting, and ultimately pull a TRIP KIT with full itinerary, web links to venues, packing list and other information. A few design choices: - It's anonymous. No account, no email required, and preferences live in your browser's local storage. Nothing is tied to a named profile, your preferences are sent to xAI's API to generate matches, but without any PII. - No ads and no advertising cookies. - I went with a mid-century travel graphic design. To me, it evokes nostalgia and romance for international travel. - It supports 10 different languages. - The initial top 10 Matching is free. The only paid part is an optional $3.75 trip kit for a single place (itinerary, 10 matched activities, checklist, PDF). It covers the Google Places API costs for venues and links, which seem oddly 'expensive'. - Matching uses an LLM (currently xAI's Grok) to generate and reason about candidates, which get shaped into place cards, maps, short videos and activities. One area I struggled with was how to group and refine the attribute selections. Higher slider levels reveal finer-grained choices and give that topic more weight. So if it matters a lot, you can really dial in what you're looking for. If it doesn't matter to you, you can skip entirely. If you see any that seem out of line, please point it out. It was a lot of work to make sense with the slider settings, and I'm not convinced it's dialed in. Finally, if you're looking for something that doesn't have a selection, you can free-form a must-have before submitting. Feedback welcome!

projects.title: Show HN: AppTraction – A Native Mac App for Apple's App Store Connect
projects.author: jscalo
projects.summary: Hey HN, I’m John. I’m excited to share something I’ve been working on for a long time and releasing today: AppTraction, a native Mac app for Apple’s App Store Connect. I spent 10 years as an engineer at Apple working on macOS and iOS, and the last 8 as an indie developer with 20+ apps on the App Store for myself and clients. AppTraction is the tool I wish I’d had when I started building my own apps. Most iOS and Mac devs that I talk to agree that Apple’s App Store Connect website is slow, confusing, and buggy. There’s a lot of useful data there, but the clunky site makes it really hard to make sense of. AppTraction brings your sales, analytics, ratings, and reviews to your Mac, and then tells you what matters. I won’t get into all the app features here, you can find those on the website, but it has some interesting capabilities so please check them out. Some background on the development process: AppTraction started as a straight port of the App Store Connect website to a native Mac app, and for about two months that’s all it was. Having the analytics data cached and instant was fantastic, but it still required a lot of time and expertise to interpret. At that point I tried connecting Claude directly to the structured data via MCP, and the results were pretty astonishing. Right away it caught that Apple had featured my apps in Australia and the UK, which I’d been totally oblivious to. It also explained that my bread baking app’s sales decline (which I knew about) wasn’t a problem with the app at all, but a recurring seasonal slump, which is evidently typical for baking apps in the summer. That’s when the Insights tab, which now looks for things like these automatically, became the main view of the app. The AI runs on your existing Claude Code or Codex subscription (or OpenRouter). AppTraction uses the CLI you already have, so there are no API fees and no API keys to expose. A bundled, read-only MCP server lets the AI query your data with real tools rather than a pasted dump, and you can point your own AI at it. Privacy: AppTraction was designed with privacy in mind from day 0 so there’s no account, no ads, and your App Store data is stored only on your Mac. AI requests go straight from your Mac to your AI provider, under your account, and my servers never see them. Pricing: It’s free for 14 days, then $6.99/month, $39/year, or $99 lifetime. Requires macOS 26 Tahoe or later. (No ASC key handy? There’s a demo app with sample data to play with.) I’d love to hear any feedback, and happy to answer questions of course.

Fuzz instead. appfuzz works with WASM and runs the .wasm thousands of times against a simulated backend and reports problems: crashes, n+1 queries, XSS, SQL injection, leaked secrets, blown IO/CPU/instruction budgets. Try it of your own - you don't need an app for the demo: https://appfuzz.dev Why: agents write code faster than anyone can review it, and in many companies people outside engineering (marketing, sales, support) want to ship apps too - pressure from the CEO is high. But then engineers get the pager alerts. One way to make them safer is to treat them like iPhone/iOS apps: sandbox, permissions, app review (what appfuzz does). projects.author: sluke23

github.name: sluke23/HowToSaveMoney
github.description: 一线城市省钱指南：面向北上广深普通打工人，涵盖租房通勤、吃饭购物、话费宽带、医保社保、个税公积金、公共资源、买房买车与防骗维权。算清金钱与时间成本，整理政策条件和办理入口，让每一块钱花得更值。

projects.summary: 阮老师好，自荐一个中文文档项目：一线城市省钱指南。 写给在北上广深工作、月收入 6000～30000 元的人。这本书不做"节俭说教"，只拆成本结构：房租、吃饭、通勤、话费宽带、医保、购物，以及那些需要自己去申请的政策待遇——公积金、个税专项附加扣除、失业金、技能补贴、保障性租赁住房。哪些能谈、哪些能领、哪些入口值得先查。 目前的形态： 17 章 94 节，另有三份附录：一年省钱日历、链接索引、政策文号核对清单 四个城市各一章，写当地特有的路径，比如北京的公积金直付房租、上海的保租房和"一张床"、深圳的青年驿站 在线检索页：按"我现在遇到的问题"查，也能按城市、章节筛，全文内嵌，离线可用 EPUB / PDF / 离线单文件 HTML 附带一个 Claude Code / Codex 的 skill，装好后可以直接问"住远一点能省多少、多花多少通勤时间"，它按书里的口径算完，并注明出自哪一节 举个例子。第 1.1 节把"住远一点省钱"改写成一道减法： 真实时薪 =（月薪 − 房租 − 通勤成本）÷（174 − 每月多耗的通勤小时） 同样月薪一万，租在公司 3 公里、月租 6000 的人，真实时薪 21.8 元；租在郊区、月租 3200、单程 90 分钟的人，43.8 元。月租贵一倍的人，时薪只有对方的一半。但结论不是"越远越好"——这张表是拿来跟自己的时间价格对照的，单程超过 75 分钟，隐性成本会反噬。 内容基于 2026 年 10 月的政策口径，涉及申领和资格的以主管部门最新公告为准，仓库里单独列了待核实清单。正文由人工智能辅助整理，已在文档中注明。 许可为 CC BY-NC-SA 4.0，其中看房清单、合同条款、维权工具箱和附录 A 为 CC BY 4.0。

projects.title: Show HN: QuanterLab, describe a trading strategy, watch it build in front of you
projects.author: serhatgirgin
projects.summary: Hi HN, I run Quanterlab which is a quantitative research platform (can as well be described as backtesting tool for trading and investing ideas) and it‘s purpose is to provide interpretable results for users' own rule sets, using point-in-time data. I am coming from mechanical engineering domain and I wanted to reflect the concepts of engineering. For example, the “strategies” or more elaborately put “market inefficiency hypothesis” are constructed as block diagrams. And in its own style, QuanterLab is quite a strange thing for a finance software. Instead of looking at candle sticks, this is to construct a logic with these block diagrams. Each one of the boxes have certain contracts with each other’s and it is all about stopping people to make things that does not make sense. Information leakage is something I care a lot and for that purpose everything constructed is placed automatically on a timeline showing you which piece of the block is using which time window which is intended as a visual safety net. And also, the AI is big part of it, which I am personally happy with my decisions on how it is implemented. AI is allowed to use tools in the platform to construct what you describe and deliver the news to you. So, it is definitely NOT something that AI exploiting information uncontrolled (overfit) and adding creativity with what you did not ask for. Similarly, the platform is available as MCP servers and connectors in many AI platforms, and again these AI models only allowed to use the tools that is exposed to them and they are obliged to present the information with certain cards exposing you the blocks to let you inspect or manually change. Lastly, anything constructed can be set as paper trade and you receive a morning brief after every working day. You can try the lab without an account or you can as well connect it to your AI as connector, 10 runs a day for guests and an account gets 30 days of the Practitioner plan, no card needed. Sorry for my awkward mistakes in the text, especially for native English speakers, this text did not pass through AI. Greetings from Germany, Serhat

projects.title: Show HN: EarthData – find places to visit or live that match what you care about
projects.author: 11thEarlOfMar
projects.summary: Hi HN, A few years ago, I was trying to find the place on Earth that had the optimal combination of attributes to vacation to or live. I couldn't find anything that wasn't a marketing funnel or was limited in geography. So I built EarthData essentially for myself, but others might find it useful. There are two modes: "visit" for a trip (travel month, length of stay, things to do) and "live" for relocation or retirement (housing, healthcare, day-to-day fit). The way it operates is to allow the user to sculpt the attributes they care about in where they visit on vacation or live. Rate and rank what matters to you. And it will returns 10 initial places, down to specific towns, with a written explanation of why each one fits. From there, the user can expand on places that look interesting, and ultimately pull a TRIP KIT with full itinerary, web links to venues, packing list and other information. A few design choices: - It's anonymous. No account, no email required, and preferences live in your browser's local storage. Nothing is tied to a named profile, your preferences are sent to xAI's API to generate matches, but without any PII. - No ads and no advertising cookies. - I went with a mid-century travel graphic design. To me, it evokes nostalgia and romance for international travel. - It supports 10 different languages. - The initial top 10 Matching is free. The only paid part is an optional $3.75 trip kit for a single place (itinerary, 10 matched activities, checklist, PDF). It covers the Google Places API costs for venues and links, which seem oddly 'expensive'. - Matching uses an LLM (currently xAI's Grok) to generate and reason about candidates, which get shaped into place cards, maps, short videos and activities. One area I struggled with was how to group and refine the attribute selections. Higher slider levels reveal finer-grained choices and give that topic more weight. So if it matters a lot, you can really dial in what you're looking for. If it doesn't matter to you, you can skip entirely. If you see any that seem out of line, please point it out. It was a lot of work to make sense with the slider settings, and I'm not convinced it's dialed in. Finally, if you're looking for something that doesn't have a selection, you can free-form a must-have before submitting. Feedback welcome!

projects.title: Show HN: Lo-fi layered over air traffic control (recorded myself)
projects.author: kkoppenhaver
projects.summary: Some of you will remember lofiatc.com and I was a huge fan and heavy user until it got shut down. It was streaming LiveATC feeds, and when those got cut off the site went dark and has been ever since. So I decided to bring it back in a way that wouldn't fall to the same fate. I've been an ATC nerd for years (ever since you could still listen to the radio on the arm rest of commercial flights) so this summer I rented a Fiat 500, stuck an airband antenna on the roof, and spent a day driving to three Chicago airports with my laptop in the passenger seat to record the audio I needed in person. This took me to the viewing area at Chicago Executive (KPWK), the cell phone lot at O'Hare (KORD), and the top of a parking garage at Midway (KMDW). The whole chain was a Bingfu mag-mount antenna connected to an airband filter and then to an RTL-SDR, all captured via SDR++. If you're interested, you can read a full post on how the recording day came together here: https://finalapproach.fm/field-notes/chicago-recording-day/ Once I had all the audio, I layered it on top of lo-fi tracks and created one "album" per airport, each with its own vibe. Each track is named after something unique to that airport or something we heard on the radio, and I've had it on as background music for work for about two months now, which is why I built it in the first place! Also important to me was putting this out there in the world with no signup required and no ads. Just like on the original site, finalapproach.fm gives you two sliders that let you push the radio up or the music up depending on which you want to hear more of. And there are pre-built mixes on YouTube and all your favorite music streaming services (search for Final Approach Radio). Happy to answer questions about the radio side, the legal side (as much as I can, obviously), or the editing (largely done with Claude Code).

projects.summary: Hi HN, I've been fascinated by aviation for some time now. Inspired by Fugleramme, I wanted a framed print of a cluster of aircraft over my house or a busy airport. So I built Overhead. (Photos in the README) The hero photo shows planes departing and landing in Changi, Singapore. How it works Flight data for a location is gathered from adsb.lol and adsb.fi as a fallback. (you can also point it to your own ADS-B receiver). projects.title: Show HN: I paid Claude US$1,070 to read the worst reviews of 30k places to stay
projects.author: orifito
projects.summary: Hi HN, I'm Oriol, a solo developer in Barcelona. Before booking anything, I used to do the same thing every time: find a place with a great rating, open the lowest-rated reviews and read them one by one. Broken AC, thin walls, a bed as hard as a board, a shower that barely works. Very often the deal-breaker was right there, written by guest after guest, under a lovely 8.9 global score. OKstays does that reading for you. It scores 33,000+ places to stay in 95 destinations on how well you'll actually sleep and stay there, and ranks them for how you travel (light sleeper, remote work, family...). This month I re-scored 30,500 places from what guests wrote. For each one, Claude reads its newest and lowest-rated reviews, then a second search collects what about 7 other review and booking sites say. It scores 67 comfort signals from 0 to 10, each with a short reason you can read on the place's page. If a deal-breaker (dirty rooms, an uncomfortable bed, a poor shower, bugs) ends up at 6.0 or below, the place is left out of every ranking. One angry guest can't do that alone: it has to be a pattern. What came out (method and charts: https://okstays.com/stats/deal-breakers ): - 1 in 39 places to stay has a deal-breaker guests keep reporting. - Half of them come down to a poor shower (51%). Bugs are next (35%). - 92% of them still have a guest rating of 8+. Across all places, it's 97%. - Under US$100 a night, deal-breakers are nearly 4.5x as common as at US$400+. - Among hotels: about 1 in 5 in New Delhi, 1 in 19 in Mexico City, and 1 of 698 in Tokyo. The cost, because HN always asks: about US$1,070 in API calls, US$3.7 cents a place, all batched (first search ~US$1.3c, second search ~US$1.2c, scoring ~US$1.2c). Before spending it, I tested methods against places I had researched in depth. My old scores were off by about 1.1 points on average; reading reviews brought that to about 0.5 (on a different, larger reference set, so read it as a direction, not a precise gain). It's free, no sign-up, and it also works inside ChatGPT, Claude and Grok as a connector (okstays.com/mcp). It earns booking commissions, and hotels can't pay to rank or to be removed. Last month it earned its first US$8.81, 18 months after I started. That was also the first money I ever made online. Two things I'd love from you: pick a city you know well and tell me if the top 5 feels right. Thank you!

projects.title: 分享一家值得关注的专线机场：节点和家宽 IP 资源挺有特色
projects.author: sonicywalker
projects.summary: 现在选机场，我觉得最重要的已经不是测速能跑多少 Mbps，而是日常使用稳不稳定、AI 工具能不能正常连接、节点 IP 质量怎么样。 尤其是平时经常使用 ChatGPT、Claude Code 这些 AI 工具，网络稳定比单纯的峰值速度重要得多。任务执行到一半突然断连，或者某个节点突然无法访问 AI 服务，都挺影响体验的。 最近比较值得关注的一家是 MESL 机场。 MESL 运行了五年多，采用 BGP 多线入口 + IEPL/IPLC 专线中继，不是单纯追求低价、大流量的路线。 它有几个比较吸引我的地方： ① 节点覆盖比较广： MESL 有 170 多个节点，覆盖 50 多个国家和地区，除了常见的美、日、新、港节点，还能找到不少冷门地区。 ② 家宽 IP 是一大特色： 除普通落地节点外，还有不同国家和地区的家庭宽带、商业宽带 IP。对于经常使用海外 AI 服务、需要特定地区网络环境的用户来说，选择余地比较大。 ③ 适合 AI 和日常办公： ChatGPT、Claude 等主流 AI 服务都有对应的可用节点，配合稳定的线路，也适合需要长时间联网的 AI 编程场景。 ④ 影音娱乐也能兼顾： 除了 AI 工具，部分节点还支持 Netflix、Disney+ 等流媒体解锁，日常刷 YouTube、看海外视频也能用上。 ⑤ 套餐比较灵活： 有不同流量档位，不管是轻度使用还是多设备、大流量需求，都可以根据自己的情况选择。 如果你比较看重专线稳定性、家宽 IP、丰富的全球节点，以及 ChatGPT、Claude Code 等 AI 工具的使用需求，MESL 确实是一家值得尝试的机场。 👉 MESL 机场官网链接 亮点 如果你比较看重专线稳定性、家宽 IP、丰富的全球节点，以及 ChatGPT、Claude Code 等 AI 工具的使用需求，MESL 确实是一家值得尝试的机场。 👉 MESL 机场官网

projects.title: Show HN: Thousand Suns, a nuclear war sandbox
projects.author: gxd
projects.summary: Hi HN, I'm the author of Thousand Suns (1KS). This has been my full-time project for the past six months and is now available as freeware for Windows, Linux and macOS (experimental) on itch.io. It started as a game but slowly turned into a serious simulation as I educated myself on nuclear war. I'm a stay-at-home dad, previously a Big Tech software engineer, and not a nuclear war expert. But I spent an enormous amount of time learning about the subject from original and derived sources, such as the well-known site NUKEMAP. It goes beyond existing free projects by simulating full conflicts on top of single detonations. The conflicts are “all out” and meant to be a demonstration of the power of present-day arsenals rather than a depiction of nuclear war escalation. This was made with Godot/C# and I spent a good amount of time hand-optimizing the code... Not because it was needed, but because it was fun! I'm not using any external libraries with the exception of Godot itself. It was all custom-made and the nuclear calculations were derived from the amazing 1977 book "The Effects of Nuclear Weapons" by Glasstone and Dolan. I decided to make it free because I think it's important to raise visibility on what is, perhaps, the most dangerous threat to our survival. Without minimizing the many other risks we face, it is the one way civilization as we know it could end tonight. Feel free to ask any questions and I hope 1KS is useful for you!

projects.title: 【作品自荐】用 Vibe Coding 做了一个在线游乐场，收录 75 款 AI 小游戏
projects.author: justDemo-hjw
projects.summary: 阮老师好，自荐一下我们在做的 QMuse 游乐场：把通过 Vibe Coding 制作的小作品，整理成一个点开就能玩的游戏合集。 体验地址： 我们通过自然语言描述玩法，让 AI 生成、修改游戏代码，再根据试玩结果不断调整。游戏使用 QMuse 制作，合集页面本身也通过 Vibe Coding 搭建。目前收录 75 款小游戏，涵盖动作、物理解谜、休闲益智、驾驶运动等类型。 可以先试这三款，直接在浏览器里打开，无需下载安装或登录： 苔庭试炼：观察守卫的攻击预警，闪避后抓住收招间隙挥剑。 画线接水：用有限的笔墨画出支撑线，把水引进杯子。 玩具蛋染色：组合遮罩和浸染顺序，还原订单上的目标花纹。 做这个项目，也是想看看 Vibe Coding 能走到哪一步：能生成游戏画面之后，实际给别人玩，还会遇到手机操作、加载、存档等问题，需要继续试玩和修正。我们一直在根据玩家反馈迭代，也给每款游戏加了玩法说明和评论入口。 这里还谈不上每款都打磨成熟，但已经积累了一批可以直接体验的小作品。欢迎试玩，也欢迎指出哪些地方还不好玩、还不顺手。

projects.title: Show HN: Black Ops II statically recompiled to native ARM64 macOS
projects.author: adrbn
projects.summary: I recompiled the three Black Ops II executables (campaign, Zombies, multiplayer) from 32-bit x86 Windows to native ARM64 macOS, ahead of time. Remill lifts each function to LLVM IR, a set of custom passes rewrites it, and the result links against a hand-written Win32 runtime whose Direct3D 11 is drawn by Metal. No Wine, no Rosetta, no JIT, one process. About 150,000 functions are translated; anything the translation misses falls back to a small x86 interpreter, so a gap costs speed instead of crashing. On an M1: campaign 51-60 fps, Zombies 57-60 on six maps, multiplayer against bots 53-60. The repo contains no game files and no translated code. It converts your own Steam copy on your Mac, which takes about 1h45 on an M1. Much of the work was done with AI coding agents, and I spent most of my time on verification: frame pacing against the game's own clock, byte checks on the input files, and run logs for every claim in the README. It's a beta. Split-screen Zombies is the current work in progress. Happy to answer questions about the lifting, the Win32 runtime or the D3D11-to-Metal layer.

projects.title: Show HN: A media server designed to be hosted on a VPS [more in the text]
projects.author: maury91
projects.summary: I've been working on this project for the last 2 years, this is the second iteration and this iteration was designed with the intent of being deployed into a VPS. Let's walk backwards from the worst case to the realistic case. 1a. The absolute worst case, someone takes a memory dump of your VPS, well you are screwed if something fishy is going on they will find about it. 1b. Someone mounts the .qcow2 image and inspects your VPS like if its a docker image without leaving any trace, also in this case, you are screwed. So we can already say, this project is not to defend you once you become a target, that's already too late. Now let's see what can be actually done. Someone takes a file system dump, yes we can work with this. An automated script looks around the file system for something fishy, yes this is literally the use case. But how to achieve this? First we need to decide what an actor wants to detect in our media server: - media files: if you do not have authorization to host them, this is the absolute worst. So how to tackle this? First step: The project encrypts them, each media file is always persisted encrypted, the encryption key is a combination of a general encryption key, and a random value stored in the database. If you have both of them you can decrypt the file, if even only one is missing they cannot be decrypted. At this point it becomes important what level of safety we want... Do you want to stop automated scripts? The database can live in the VPS, unless a script is targeting exactly this project they will not be able to know that file X needs to be decrypted with Y Do you want to be "safe" in case of a file system snapshot? The database then must be external to the VPS Second step: The length of the media file is a giveaway, let's add some random padding to it. - torrent info hashes, names, magnets, blobs, etc... This are in the gray zone, but a script could still treat the presence of a specific torrent infohash in your system as something to flag you for. We store them encrypted in the database, if you separate the database from the VPS then you have the decryption key in the VPS and the encrypted infohash in the database, a snapshot of the DB alone is not enough. Both VPS and DB are needed at the same time. Yes, I'm aware this is not enough to stop a determined sysop, but this is not the purpose of it, the purpose is to never reach the point where they inspect you. If this peculiarity of the project intrigues you, you can find out more about it at: https://github.com/maury91/miauflix I do also have another feature I'm quite proud of, ahead-of-time downloads. I think the process of imdb_id -> torrent hash -> torrent file -> loading seeds -> download initial parts to be too long ( time wise ), so I worked for it to happen before you click "watch": - catalog data ( TMDB/Trakt ) is constantly synched in backgrounds queues - sources are searched by priority in background queues - torrent health ( seeders/leachers ) are kept up-to-date periodically in background queues - torrent metadata is download in background queues and in case of mismatching data the torrent is deleted (a torrent containing movie_name.exe is marked as fake) - the initial sectors needed to stream a file are download when you enter the details page, if you don't click on "watch" like flash but you spend a little bit of time reading the description ( or in future watching the trailer ), everything will be warm and streaming can start immediately I don't know if someone ever used it, but I contributed to webtorrent because when I was reloading a torrent it would make the server hang: https://github.com/webtorrent/webtorrent/pull/2878 [I was a little bit burn out at the time of this PR]

projects.title: Show HN: Totle, daily math puzzle game; Saturday puzzles have the fewest answers
projects.author: zemelett
projects.summary: My oldest two kids are off to college and since leaving we've been playing the Wordle and 'sharing' our solutions with each other. It's been a fun way to stay connected with them, and it's become a bit of a challenge to see if we can beat each other's solutions. This got me thinking about other ways I could connect with them. The thing about the Wordle is that it doesn't take a large commitment of time, you can just pull it out when you've a few spare minutes. So I set out to build a game that would borrow from many of the themes that keep pulling us back to Wordle. What I created is called Tōtle which fits another one of our (okay my) favorite things; Dad jokes and puns (as it’s pronounced total). Here's how it works. You get five different numbers from a number pool 1 to 20, and a target from the remaining pool. Combine two at a time with + − × ÷, using all five numbers, every result a positive whole number, each puzzle always takes 4 moves. You get 3 rounds and 4 undos per round; a medal for fewest moves (perfect 4 = crown). There's a spoiler-free share card, like Wordle’s grid. The combinatorics math works out like this: C(20,5) (that's choose 5 from 20) × 15 possible target numbers = 232,560 possible puzzles. An interesting side quest: exhaustive search discovered that exactly 6 can’t be solved. They all are from the group of 6 numbers: 3, 7, 16, 17, 19, 20. If any one of those is chosen as the target the other 5 cannot make the target. I'm not sure if there are any interesting reasons or patterns. Every puzzle was sorted into 7 difficulty bands, by how many solutions each has, to provide a way to add increasing difficulty along the week. Sunday draws from the easiest 30%, Saturday from the hardest 3%, the game shows “harder than X% of puzzles” on the hardest days; Saturdays so far have been in the 98th–99th percentile of difficulty. 5 Saturdays were discovered to have exactly one answer (answer here means ways that only regroup or reorder the same moves count as one); the first is #68, Saturday, December 19, 2026. A few things I'd love to know from y'all: Difficulty: does the Sunday-to-Saturday curve feel right, and are Saturdays too hard? I've experimented with a mode that offers some help. But it's still under development. First-time play: was anything confusing, like dragging vs. tapping or how rounds work? Phones: How does it play on your phone vs your computer?

projects.title: Show HN: Android and iOS games running offline in the browser
projects.author: phoamapp
projects.summary: Hi everyone. I’m a 19yo solo developer and I’m making a project called Phoam. In middle school, I made a little games website for the people in my school, but it became surprisingly popular. Students would ask me to add mobile apps, and I remember searching how to run APKs online and not finding what I wanted. I’ve always liked the idea that if software ran on one machine at some point, it should also run on another. Apple dropped support for 32-bit apps many years ago, leaving tons of nostalgic games unplayable on modern iPhones. Some newer Android phones also no longer support 32-bit apps, meaning having an APK for an app is not enough to play it again. I knew about projects like Wine and Ruffle that had made software run in a way it was never designed to, and one day I just decided to start my own engine! Phoam runs supported Android APKs and early iOS IPAs in the browser. The apps’ original code runs locally on your device, so it isn’t streaming from another phone or computer. On an iPhone, you can add them to your home screen. It’s still very early, and compatibility varies. The public demos are Replica Island and Explora-Ball, which I can legally share. You can try them at https://phoam.app/demos without an account. Uploading your own apps isn’t public yet, and using your own files would require the necessary rights. Also worth saying, AI has helped a lot with the coding, but I’ve been directing the project and testing the results. Which old Android or iOS game would you most want to play again?

projects.summary: 之前一直做内容站和联盟站，最近想换个方向，试做一个工具站 刚好圣诞节也快到了，就想有没有什么抽签、聚会小游戏之类的需求，可以拿来做第一次尝试.最后选了交换礼物抽签，也就是海外比较常见的 Secret Santa：一群人参加，每个人抽到一个人，给对方准备礼物. 功能简单, 第一次上手容易 填上活动名称、参加的人，再设置一下规则，就可以抽签了。比如情侣之间不想互相抽到，就把这两个人设成不能配对。每个人都会送出一份、收到一份，也不会抽到自己. 这些基础功能，DrawNames 之类的网站都有。我自己多想了了一点的是就抽完以后怎么分享 我把它做成了每个人都有一个单独的邀请链接，可以分别发给来参加聚会的人.对方打开，就能看到时间、地点、预算这些信息，再点一下看自己抽到了谁 组织者不用抽完签以后，再挨个打字告诉大家.不过组织者自己是可以查看全部结果的 网站叫 **Gift Name Picker**，目前是英文的，免费，不用注册.如果公司里面有办互相抽奖有可以用一下： [https://giftnamepicker.com/]( https://giftnamepicker.com/) 这次做下来，我还挺喜欢现在这个 UI 的! 整个站都是用 Codex 第一版就是那种比较常见的、 墨绿色,很像鹈鹕骑单车的风格，但我觉得少了点自己的风格 后来就去 Behance 和 Dribbble 找了喜欢的设计，截个图丢给 Codex ，它着照那个感觉改。改完反而挺惊喜的，配色、favicon ，还有页面上的一些小装饰，都一起帮我搭出来了.来回调了一版，就变成了现在这样。 现在网站主要就是三块： 抽签工具、其他交换礼物玩法的介绍，还有礼品推荐.其他玩法目前只是介绍，还没做成工具。 礼品推荐页里放了联盟链接，用这个方式变现, 现在是放 Amazon 的,但其实 Temu 佣金比较高,还在纠结 我之前做联盟站，所以还是会往这个方向想：既然大家是已经在组织交换礼物了，接下来可能就要考虑买什么，看看这两个需求能不能接起来。当然，目前只是这么想，能不能赚到钱还不知道. 至于广告，我的感觉是，这种工具很多人可能一年就来用一两次，暂时也没太指望靠广告赚钱。 后面还想加一个 Wishlist ，让参加的人填一下自己想收到什么。这样抽到他的人也有个参考，不用完全靠猜, 我看其他同类产品里有这个功能，感觉挺适合这个场景 第一次做工具站，先拿一个小需求练练手，如果你们组织过交换礼物，挺想知道实际最麻烦的是哪一步，有没有其他场景的类似需求之类的

projects.author: dragonknightk

github.name: dragonknightk/jav-speed-bump
github.description: 🚧 基于行为心理学与前额叶唤醒机制的戒色/防沉迷 Chrome 扩展：拦截成人站点、敏感搜索与 Steam 客户端重装，用 10 分钟逻辑推理题（数独/数织/24点/心算）陪你温和度过冲动浪峰 (Manifest V3 · 100% 纯本地)

projects.summary: 自荐一个刚上架 Chrome 应用商店的开源戒色与防沉迷浏览器扩展：色情减速带（JAV Speed Bump）。 GitHub （MIT 协议，中英双语） Chrome 商店： 开发背景：为什么传统的“网站封锁”对戒色无效？ 很多人在尝试戒掉色情网站或成人游戏（黄油）成瘾时，都会去改系统 hosts、配代理拦截规则，或者安装传统的网站黑名单插件。但凡亲身试过的人都知道：一堵死墙是拦不住自己的。 因为设下封锁的人是你自己，掌握解除开关的人也是你自己。白天理智在线时一切正常，但到了深夜孤独、焦虑或疲惫、多巴胺冲动上头的时候，花不到 30 秒就能把拦截规则亲手关掉，随后陷入“破戒—羞耻—彻底放纵”的恶性循环。 结合行为心理学中的「阻力成本（Friction Cost）」、「前额叶皮层唤醒」与「冲动冲浪（Urge Surfing，生理冲动浪峰通常在 10～15 分钟内自然消退）」，我开发了这款不靠生硬一刀切封堵、而是用逻辑算力帮大脑踩刹车的戒色扩展。 核心机制与特点 1. 多维度成人内容与 Steam 黄油防重装拦截： 内置 160+ 高危成人域名、成人专用顶级域及敏感搜索词过滤；同时针对“为戒黄油卸载了 Steam、却在深夜冲动重装客户端”的痛点，提供分级防护——日常逛 Steam 商店与社区完全正常，但一旦点击客户端下载，立即触发减速带拦截。 2. 10 分钟前额叶逻辑唤醒关卡： 触发拦截后进入逻辑题关卡，需连续完成 3 组随机生成的题目（六宫数独、数织 Nonogram、24 点、四则心算），题目难度随近期触发频率动态递增。通过调动工作记忆做逻辑推演，唤醒负责理性的前额叶皮层；右侧同步展示 15 分钟「冲动消退曲线」，中途切屏或最小化窗口会自动重置当前题组。 3. 诱因复盘与线下状态切换： 引导记录每次触发的诱因（无聊空虚、焦虑压力、深夜孤独、身心疲惫、碎片等待），给出 3 件立刻可做的线下状态切换小事，并在本地生成高发时段（0–23 时）与连续克制统计图表。 4. 24 小时冷静期与防卸载保护： 添加屏蔽规则立即生效；但移除任何规则或关闭防护，必须等待 24 小时冷静期，或当场完成 3 组高难度逻辑题。设置页还内嵌了一键防卸载上锁工具，可将浏览器扩展管理页的「停用 / 移除」按钮锁灰，防止冲动时直接卸载扩展。 5. 零依赖、100% 纯本地隐私保护： 基于 Chrome Manifest V3，全项目零第三方依赖，无任何远程脚本或网络上传，所有设置与触发记录仅保存在用户本机 chrome.storage.local。 界面截图

github.description: The fastest binary serializer for C#. Source-generated, zero-allocation: services, RPC, messaging, caching, storage, Unity and Godot.

projects.summary: Nino is a source-generated binary serializer for C#, and as far as we know the fastest one. In the same BenchmarkDotNet run on GitHub runners against MemoryPack 1.21.4, it serializes classes and polymorphic types 3.5–7.2x faster and deserializes them 1.7–2.1x faster (arrays of unmanaged structs are on par). Deserializing into existing objects allocates nothing. Reproduce: https://nino.xgamedev.net/en/docs/v4/benchmarks It is built to read bytes you do not trust: lengths are checked before allocating, depth is bounded, hash flooding is limited, and the read paths are fuzzed in CI. The bytes are a spec, not a memory dump, so CoreCLR, Mono, IL2CPP and 32-bit hosts write the same bytes, and runtimes for TypeScript, Go and Rust pass the same conformance corpus. Trade-offs: positional by default (VersionTolerant or Keyed for stored data), a 4-byte type id on polymorphic values, no System.Type, needs C# 9 and Roslyn 4.3+. Docs: https://nino.xgamedev.net

projects.title: Show HN: NLP capabilities of Opus, Astra, Argon measured by Codenames skills
projects.author: daluan
projects.summary: Hello Show HN, I'm a college student, and I enjoy playing word games like Codenames, but it can be hard sometimes to find enough people to play when everyone is available, so I made an app that allows you to fill any seat with an AI teammate and also play against AI. This way it allows for people to get the full strategic experience of codenames just on their own. Through this experiment, I was also able to measure and benchmark a few different LLMs through AWS Bedrock API calls and give them ELO ratings based on stuff like win rate and clue/guess accuracy. If anyone is interested, they can see more about my benchmarking methodology here: https://wordspies.com/hn#method . I think it's pretty interesting because it gives you a lot of insight into these various LLMs' NLP capabilities. A few interesting stats were that I rated Gemini 4 Argon at 1775, GPT-6.1 Sol at 1744, GPT-6 Astra at 1723, Claude Fable 5.1 at 1623, and Claude Opus 5.5 at 1592. There are quite a few interesting things you'll find from there, like how, although newer and more expensive models tend to perform better, there are some rare exceptions, like Kimi K2.5 slightly edging out Kimi K3. Check the site out if you're interested in NLP and data science and would like to see what level of frontier LLMs you can successfully beat!

projects.title: X/twitter 运营必用 Skill, 可以审查发帖, 也可以问问题
projects.author: liyu7352
projects.summary: 前段时间研究了一轮 X / Twitter 的公开推荐代码，整理成了文章。后来发现，这些内容更适合做成一个可以随时提问的工具：碰到具体问题，直接查对应的代码和适用条件。 于是做了 **For You Skills**，给 Claude Code 、Codex 、Cursor 等支持 Skills 的工具使用。 项目：[github.com/alexliyu7352/for-you-skills]( https://github.com/alexliyu7352/for-you-skills) 如果你也在经营 X ，可能纠结过这些问题： - 今天已经发了一篇，另一篇要不要等到明天？ - 一篇长文，应该发普通 Post 、Thread ，还是 Article ？ - 网上说“第二篇曝光打六折”，这个说法到底从哪来的？ - 草稿写好了，开头、长度和配图有什么具体问题？ 这些都可以直接问它。 我比较在意的是**回答的依据能不能查到**。所以除了研究结论，也把对应的原始代码链接、适用条件和未解决的问题整理进了知识库。回答时会查相关条目，再给建议；公开证据不足的地方，也要说明白。 比如“第二篇打六折”这个案例，重点就是查清楚代码里的“第二篇”到底在数什么，以及分数倍率能不能直接理解成曝光比例。演示里保留了这次问答和对应源码，可以自己核对。 有草稿的话，也可以让它审稿。它会检查实际开头、统计长度、考虑首图和后续配图、判断内容更适合哪种发布形式，并给出具体修改。目前一共 8 个技能，通过一个总入口按问题选择工作流。 安装先用这一条： ```bash npx skills add alexliyu7352/for-you-skills --skill x-assistant ``` 装好后，可以在对应工具里试着问： > 使用 x-assistant：我今天上午已经发了一篇 X 帖子，下午还有一篇不同主题的内容。该今天发还是明天发？请给建议，并说明相关源码支持什么、不能证明什么。 也说明一下边界：知识库基于特定版本的公开源码研究，不能据此确认全部线上配置，也不能保证涨粉或曝光。模型、联网和生图等能力由你使用的工具提供。 这里有 [78 秒案例演示及完整记录]( https://github.com/alexliyu7352/for-you-skills/tree/main/docs/demo)，之前的 [中文研究文章]( https://blog.go5.si/posts/zh/x-algorithm-teardown/) 也保留着。 想找一些本身就在用 AI 工具、也有 X 发帖需求的人试试。尤其欢迎拿你真正纠结过的问题，或者一篇准备发布的草稿来测试。 如果试了，最想听到的是：**它有没有帮你做出一个具体决定？哪一段回答仍然空泛，或者证据对不上？**

projects.title: [分享创造] 做了个把游戏录像整理成原型开发计划的小工具
projects.author: Aleks
projects.summary: # [分享创造] 做了个把游戏录像整理成原型开发计划的小工具 大家好，分享一个最近做的小项目：**rea-game**。 ![]( https://github.com/AleksChen/rea-game/raw/main/assets/cases/phantom-blade-zero-cover.jpg) 做游戏原型时，我经常会先找一段参考游戏录像。但看完之后，脑子里通常混着几种东西：画面里确实发生了什么、我猜测背后的规则是什么、还有哪些信息光看这段视频根本确认不了。 所以做了这个小工具，想把这些观察整理成一份能继续用于原型开发的材料。 它大致是这样工作的： 1. 用 FFmpeg 从本地游戏录像中按时间提取画面，并记录时间戳。 2. 人工检查画面和对应视频片段，把观察、推断、未确认的问题和实现建议分别写进 review 文件。 3. 运行命令生成 Markdown 报告，包括玩法循环、交互、界面、视听表现、待确认问题，以及一个原型实现计划。 它不会自动“看懂”视频。分析还是需要人来做，也可以请支持视觉输入的助手帮忙；工具负责把证据和结论组织起来，并检查时间戳和格式，尽量避免把猜测写成已确认的规则。 项目是 MIT 许可的开源 CLI ，使用 Python 和 FFmpeg ，在本地处理视频，不需要 API Key 。目前需要从源码安装： ```sh git clone https://github.com/AleksChen/rea-game.git cd rea-game python3 -m venv .venv source .venv/bin/activate python -m pip install . rea-game extract "/path/to/gameplay.mp4" -o out/my-game ``` [项目地址]( https://github.com/AleksChen/rea-game):https://github.com/AleksChen/rea-game
