This guide includes a question set, a rule sheet to print out, and everything else you need to know. If you don't want to print out anything, you can also use fermi.org/play to see the questions on your device. Fermi Poker combines the betting mechanics of poker with Fermi estimation questions like "How many new smartphones were sold worldwide in 2024?" or "How many chickens were slaughtered for meat worldwide in 2024?" Once you've submitted a range estimate, there are four betting rounds, with two hints and the answer revealed between them. The aspiration was to create a game that teaches important rationality concepts (Fermi estimation, Bayesian updating, cognitive empathy, world-modeling, emotional regulation, etc.) If you want to host a tournament at your school or university, please consider reaching out as I can provide some funding to cover the cost of poker chips and small prizes.

projects.title: 做了一个开源的 YouTube 桌面客户端 Lumtub：原生播放，推荐在本地跑，支持 Windows / Linux / macOS
projects.author: benedict00
projects.summary: # Lumtub：免费开源的 YouTube 桌面客户端 大家好！分享一个我做的开源软件 **Lumtub**。它是一个 YouTube 桌面客户端，支持 Windows、macOS 和 Linux，**免费、没有付费版，基于 GPL-3.0 完全开源**。 ![Lumtub 播放页]( https://raw.githubusercontent.com/0x696c757a696f/lumtub/main/docs/screenshots/watch.png) 🎞️ **一分钟宣传片**： https://github.com/0x696c757a696f/lumtub/raw/main/docs/promo/promo-en.mp4 --- ## 为什么做它 我每天在 YouTube 上看很多视频，但有三件事一直让我不舒服： 1. **浏览器播放 4K 视频时风扇狂转**； 2. **首页推荐越看越窄**，而且不知道为什么会推荐这些； 3. **看外语视频时**，为了双语字幕得装一堆浏览器扩展。 所以我做了 Lumtub：**不用浏览器内核，改用 mpv 原生播放，推荐算法完全在你自己的电脑上运行。** ![Lumtub 功能演示]( https://raw.githubusercontent.com/0x696c757a696f/lumtub/main/docs/screenshots/tour.gif) --- ## 核心特性 ### 播放 * **原生 mpv 播放**：最高 8K，自动选择电脑能硬解的编码（H.264 / VP9 / AV1），画质按钮直接标出 1080P60 这样的帧率。 * **播放控制**：迷你播放器、画中画、关灯模式、A-B 循环、倍速、逐帧和一键截图。 * **高画质直播**：直播支持 1080p 以上画质，直播聊天和聊天回放**可以显示成弹幕**。 * **投屏**：投到电视（Chromecast / DLNA），最高 4K，可选 8K。 * **内置下载**：下载完成后可以直接在应用里播放。 ### 推荐与隐私 * **本地推荐**：首页推荐在本机计算，**每张卡片都写明推荐理由**，可以标记“不感兴趣”。 * **数据只在本机**：观看历史、搜索记录和统计**只存在你的电脑上，不上传**。 * **不登录也能用**：不会擅自读取浏览器的 Cookie 或配置；只有你主动选择“用浏览器登录”时才会用到。 * **频道管理**：可以彻底屏蔽频道，也可以只设为“不再推荐”。 * **屏蔽 AI 视频（可选）**：开启后会隐藏标注为 AI 生成的视频，以及社区整理的 AI 垃圾频道名单里的频道。 * **频道管理**：可以彻底屏蔽频道，也可以只设为“不再推荐”。 * **专注模式**：隐藏首页推荐、评论和相关视频，只看想看的。 ### 字幕与语言 * **双语字幕**：第二字幕翻译第一字幕，**逐句对齐**。 * **沉浸式翻译**：标题、简介和评论都能翻译，可接多家翻译服务。 * **语音转字幕**：没有字幕的视频也能自动生成字幕（需自备 Key）。 * **AI 总结**：根据字幕先总结视频内容，再决定要不要花 40 分钟看完（需自备 Key）。 * **72 种界面语言**。 ### 登录（可选） * **Google 登录**：订阅、播放列表、点赞、评论，还能保存到 YouTube 播放列表。 * **电视码或浏览器登录**：社区动态、投票、给评论点赞，以及你有权限看的**会员专属视频**。 * **直播里发弹幕**：登录后可以在直播聊天里发言。 * **登录信息加密存本机**：浏览器登录会开一个单独的临时窗口，只保留 YouTube 的 Cookie 并加密保存，其他全部删除；观看记录默认不同步到 YouTube。 ### 发现与频道 * **分区探索**：像 B 站一样按分区和子分区浏览，可按为你推荐、热门、最新、冷门宝藏、新人创作者、长视频排序，也能自建分区。 * **按真实语言筛选**：会检查音轨和字幕，选“意大利语”就真的是在讲意大利语的视频。 * **频道页**：视频、Shorts、直播、播放列表、播客和社区动态都有，还能在频道内搜索。 * **订阅分组**：订阅可以分组，正在直播的频道会标出来。 * **按频道记住倍速和音量**：播客 1.5 倍、音乐 1 倍，自动切换。 ### 更多功能 * **内置插件**：SponsorBlock、Return YouTube Dislike、DeArrow（默认关闭，按需开启）。 * **外观**：浅色/深色、10 套配色、护眼暖光，还有紧凑模式和低占用模式。 * **系统集成**：关闭或最小化到托盘，接入系统媒体控制。 * **自动更新**：应用本体、yt-dlp 和 libmpv 都会自动更新，每个更新包都有**签名校验**。 ![搜索]( https://raw.githubusercontent.com/0x696c757a696f/lumtub/main/docs/screenshots/search.png) ![设置]( https://raw.githubusercontent.com/0x696c757a696f/lumtub/main/docs/screenshots/settings.png) --- ## 三个平台 **Windows** ![Windows 版]( https://raw.githubusercontent.com/0x696c757a696f/lumtub/main/docs/screenshots/windows.png) **macOS** ![macOS 版]( https://raw.githubusercontent.com/0x696c757a696f/lumtub/main/docs/screenshots/macos.png) **Linux** ![Linux 版]( https://raw.githubusercontent.com/0x696c757a696f/lumtub/main/docs/screenshots/linux.png) --- ## 技术栈 * **界面**：Flutter * **核心**：Rust * **播放**：libmpv * **解析**：yt-dlp --- ## 下载与安装 项目还在早期阶段，最新版本在 GitHub Releases： 🔗 **[下载 Lumtub]( https://github.com/0x696c757a696f/lumtub/releases/latest)**· **[项目主页]( https://github.com/0x696c757a696f/lumtub)** | 平台 | 说明 | | :--- | :--- | | **Windows** | 安装版或便携版，**不需要管理员权限**。 | | **Linux** | AppImage（x64 / arm64），需要 Debian 12、Ubuntu 24.04、Fedora 37 或更新的系统。 | | **macOS** | Apple 芯片和 Intel 芯片各一个版本。暂未做苹果公证，第一次打开请按 README 的说明解除隔离。 | --- ## 最后 欢迎下载试用、提 Issue。如果觉得有用，**给项目点个 Star 🌟 和捐赠就是对我最大的支持！**

projects.summary: 我是作者，自荐一个自己做的开源项目：Onion Board，Windows 上的音效板（soundboard）。 打游戏或语音聊天时按一个键，语音频道里的人就能听到你放的音效。这类工具通常要装虚拟声卡，再把聊天软件的麦克风换成虚拟设备。Onion Board 默认换了个做法：给你现有的麦克风加一个 Windows 音频效果，把音效直接送进去，语音软件和游戏继续用原来的麦克风，不用改选设备。 因为改的是 Windows 里的麦克风，用这个麦克风的软件一般都能听到。我主要在 Discord、Zoom 和游戏里测过，KOOK、YY 这些国内常用的语音软件还没测过，欢迎反馈。 全局热键：在游戏里也能触发，还支持游戏内浮层和 MIDI 设备。 变声器：内置多种声音，说话时实时变声。 文字转语音：打字后由电脑语音念出来，可以用 Windows 自带的语音，也可以接本机的 TTS。 简体中文界面：已经翻译好，不用另装语言包。 有几点先说清楚： 只支持 Windows 10 / 11。 第一次开启“直接送进麦克风”时，Windows 会要一次管理员权限。不想这样的话，也可以改用虚拟声卡。 安装包还没有代码签名，Windows 可能会弹出警告。 程序会发送一个匿名的每日使用计数，可以在设置里关掉。 这个项目是我借助 AI（Claude Code）开发的，提交记录里也看得到。 免费，没有广告，不用注册账号，采用 GPL-3.0-or-later 许可证。

projects.title: Show HN: An online shop where your friends can hurry the courier
projects.author: AmsterErdo
projects.summary: I built an emulator of a flash-sale fashion outlet with no registration and fake checkout that never takes money. You can browse items that are on sale, watch in real time as they go out of stock one by one, and get notified when they are back on sale (possibly with different prices). Every order placed on the website gets “tracking” which fails on the delivery day with one of 50 available reasons (for example, “a raccoon in the Newark depot has claimed your parcel; animal control reports that it seems happy there”). But you can also share the tracking with your friends, and they can hurry the courier; the more hurries, the more spectacularly it fails, until your parcel lands in the Svalbard seed vault, the North Pole, the International Space Station or some such place. The complete shop contents (campaigns, prices, item availability and stock levels) are computed from the current time with a fixed seed (FNV-1a for hashing, mulberry32 as the PRNG). I wrote the mechanism first in JS and then ported to PHP (for the website) and Flutter (for the mobile app); a test ran over several thousand random time points to verify they are identical. The Flutter app uses its own generator because it can work offline - no contact with the website is necessary. Item images are generated with OpenAI API, except models in swimsuits. OpenAI refused a lot of swimsuit image prompts, so I had to switch to Gemini for these as Gemini has no qualms about this kind of content. Does this kind of site feel like shopping to you? projects.summary: 我是作者 zhaoolee，自荐摄影学英语 Web（PicLex）。它把电影画面、双语台词和目标词放进同一张练习卡，支持看图拼词、句子听力与跟读，让学习者从熟悉的场景开始练英语。打开网页即可使用，无需注册；也能拍照制卡、导入自己的卡组，并通过 Docker 自托管。 亮点 从场景进入练习：经典电影卡组包含 100 张卡片、100 个目标词，拼写、听力和口语共用同一组内容。 把自己的生活变成学习材料：支持拍照制卡、导入 .piclexdeck，以及分享公开卡组的练习链接；另有歌曲、程序员英语和摄影等主题。 体验入口直接：无需登录即可开始，进度与导入内容保存在当前浏览器。 便于学习和二次开发：代码采用 MIT 许可，提供使用、开发、卡组发布文档及 Docker 部署方式。 截图或演示视频 在线体验 · 直接打开经典电影卡组 补充说明：AI 制卡会将照片发送给所选服务；相机和语音功能依赖浏览器支持与授权。公开卡组内容的权利以原来源为准，不包含在代码的 MIT 许可内，详见素材说明。

projects.title: 【开源项目自荐】Fun - 基于 C 转译且内置 M:N 虚拟线程的静态类型系统级编程语言
projects.author: omdxp

github.name: omdxp/fun
github.description: Fun is a statically-typed language that transpiles to C, combining safety and performance with C's efficiency.

projects.summary: Fun 是一款静态类型的自研编程语言，它直接转译（Transpile）为可读的 C 语言代码。该项目专注于提供极简的语言表面、强大的静态类型系统、实用的并发原语以及对编辑器极其友好的工具链（内置 FLS 语言服务器、格式化、诊断等）。 核心特性： 1. 高性能 C 转译： 编译产物为 C 语言，具备极佳的跨平台便携性、极低的运行时开销与零性能损耗的 C 语言互操作能力。 2. 混合并发模型： 同时支持 M:N 虚拟线程（通过 fork 实现轻量级 I/O 任务与异步资源加载）以及 1:1 系统原生 OS 线程（std.thread，用于固定高帧率的系统如渲染和物理引擎）。 3. 灵活的数值类型： 提供高层默认数值类型（num, dec）的同时，支持固定宽度标量类型（i32, u64）以及任意宽度的整数（iN, uN），极其适合游戏引擎底层与系统级开发。 4. 开箱即用的工具链： 内置代码格式化（fun -fmt）、静态分析（fun lint）与调试映射（fun -g）。

projects.title: Show HN: Lo-fi layered over air traffic control (recorded myself)
projects.author: kkoppenhaver
projects.summary: Some of you will remember lofiatc.com and I was a huge fan and heavy user until it got shut down. It was streaming LiveATC feeds, and when those got cut off the site went dark and has been ever since. So I decided to bring it back in a way that wouldn't fall to the same fate. I've been an ATC nerd for years (ever since you could still listen to the radio on the arm rest of commercial flights) so this summer I rented a Fiat 500, stuck an airband antenna on the roof, and spent a day driving to three Chicago airports with my laptop in the passenger seat to record the audio I needed in person. This took me to the viewing area at Chicago Executive (KPWK), the cell phone lot at O'Hare (KORD), and the top of a parking garage at Midway (KMDW). The whole chain was a Bingfu mag-mount antenna connected to an airband filter and then to an RTL-SDR, all captured via SDR++. If you're interested, you can read a full post on how the recording day came together here: https://finalapproach.fm/field-notes/chicago-recording-day/ Once I had all the audio, I layered it on top of lo-fi tracks and created one "album" per airport, each with its own vibe. Each track is named after something unique to that airport or something we heard on the radio, and I've had it on as background music for work for about two months now, which is why I built it in the first place! Also important to me was putting this out there in the world with no signup required and no ads. Just like on the original site, finalapproach.fm gives you two sliders that let you push the radio up or the music up depending on which you want to hear more of. And there are pre-built mixes on YouTube and all your favorite music streaming services (search for Final Approach Radio). Happy to answer questions about the radio side, the legal side (as much as I can, obviously), or the editing (largely done with Claude Code).

projects.title: Show HN: Open-world text adventure played through AI agents
projects.author: pontes
projects.summary: Hey HN, I am building Eremoterra, this experiment of trying to make a game out of an MCP (to learn MCP stuff, but also had a lot fun designing the game). You play in your own agent. The server returns a fact sheet for the place you are. The world is like real Earth, but empty (until the players start to arrive) and only the natural wold (as humanity never existed). The agent narrates the sheet and can write what you confirm in a sort of lore book, typed events and fixed templates, so the model cannot become the source of truth. I added some NPCs that, i hope, bring some interesting emergent behaviour. Within the game there are also "journeys", which is more like traditional text adventures of trying to find something and bringing it home. The world is one Rust process and one RocksDB. The Earth is 233,280,000 parcels of one arcminute. Geography is a memory-mapped atlas of about 1.9 GB, built from public natural-state data. Light, weather, and tide are a function of that atlas, the coordinates, and the clock. The world game runs the real time clock. I would love to have some beta testers for it. https://eremoterra.com

projects.title: 花了 6 年搭了一个去中心化的社交网络作品
projects.author: printfcoder
projects.summary: AI 真的要淘汰传统的程序员角色了。我大概是在 2019 年有这个想法，那个时候对各大厂商的 App 后台数据上报非常不爽，就想未来有没有一种可能，每个人掌握自己的社交关系？而不是被几个大厂拿去当成护城河。 所以这些年就慢慢找时间往这个方向靠，期间探索、架构、实现都搞过一些玩具版本。进展非常慢，一方面确实是时间不够；另一方面是需要相大量的技术储备，前后端、Mobile App 、架构、网络、设计等，都要自己来一个一个去摸索，尝试找了一些朋友，都对这个场景兴趣不是很大，基本只有极少人对隐私、数据保护有相当的诉求，大部分朋友还是习惯于让大公司掌握、管理自己的数据资源，故而在前期找到志合的朋友比较困难。 但是，我们的这些身外之物，我真的认为个人未来最重要的东西就是数据，而不再只是金钱。 我搞的这套方案，是一个去中心化的社交网络。可以简单看看 Desktop 端的运行效果：三个人，三台各自独立部署的节点，没有中心服务器，消息直接在节点之间联邦送达。下面是三个独立节点第一次联邦跑通时的对话。 我暂时给这个方案起名叫 Peers-Touch ，意为大家可以直接轻碰接触。整体思考是通过一个去中心化（联邦式）网络框架，在上头先长了这个社交产品。每个人跑自己的 Home Station ，可以运行在 NAS 、树莓派、云主机都行；身份、关系、消息全在自己手里（也就是个人 Station 上），Station 之间像邮件一样联邦互连，端到端加密，规划中，我也做了 Agent 、小程序和区块链，都跑在自己的 Station 上，作为智能时代和扩展方向的预留。 下图是大体的产品架构 https://i.imgur.com/HNzSw2V.png 再说怎么做出来的。 这个项目 6 年前开工。前几年是传统写法，一个模块一个模块地做；后面基本是我带着 Trae 完成的——一个人，Go / Rust / TS / Kotlin / Swift 五个栈，80 多万行，从架构到真机验收。不是我突然变猛了，是干法变了：做什么、架构怎么定、人怎么排，AI 给；具体写，AI 也给。 视频在这，2 分 52 秒，从节点部署、联邦互联、端到端加密到 Agent 都过了一遍（播放器可能默认压到 360p ，点右下角齿轮切 1080p ）： https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ZU6kMt3BQrs 代码在这： https://github.com/peers-labs/peers-touch ，还在成长，欢迎拍砖，欢迎 Star 。 一些目前的设想： https://peers-touch.vercel.app/ 最后说点感想。 我当程序员第 14 个年头了，从传统行业、金融、互联网都干过，现在团队正在转行做 Agent 相关的事，虽然也是趋势所迫，不过我也认为 Agent 本身也是过滤，一方面传统行业的技能、知识等，会慢慢向大模型基建下沉，这是已经能看到的事实，未来这个协作过程会从现在的“领域-Agent-LLM”的路径，直接转成“领域-LLM-Infra”，LLM 平台会进一步泛化现在 Agent 的能力变成口语就能驱动的万物即可 Agent 的样子，讲几句话就能做一个自己的 Agent ，当全部都是 Agent 的时候，约等于没有 Agent ，当然只是我的观点。 未来 Idea 到实现会是个比较廉价的过程，AI 挤压我们传统就业空间的矛盾总会有利的一面，大家都可以大胆去选择探索未来。“因为生命有限的，所以我们的选择，都被赋予了重量”。 程序员转不转型，已经不用讨论了。一个人端到端干完这几年，我反而觉得有三样东西更值钱： 1. 想得出新东西。做什么比怎么做稀缺，这轮 AI 替不了。 2. 学得动。新东西到手，几天之内得能拿它干活。 3. 落得了地。从想法到真机跑通、能交付，结果和锅还是你的。 造的过程，也在体验生命的厚度，哪怕失败了也是能接受的。

projects.title: Show HN: Grid – A Hold'em arena where your AI agent plays your strategy (Beta)
projects.author: taelimoh
projects.summary: Hi HN, my friend's team and I have been building a game called GRID, a dog poker game with an AI twist. Under the cute dog graphics, GRID is an arena where LLMs compete, with no-limit hold’em as the medium. You duke it out as a strategist, vibe coder, and bot maker. Why: models get compared on benchmarks all the time, but rarely as my agent against yours in its truest form. GRID is our attempt at creating that arena, because we believe this type of game will exist in the future, as AI becomes as common a tool as the browser. How it works: * Paste a prompt and an MCP config into Claude Code, Codex or any MCP client. The agent waits for its turn and sends actions back through tool calls. * The strategy is text written in the game, up to 6,000 characters. We thought it’d be cool to have a preset, “Play like Elon”, to show you what you can do. * You can change the strategy any time, and it applies from the next action. You can even ask your AI to change it for you, based on what it learns about its opponents’ strategies from the match history. * Free beta. Play chips only. We just opened up the game today and are gathering data on how to steer this ship next. Rough edges: * MCP can be finicky, especially if you refresh your browser while in a match. If this happens and you can’t get your agent to connect, wait 5 min and retry | log out using the settings button at the top left and log back in. Stability is currently our top priority. * MCP also uses a lot of tokens, more than the game should, because every tool call costs tokens. We plan to overhaul this with a new connection type in a future version so it’s much more efficient. * There’s a built-in local model for folks who don’t want to use their own AI. It plays basic hold’em OK but struggles to follow written strategies. If you want to try it, I’d recommend leaving your strategy blank. Sadly, it plays best with no instructions. * House bots fill empty seats. We made this choice so matches happen even when only a few people are online. Honestly, I’m most curious how you’d write a strategy that holds up against everyone else’s agents. And if MCP setup breaks on you, please tell me. We'll be in the thread as long as possible.

projects.title: Show HN: A terminal viewer for plain text data files (JSON,YAML,CSV,XML,)
projects.author: rjrodger
projects.summary: When I started working hands-on with OpenAPI specifications, it became clear very quickly that using an editor to read large volumes of deeply nested JSON sucks, a very great deal. So I went looking for something to help, and came across https://jless.io This is an awesome terminal app for navigating nasty JSON documents. I am forever indebted to Paul Martinez for writing this tool. But it did have some gaps. It couldn't reload files that had changed, keeping your place in the JSON structure, which I really needed. And it only loaded one file at a time. But unfortunately it was written in Rust, and I didn't know Rust, and back in the pre-AI days that was kind of a huge blocker. But of course once we got models that could actually write decent code, the obvious idea came to me - I'll just add my features and submit a PR! Happy days. Except by that stage my requirements had grown - I also needed to handle many other file formats, like CSV, TOML, INI, and even XML. So I got side-tracked extending another side-project - an easy going JSON parser that supported comments, and trailing commas, the usual sort of thing. During COVID, with a SaaS startup in the events space now on the rocks, I was looking for some distraction and decided to refactor this little easy-going JSON parser of mine. It used a generated parser and was slow. I read some blog posts about how all production-grade language parsers are pretty much hand-crafted recursive descent, and thought, how hard could it be! Five years later, after many many fun experiments, and production use, I ended up with a runtime parser system: https://tabnas.dev This is a quirky approach to parsing that is partly recursive descent, partly a state machine, and mostly empirical hacking. It works, and it's pretty fast, and I use it for real projects. It has the nice property that grammars are dynamic - you don't generate code, the grammar is executed. A fancy regular expression engine, but revved up to parse anything into a proper abstract syntax tree. Now with that in hand, I could return to the original project and create my own version of jless that solved the itches I needed to scratch: a watch mode; multiple tabs; load any data format into a tree structure Now I still don't know Rust. I mean I like the idea, but there are only so many hours in the day. But now we have AI, so now I do get to go to the candy store. Combining jless.io, and tabnas.dev, and my requirements, I built (caused to be built?), aless - the less for any format! Now this is also a nice stress test for the tabnas parsing engine, and I was very pleased about that too. So if you need to review lots of data structure files on the command line, and need a terminal app to do so, this is for you. I can't help but be struck by the irony however that the need for such a thing is much less now - I mostly get agents to look at large JSON documents now. Still, our puny human brains need help sometimes, and this lets me review documents when I need to. It is also really nice and satisfying to see how easy it is to now bring together open source components to create what is essentially personal software. But I think the key thing out of this little project is that the basic physics of software development remain the same. Software should be built from components glued together. Components should have well-defined interfaces. Aim to reduce cognitive load - this is useful to both humans and machines. Yes, the entire thing could be built from scratch, using a textual specification, and be a mire of over-engineered AI slop, and still be perfectly usable. But the way I actually built it, with AI as a coding companion, using components was deeply satisfying because I still understand the essence of the code, while being able to ignore the accidental complexity. Components give you another layer of abstraction with fewer things to think about, and that allows your human mind to stay in the game.

projects.author: jtommy14
projects.summary: Hey HN, I’m Jake. I know this isn't for work or AI tool like most other products on here, but hopefully this will bring some joy and adventure to your personal life. I used to spend hours combing Goodreads and Reddit to see if I’d actually like a book before I commit to buying it and reading it. A single number for the rating, like 4.37 stars, wasn’t really helpful because everybody values different things (characters, plot, writing, etc). And the reviews were most helpful, but reading them all took a bunch of time and I’d often run across spoilers. So for over a year I kept a spreadsheet rating every book I read on what actually decided whether I liked it. For me, that’s mostly characters, plot, ending, and twists. I thought this was actually helpful, unlike a single rating, plus it was super fun to rate books this way. So I built Fic Scout, a way for everybody to rate books based on these categories and then help you find your next book. Of course, the new features are growing and growing: you can now save a TBR list, play a fantasy book/wordle game, and we’ve built a book recommendation engine. But building is fun, and books are fun, so here we go. Question for HN: when you pick your next fiction book, what’s actually most important to you in a book? Plot, characters, prose, ending? Something else?

You play by doing the job: answering mail in Lookout Express, chatting with simulated colleagues in Natter, adding up favours in the spreadsheet, and doing small Paint jobs. Over a year of in-game days you get promoted, people join and leave, and a daft office story goes on. You can also slack off with Solitaire, FreeCell, Mahjong, Draughts, 2048, and a word puzzle. Technical bits people might find interesting: - Everything on screen is drawn by a GUI toolkit I written in C#. Windows, menus, tree views, list views, drag and drop and colour schemes all draw their own pixels, with bitmap fonts. Nothing uses native widgets or HTML. - The game uses raylib (Raylib CS wrapper) and via the browser as .NET WebAssembly (AOT) drawing to a canvas. - Saves live in IndexedDB as a zipped copy of the "C: drive". You can download that zip as a backup and restore it. I made this after making the GUI toolkit, which I made because of my love of the aesthetic of this time. I should mention that this doesn't work well on a phone sized screen; you really need a computer to play. I should also mention that I did use Claude Code to write a good chunk of this after I had established the drawing/widget core.

projects.title: Show HN: Resource Manager – Manage all resources on the computer
projects.author: BIOcanse
projects.summary: Hello everyone, I'm BIOcanse. Windows Task Manager has inaccurate readings and limited monitoring items. Various hardware adjustments are also very separated—CPU, GPU, and fans all require their own individual software. Their interfaces and interactions are primitive, and they often overwrite each other's configurations. Moreover, driver management of the CPU and GPU is too clumsy, and the memory usage issue on Windows is also very serious. So I made Resource Manager to view and manage all these resources in one place, making monitoring and scheduling work seamlessly together. Monitoring: This software integrates almost every possible monitoring item, letting you look at your computer from a God's-eye view! Scheduling: One of the core features. It uses algorithms I wrote to optimize memory usage and reasonably schedule processes across multiple CPU cores. It also supports GPU scheduling, which means it can switch the GPU a program uses while it is running. For example, after launching a game, if GPU usage is high or VRAM is about to overflow, it will move the remaining software to another GPU (for most personal computers, this is usually the integrated GPU). Reporting: Many times, computer performance problems are actually just caused by a single program or driver—the benefits of 100 programs optimizing themselves cannot make up for a memory leak in just one program. The reporting page reports abnormal resource usage (CPU, GPU, memory, VRAM, disk read/write, network traffic, and causing system interruptions). Hardware Adjustment: All the parameters you can think of for hardware like the CPU and GPU can be adjusted here. However, my own setup is an AMD CPU + NVIDIA GPU, so other setups still need to be verified. I do have several computers with Intel CPUs to verify Intel CPU support, but I really do not have a single AMD GPU. Although most of it uses mature open-source dependencies, there may still be risks, so please use it with caution.

projects.author: kolchinski
projects.summary: Hey, Alex here, I'm one of the founders. We've built phone agents for enterprise customers for two years and kept seeing the same failure: agents that mishear callers and then do something confidently wrong. We're announcing two things in this launch. #1 is the stack: instead of one transcription model → one LLM → one TTS, most conversation turns runs through several transcription models and LLMs (a fast and a slow LLM in the same call, models switched per turn, audio sent straight to an LLM alongside transcripts). That gets us 99.4% on Big Bench Audio. That's the second-highest published score; the only model above us takes almost 9 seconds to start talking as far as we've measured, which doesn't work on a phone call. Eval set and transcripts are on Hugging Face - http://huggingface.co/datasets/kolchinski/bba-storm-eval #2 is Zeus, an agent that configures our voice AI stack per use case and per conversation. We tried doing this with Claude Code and Codex and they were bad at it: they can't run simulated calls out of the box, don't do well with audio input and spotting problems in calls, and tend to blindly believe vendor marketing about which model is best vs actually trying the models. Zeus has evals on real calls, can simulate calls in hard situations, and listens to production calls to find problems, so it can check its own work the way a coding agent runs tests to make sure the code it wrote actually works. Pricing is cost-plus (vendor prices + hosting + a 17–25% margin), no subscription. Zeus is free for now. You can try it with a free $10 credit. Happy to answer questions.

projects.title: Show HN: Pots – Open-source Grok Bot alternative, used by 6 startups for a month
projects.author: Crokily
projects.summary: Hi HN, I'm Crokily. Pots is an AI coworker that lives in the chat your team already uses: Slack, Discord, Telegram, or any channel with a Chat SDK adapter. It is MIT-licensed and runs on a machine you give it, with the model you choose. To be honest, the first time I used Grok Bot, its design really impressed me. Unlike OpenClaw before it, it was not just Claude Code connected to a chat app. It truly cared about how it works with people. It felt like a living AI assistant, and working with it was painless. That is the idea I kept learning from the whole time I built Pots: it is not an agent hooked up to a chat channel. It should be a coworker that feels alive and is comfortable to work with. But Grok Bot is only Grok's bot. Which model you get depends on your X subscription, your data and your machine are all in the cloud, and most of all, it is a standalone app, and most of its features serve that app. Pots is a bit different. In Sydney I have talked with quite a few founders. Grok Bot is good, and it helps them a lot with their personal tasks. But when I asked who had actually put Grok Bot into their company's work to make their startup team faster, nobody had. So I think Pots is in a different place from Grok Bot, and from most open-source Grok Bot alternatives: it grew out of what real startup teams need. Before I open-sourced it, 6 small startups I met at startup events had been using it with me for over a month. Pots is built first for the channels startup teams already work in, not for an app of its own, so most of what it does serves the places where you actually work. The teams use Pots as a middle layer: a CEO talks ideas through with the team in chat, Pots listens, and then it builds a prototype that both sides can check. They use Pots for competitor research: because Pots runs inside their channels, it knows their product well. Not only the GitHub repo, but the team's daily discussions and what the team cares about. Pots has been listening quietly the whole time, so it knows the product with no setup at all. It also works well with each channel: it talks to people with the channel's own controls, like Slack and Discord buttons and cards, and when it hands over something complex, it deploys a page with its built-in server so everyone sees it in a better form. So Pots is different from Grok Bot and from most open-source alternatives. It came out of what real startup teams need. Its channel features start from what each company's work needs, and it can join your real work setup with no setup and still do well, instead of being one more app that nobody uses and that is hard to start with. And it ran in real business for a while before I cleaned it up and open-sourced it. The difference from Grok Bot is also exactly why I made Pots an open-source Grok Bot alternative. I have OpenAI and Claude subscriptions with plenty of quota, and my own servers, so I don't want an X subscription to limit me. I want to use whatever model I want and do whatever I want. I can even switch to an open model, and none of my data goes into anyone's pocket. Try it (Node 24+, macOS, Linux or Windows): the easiest way is to ask your coding agent (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor) to read docs/for-agents.md in the repo and set up Pots for you. Or by hand: npm install -g pi-durable-bot, then pots init. I'd love feedback, especially on how it decides when to act.

projects.title: Show HN: Black Ops II statically recompiled to native ARM64 macOS
projects.author: adrbn
projects.summary: I recompiled the three Black Ops II executables (campaign, Zombies, multiplayer) from 32-bit x86 Windows to native ARM64 macOS, ahead of time. Remill lifts each function to LLVM IR, a set of custom passes rewrites it, and the result links against a hand-written Win32 runtime whose Direct3D 11 is drawn by Metal. No Wine, no Rosetta, no JIT, one process. About 150,000 functions are translated; anything the translation misses falls back to a small x86 interpreter, so a gap costs speed instead of crashing. On an M1: campaign 51-60 fps, Zombies 57-60 on six maps, multiplayer against bots 53-60. The repo contains no game files and no translated code. It converts your own Steam copy on your Mac, which takes about 1h45 on an M1. Much of the work was done with AI coding agents, and I spent most of my time on verification: frame pacing against the game's own clock, byte checks on the input files, and run logs for every claim in the README. It's a beta. Split-screen Zombies is the current work in progress. Happy to answer questions about the lifting, the Win32 runtime or the D3D11-to-Metal layer.

projects.summary: I made an agent-native 3d/vfx engine. Agents are good at making interesting scenes in Blender/Unreal/Nuke/etc. But these tools are fundamentally limited compared to what coding agents are capable of. Many simplifying assumptions are baked into these tools in order to fit human authoring methods. In vork, agents write the whole scene as code, including their own shaders, materials, cameras and physics, and vork renders it on the GPU. The core API fits in about 2,500 tokens. So, for example, almost every 3d engine assumes light moves in a straight line. Light near a black hole does not; so the best you can do in e.g. Blender is faking gravitational lensing. In vork, you can model it for real. If you want a camera lens that simulates a dragonfly's eye, or realistically-modeled Fata Morgana, this is also possible in vork.

projects.author: chelsea8085
projects.summary: 之前一直做内容站和联盟站，最近想换个方向，试做一个工具站 刚好圣诞节也快到了，就想有没有什么抽签、聚会小游戏之类的需求，可以拿来做第一次尝试.最后选了交换礼物抽签，也就是海外比较常见的 Secret Santa：一群人参加，每个人抽到一个人，给对方准备礼物. 功能简单, 第一次上手容易 填上活动名称、参加的人，再设置一下规则，就可以抽签了。比如情侣之间不想互相抽到，就把这两个人设成不能配对。每个人都会送出一份、收到一份，也不会抽到自己. 这些基础功能，DrawNames 之类的网站都有。我自己多想了了一点的是就抽完以后怎么分享 我把它做成了每个人都有一个单独的邀请链接，可以分别发给来参加聚会的人.对方打开，就能看到时间、地点、预算这些信息，再点一下看自己抽到了谁 组织者不用抽完签以后，再挨个打字告诉大家.不过组织者自己是可以查看全部结果的 网站叫 **Gift Name Picker**，目前是英文的，免费，不用注册.如果公司里面有办互相抽奖有可以用一下： [https://giftnamepicker.com/]( https://giftnamepicker.com/) 这次做下来，我还挺喜欢现在这个 UI 的! 整个站都是用 Codex 第一版就是那种比较常见的、 墨绿色,很像鹈鹕骑单车的风格，但我觉得少了点自己的风格 后来就去 Behance 和 Dribbble 找了喜欢的设计，截个图丢给 Codex ，它着照那个感觉改。改完反而挺惊喜的，配色、favicon ，还有页面上的一些小装饰，都一起帮我搭出来了.来回调了一版，就变成了现在这样。 现在网站主要就是三块： 抽签工具、其他交换礼物玩法的介绍，还有礼品推荐.其他玩法目前只是介绍，还没做成工具。 礼品推荐页里放了联盟链接，用这个方式变现, 现在是放 Amazon 的,但其实 Temu 佣金比较高,还在纠结 我之前做联盟站，所以还是会往这个方向想：既然大家是已经在组织交换礼物了，接下来可能就要考虑买什么，看看这两个需求能不能接起来。当然，目前只是这么想，能不能赚到钱还不知道. 至于广告，我的感觉是，这种工具很多人可能一年就来用一两次，暂时也没太指望靠广告赚钱。 后面还想加一个 Wishlist ，让参加的人填一下自己想收到什么。这样抽到他的人也有个参考，不用完全靠猜, 我看其他同类产品里有这个功能，感觉挺适合这个场景 第一次做工具站，先拿一个小需求练练手，如果你们组织过交换礼物，挺想知道实际最麻烦的是哪一步，有没有其他场景的类似需求之类的

projects.title: Show HN: Jacq, a DSL that compiles model and kernel descriptions to CUDA
projects.author: keithba

github.name: ImpossibleComputing/jacq
github.description: Jacq inference compiler and CUDA kernel DSL

projects.summary: I was working (with agents) on testing out various attention algorithm ideas I had, and I found that the existing infrastructure/libraries made it more difficult than it should be. So I created Jacq, a DSL and compiler. A jacq file describes a model’s configuration, weights, layers, and pipeline. Jacq turns it into a standalone CUDA inference runtime and a Python weight exporter. Kernel descriptions can also generate CUDA harnesses. The easiest way to try it is the TinyLlama example in the README. Building, validating, visualizing, and generating CUDA only require Rust. Of course, running inference does require an NVIDIA GPU, CUDA, Python dependencies, and weights. Jacq doesn't support other GPU vendors (AMD, etc) or Metal, yet (PR's welcome!) There's also an experimental vLLM patch to compile and patch your jacq file into a vLLM build, as well. Feedback very welcome!

projects.title: X/twitter 运营必用 Skill, 可以审查发帖, 也可以问问题
projects.author: liyu7352
projects.summary: 前段时间研究了一轮 X / Twitter 的公开推荐代码，整理成了文章。后来发现，这些内容更适合做成一个可以随时提问的工具：碰到具体问题，直接查对应的代码和适用条件。 于是做了 **For You Skills**，给 Claude Code 、Codex 、Cursor 等支持 Skills 的工具使用。 项目：[github.com/alexliyu7352/for-you-skills]( https://github.com/alexliyu7352/for-you-skills) 如果你也在经营 X ，可能纠结过这些问题： - 今天已经发了一篇，另一篇要不要等到明天？ - 一篇长文，应该发普通 Post 、Thread ，还是 Article ？ - 网上说“第二篇曝光打六折”，这个说法到底从哪来的？ - 草稿写好了，开头、长度和配图有什么具体问题？ 这些都可以直接问它。 我比较在意的是**回答的依据能不能查到**。所以除了研究结论，也把对应的原始代码链接、适用条件和未解决的问题整理进了知识库。回答时会查相关条目，再给建议；公开证据不足的地方，也要说明白。 比如“第二篇打六折”这个案例，重点就是查清楚代码里的“第二篇”到底在数什么，以及分数倍率能不能直接理解成曝光比例。演示里保留了这次问答和对应源码，可以自己核对。 有草稿的话，也可以让它审稿。它会检查实际开头、统计长度、考虑首图和后续配图、判断内容更适合哪种发布形式，并给出具体修改。目前一共 8 个技能，通过一个总入口按问题选择工作流。 安装先用这一条： ```bash npx skills add alexliyu7352/for-you-skills --skill x-assistant ``` 装好后，可以在对应工具里试着问： > 使用 x-assistant：我今天上午已经发了一篇 X 帖子，下午还有一篇不同主题的内容。该今天发还是明天发？请给建议，并说明相关源码支持什么、不能证明什么。 也说明一下边界：知识库基于特定版本的公开源码研究，不能据此确认全部线上配置，也不能保证涨粉或曝光。模型、联网和生图等能力由你使用的工具提供。 这里有 [78 秒案例演示及完整记录]( https://github.com/alexliyu7352/for-you-skills/tree/main/docs/demo)，之前的 [中文研究文章]( https://blog.go5.si/posts/zh/x-algorithm-teardown/) 也保留着。 想找一些本身就在用 AI 工具、也有 X 发帖需求的人试试。尤其欢迎拿你真正纠结过的问题，或者一篇准备发布的草稿来测试。 如果试了，最想听到的是：**它有没有帮你做出一个具体决定？哪一段回答仍然空泛，或者证据对不上？**

Fuzz instead. appfuzz works with WASM and runs the .wasm thousands of times against a simulated backend and reports problems: crashes, n+1 queries, XSS, SQL injection, leaked secrets, blown IO/CPU/instruction budgets. projects.title: Show HN: Lo-fi layered over air traffic control (recorded myself)
projects.author: kkoppenhaver
projects.summary: Some of you will remember lofiatc.com and I was a huge fan and heavy user until it got shut down. It was streaming LiveATC feeds, and when those got cut off the site went dark and has been ever since. So I decided to bring it back in a way that wouldn't fall to the same fate. I've been an ATC nerd for years (ever since you could still listen to the radio on the arm rest of commercial flights) so this summer I rented a Fiat 500, stuck an airband antenna on the roof, and spent a day driving to three Chicago airports with my laptop in the passenger seat to record the audio I needed in person. This took me to the viewing area at Chicago Executive (KPWK), the cell phone lot at O'Hare (KORD), and the top of a parking garage at Midway (KMDW). The whole chain was a Bingfu mag-mount antenna connected to an airband filter and then to an RTL-SDR, all captured via SDR++. If you're interested, you can read a full post on how the recording day came together here: https://finalapproach.fm/field-notes/chicago-recording-day/ Once I had all the audio, I layered it on top of lo-fi tracks and created one "album" per airport, each with its own vibe. Each track is named after something unique to that airport or something we heard on the radio, and I've had it on as background music for work for about two months now, which is why I built it in the first place! Also important to me was putting this out there in the world with no signup required and no ads. Just like on the original site, finalapproach.fm gives you two sliders that let you push the radio up or the music up depending on which you want to hear more of. And there are pre-built mixes on YouTube and all your favorite music streaming services (search for Final Approach Radio). Happy to answer questions about the radio side, the legal side (as much as I can, obviously), or the editing (largely done with Claude Code).

projects.title: Show HN: A terminal viewer for plain text data files (JSON,YAML,CSV,XML,)
projects.author: rjrodger
projects.summary: When I started working hands-on with OpenAPI specifications, it became clear very quickly that using an editor to read large volumes of deeply nested JSON sucks, a very great deal. So I went looking for something to help, and came across https://jless.io This is an awesome terminal app for navigating nasty JSON documents. I am forever indebted to Paul Martinez for writing this tool. But it did have some gaps. It couldn't reload files that had changed, keeping your place in the JSON structure, which I really needed. And it only loaded one file at a time. But unfortunately it was written in Rust, and I didn't know Rust, and back in the pre-AI days that was kind of a huge blocker. But of course once we got models that could actually write decent code, the obvious idea came to me - I'll just add my features and submit a PR! Happy days. Except by that stage my requirements had grown - I also needed to handle many other file formats, like CSV, TOML, INI, and even XML. So I got side-tracked extending another side-project - an easy going JSON parser that supported comments, and trailing commas, the usual sort of thing. During COVID, with a SaaS startup in the events space now on the rocks, I was looking for some distraction and decided to refactor this little easy-going JSON parser of mine. It used a generated parser and was slow. I read some blog posts about how all production-grade language parsers are pretty much hand-crafted recursive descent, and thought, how hard could it be! Five years later, after many many fun experiments, and production use, I ended up with a runtime parser system: https://tabnas.dev This is a quirky approach to parsing that is partly recursive descent, partly a state machine, and mostly empirical hacking. It works, and it's pretty fast, and I use it for real projects. It has the nice property that grammars are dynamic - you don't generate code, the grammar is executed. A fancy regular expression engine, but revved up to parse anything into a proper abstract syntax tree. Now with that in hand, I could return to the original project and create my own version of jless that solved the itches I needed to scratch: a watch mode; multiple tabs; load any data format into a tree structure Now I still don't know Rust. I mean I like the idea, but there are only so many hours in the day. But now we have AI, so now I do get to go to the candy store. Combining jless.io, and tabnas.dev, and my requirements, I built (caused to be built?), aless - the less for any format! Now this is also a nice stress test for the tabnas parsing engine, and I was very pleased about that too. So if you need to review lots of data structure files on the command line, and need a terminal app to do so, this is for you. I can't help but be struck by the irony however that the need for such a thing is much less now - I mostly get agents to look at large JSON documents now. Still, our puny human brains need help sometimes, and this lets me review documents when I need to. It is also really nice and satisfying to see how easy it is to now bring together open source components to create what is essentially personal software. But I think the key thing out of this little project is that the basic physics of software development remain the same. Software should be built from components glued together. Components should have well-defined interfaces. Aim to reduce cognitive load - this is useful to both humans and machines. Yes, the entire thing could be built from scratch, using a textual specification, and be a mire of over-engineered AI slop, and still be perfectly usable. But the way I actually built it, with AI as a coding companion, using components was deeply satisfying because I still understand the essence of the code, while being able to ignore the accidental complexity. Components give you another layer of abstraction with fewer things to think about, and that allows your human mind to stay in the game.

Windows, menus, tree views, list views, drag and drop and colour schemes all draw their own pixels, with bitmap fonts. You can download that zip as a backup and restore it. I made this after making the GUI toolkit, which I made because of my love of the aesthetic of this time. I should mention that this doesn't work well on a phone sized screen; you really need a computer to play. I should also mention that I did use Claude Code to write a good chunk of this after I had established the drawing/widget core.

I started with french names using official statistics about first and last names, which also gave me a pretty simple model for likely anagrams: P(first + last) = P(first) * P(last). Then, I started checking which anagra-names (I coined the term) appeared in the 2021 Facebook leak. Finally, I improved my ranking using a factorization model. All this is available as a light and fast webpage thanks to a lot of cool algorithmic tricks detailed here: https://louisabraham.github.io/anagranames/how.html About the use of AI: Claude Code was fantastic for building the frontend (including the interactive globe) and writing the MLX code (I would otherwise have used PyTorch, which is slower on my machine). It also handled the quantization with very little guidance, which was particularly useful since I'm not an expert in that area. That said, I'm glad I learned CS before LLMs existed and still master it enough to work out the ideas and specs for everything else in my head / on paper before handing the implementation over to the agent.

projects.title: 分享一家值得关注的专线机场：节点和家宽 IP 资源挺有特色
projects.author: sonicywalker
projects.summary: 现在选机场，我觉得最重要的已经不是测速能跑多少 Mbps，而是日常使用稳不稳定、AI 工具能不能正常连接、节点 IP 质量怎么样。 尤其是平时经常使用 ChatGPT、Claude Code 这些 AI 工具，网络稳定比单纯的峰值速度重要得多。任务执行到一半突然断连，或者某个节点突然无法访问 AI 服务，都挺影响体验的。 最近比较值得关注的一家是 MESL 机场。 MESL 运行了五年多，采用 BGP 多线入口 + IEPL/IPLC 专线中继，不是单纯追求低价、大流量的路线。 它有几个比较吸引我的地方： ① 节点覆盖比较广： MESL 有 170 多个节点，覆盖 50 多个国家和地区，除了常见的美、日、新、港节点，还能找到不少冷门地区。 ② 家宽 IP 是一大特色： 除普通落地节点外，还有不同国家和地区的家庭宽带、商业宽带 IP。对于经常使用海外 AI 服务、需要特定地区网络环境的用户来说，选择余地比较大。 ③ 适合 AI 和日常办公： ChatGPT、Claude 等主流 AI 服务都有对应的可用节点，配合稳定的线路，也适合需要长时间联网的 AI 编程场景。 ④ 影音娱乐也能兼顾： 除了 AI 工具，部分节点还支持 Netflix、Disney+ 等流媒体解锁，日常刷 YouTube、看海外视频也能用上。 ⑤ 套餐比较灵活： 有不同流量档位，不管是轻度使用还是多设备、大流量需求，都可以根据自己的情况选择。 如果你比较看重专线稳定性、家宽 IP、丰富的全球节点，以及 ChatGPT、Claude Code 等 AI 工具的使用需求，MESL 确实是一家值得尝试的机场。 👉 MESL 机场官网链接 亮点 如果你比较看重专线稳定性、家宽 IP、丰富的全球节点，以及 ChatGPT、Claude Code 等 AI 工具的使用需求，MESL 确实是一家值得尝试的机场。 👉 MESL 机场官网

projects.title: Show HN: Yogurt – Free, private, open-source alternative to Granola
projects.author: brownrout
projects.summary: Hey HN, I’m Eric and I want to share an OSS project that I’ve been building in my free time. Yogurt is a free, MIT licensed desktop app that uses on-device AI models to transcribe, summarize, and chat with your meetings. Similar to Granola, Yogurt runs in the background and does not join your calls. But unlike Granola, Yogurt is open-source, free to use, and private. Your meeting transcripts, call recordings, and summaries never leave your computer. As small OSS models have gotten faster and more powerful, Yogurt seemed like a pretty obvious win for privacy and cost conscious folks. You do not need a frontier model to summarize meeting notes or answer questions about them. And if you want to make your notes available to a frontier model, you can just share it with Anthropic, OpenAI, etc. directly via Yogurt’s local MCP server. There’s no need to use a paid cloud service as a middleman. I tried some of the most popular OSS note taking tools, and most were missing features like calendar integration, MCP server, etc. or required you to connect or create an account. And more than that, they didn’t feel polished enough for it to be something I actually wanted to use daily, and so I built Yogurt to scratch that itch. I spent a lot of time fine-tuning every UI interaction/animation and optimizing the model calls to get the most out of your hardware + make it snappy. To support Windows/Mac/Linux, I decided to go with Electron. I use whisper.cpp for transcription and Apple’s on-device SpeechAnalyzer if your system supports it. For call summaries and questions, I use a local open weight LLM that automatically gets downloaded and set up based on what your hardware can handle without your cooling fans firing off like crazy (this part uses llama.cpp). I’ve spent a lot of time working on details like echo detection/reduction, global/folder/local level search respectively, and auto-end recordings. Hope this is useful for any of you who have held out on using AI note tools for privacy or cost reasons, or for folks using cloud tools who want to switch to something free and open source that still feels great to use. Would love to hear what you think about the onboarding and note taking experience :)

projects.summary: （MIT，免费） 提示词优化器（prompt-optimizer）是一个 Skill，也就是写给 AI 读的一份工作说明。把它装进 Claude Code、Codex 这类能读技能文件的工具，或者把 SKILL.md 贴进 ChatGPT GPTs、Claude Projects 的自定义指令里，它会把你随手写的需求或已有的提示词，改成一份可以直接复制给 AI 用的提示词。它只改提示词，不替你做提示词里的事。 它的规则偏保守，重点是保真： 原话逐字保留。 你的需求原样放在「用户原话（按此执行）」一节，数字、日期、人名、文件名、「下周三前」这类相对时间都不改。 补充只是建议。 优化器加的步骤和检查写在「补充说明」里，开头固定一句「与用户原话冲突时，以用户原话为准」；不自己加字数、格式和验收标准。 缺的信息不编。 AI 能查的写明去哪查；只有你知道的留成待填空位；真正的缺口列在「待确认」里，并写明不回答时怎么处理。 分得清指令和材料。 贴进来的材料里写着「忽略之前的规则」，只当成要处理的文字。 按需自动调用。 问题清楚就直接回答；只有明显含糊、缺关键信息，或你明确说「优化提示词」时才调用，省调用次数和 token。 一个版本适用所有语言，跟随你的语言回复，原话和材料不翻译。 Claude Code 安装： text /plugin marketplace add Samuel-Shek/prompt-optimizer-skill /plugin install prompt-optimizer@prompt-optimizer Codex 和手动安装见 README。测试方法和局限也写在仓库里（考卷规模小，主要在 Claude 和 GPT 上测过），欢迎提交它做错的案例。

Ramble is designed for Apple Watch & offline first - to capture voice quickly and queue up messages to send when it can. The slim relay backend uses cloud transcription (Grok Whisper currently), then holds the message in an inbox for your agent to pickup and process, then gets purged from the backend after acknowledgement. No accounts, no signups. It uses Apple's App Attest for endpoint security. It works great with current gen personal agents like Muse, GrokBot, etc. (GrokBot supports incoming webhooks so its instant. Muse doesn't, so it polls every couple minutes (without waking the agent)) The linking process is surprisingly easy. Would love to hear what you think!

projects.title: Show HN: Get your coding agent off ~2019 JavaScript, onto modern web primitives
projects.author: paulirish

github.name: GoogleChrome/modern-web-guidance
github.description: Keep your coding agent up to date with the latest web best practices

projects.summary: Browsers natively handle a lot of what used to take 50 lines of JS (or a dependency): `CSS.highlights` for text range highlighting without <span>s everywhere, `<dialog>` and showModal() give you backdrops and ideal focus management, `field-sizing` to auto-grow textareas as the user types.. (Something yesterday's ftrain post touched on [0]) Models know about some of these by name, but consistently won't default to using the platform-native solution and instead prefer the incumbent <div>+JS based pattern. We started an effort in Chrome to supplement coding agents with this key domain knowledge and we're shipping our 1.0 today, in collaboration with Firefox, MDN, and Edge. 200+ guides (~1.7MB) of curated, hand-crafted implementation best-practices from web experts, updated as the web evolves. (Open source, obv, so.. we'll welcome your bikeshedding ;) Readable versions here: [1] I've spent the last 9 months obsessing over how to ship this as an agent skill + (Agentic RAG) CLI without blowing up your context window. (Or cedeing activation mechanics to MCP dynamic tool search). The skill description is minmaxed for activating on relevant frontend tasks. The RAG work I'm pretty proud of… originally a 500mb native stack down to a ~7MB pure-JS package, ~10ms search on your CPU. We just introduced a deterministic 'legacy-scan' (trained on 30k github repos) to identify old 'n dusted patterns that your agent can modernize. (92% avg precision on held-out repos.) People make a lot of claims about what coding agents are good/bad at. We wanted receipts, so we invested heavily in eval infra [2] to help us hill-climb, but also to identify when knowledge is common enough we can prune our guides. (Ofc, some of the things we thought AI didn't know turned out to be wrong :) We run codex/claude/agy against 200 tasks without the skill and then with.. In total ~1,700 playwright/AST-based assertions. Agents go from 55% pass unguided to 92% guided. Try it out: DISABLE_TELEMETRY=1 npx modern-web-guidance@latest install DISABLE_TELEMETRY=1 npx modern-web-guidance@latest search "animate dialog modal" DISABLE_TELEMETRY=1 npx modern-web-guidance@latest legacy-scan ./src If you spot something wrong or weird, give us a holler! Longer write-up on the 1.0: https://developer.chrome.com/blog/modern-web-guidance-v1 --- 0: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50416456 1: https://developer.chrome.com/docs/modern-web-guidance/guides 2: https://googlechrome.github.io/modern-web-guidance-src/

projects.summary: Hi HN! I built Editmamei, a local MCP server for Adobe Photoshop and GIMP. I built it because I wanted to connect Claude to a powerful photo editor, since Claude can't generate images itself. Apparently I wasn't the only one, Adobe previewed their own local Photoshop MCP yesterday, announcing at Adobe MAX a private beta in early 2027. Editmamei brings the AI agent of your choice into Photoshop and lets it do as much or as little of the editing as you want. It has tools to measure and inspect, apply filters, transform the image, insert other images and create objects, and it can use some of Photoshop's more advanced features like Select Subject and Sky Replacement. The agent "sees" each edit with downscaled previews, layer trees, histogram calculations and other tools, so someone who has never used Photoshop can ask for a recommended edit, and a professional can hand Editmamei the specific directions for tedious actions and batch automation, keeping the finishing and favorite parts for themselves. Everything is done layer by layer in a fully editable PSD, just as a normal Photoshop user would work. Photoshop has more features overall, but GIMP is just as capable for normal photo processing and design. The main difference is the Adobe-specific tools; GIMP doesn't have heal/clone or AI subject and sky selection. Photoshop runs on Windows and Mac; GIMP runs on Windows, Mac and Linux. Source available: https://github.com/editmamei/editmamei I'd love feedback, and suggestions for other editors this could support!

projects.summary: Hi HN, I built Whisperstream, a free and open-source dictation app for Windows. Stream-1 Mini is a Qwen 0.6B finetune for removing filler and applying spoken corrections. Superwhisper is the only Windows app that offers this, is paid, and in our benchmark we outperform their S1 mini with 36% less failures. projects.summary: hi HN! I built Mimzie, an agent neutral AI workspace inspired by the Claude Suite (Docs, Sheets, Slides) and Cowork. It's a free desktop app that runs ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, and Grok in their native CLI harnesses. Think T3 Code or Conductor but for knowledge work. It's basically a GUI for managing knowledge work agents in various form factors. One of those form factors is Bots, akin to Grok Bot or Dots. The original idea for mimzie was simple: I pay for Claude and ChatGPT, and a lot of my day-to-day work lives in .xlsx, .pptx and .docx files. Moreover, I was sick and tired of losing context between AI platforms. I didn't want to bet the house on one AI lab's product, be it the ChatGPT or the Claude Desktop app. So I built an AI desktop app that was agent neutral. The goal of mimzie is to bring the kind of agent workflows that devs have had with codex and claude code into the hands of everyone. And to have a friendly GUI to do it. I've found that the personal agents, hermes and openclaw, are intimidating to set up and confusing to the average non-technical person. some of the core principles of mimzie: - your file stays your file: edits are done locally and .docx, .pptx, .xlsx, and .md and synced to the cloud after - every change is reviewable: edits show up as tracked diffs that you accept or reject, at the smallest unit that makes sense (e.g. a sentence in .docx) - free, and no new subscription needed: bring whichever AI plan or plans you already have. You shouldn't have to pay twice for the same inference, and you SHOULD take advantage of the insane subsidization in the current ChatGPT and Claude plans. - Bots with any AI: I love the concept of grok bot, not so much its limited choice of models. I strongly believe that long-standing "ai teammates" should be agent neutral and in your control Try mimzie out: it's a free beta at mimzie.com it's early, lots of rough edges, but I've had the time of my life developing it. I'd love to answer questions and hear any and all feedback.

projects.title: Show HN: Pots – Open-source Grok Bot alternative, used by 6 startups for a month
projects.author: Crokily
projects.summary: Hi HN, I'm Crokily. Pots is an AI coworker that lives in the chat your team already uses: Slack, Discord, Telegram, or any channel with a Chat SDK adapter. It is MIT-licensed and runs on a machine you give it, with the model you choose. To be honest, the first time I used Grok Bot, its design really impressed me. Unlike OpenClaw before it, it was not just Claude Code connected to a chat app. It truly cared about how it works with people. It felt like a living AI assistant, and working with it was painless. That is the idea I kept learning from the whole time I built Pots: it is not an agent hooked up to a chat channel. It should be a coworker that feels alive and is comfortable to work with. But Grok Bot is only Grok's bot. Which model you get depends on your X subscription, your data and your machine are all in the cloud, and most of all, it is a standalone app, and most of its features serve that app. Pots is a bit different. In Sydney I have talked with quite a few founders. Grok Bot is good, and it helps them a lot with their personal tasks. But when I asked who had actually put Grok Bot into their company's work to make their startup team faster, nobody had. So I think Pots is in a different place from Grok Bot, and from most open-source Grok Bot alternatives: it grew out of what real startup teams need. Before I open-sourced it, 6 small startups I met at startup events had been using it with me for over a month. Pots is built first for the channels startup teams already work in, not for an app of its own, so most of what it does serves the places where you actually work. The teams use Pots as a middle layer: a CEO talks ideas through with the team in chat, Pots listens, and then it builds a prototype that both sides can check. They use Pots for competitor research: because Pots runs inside their channels, it knows their product well. Not only the GitHub repo, but the team's daily discussions and what the team cares about. Pots has been listening quietly the whole time, so it knows the product with no setup at all. It also works well with each channel: it talks to people with the channel's own controls, like Slack and Discord buttons and cards, and when it hands over something complex, it deploys a page with its built-in server so everyone sees it in a better form. So Pots is different from Grok Bot and from most open-source alternatives. It came out of what real startup teams need. Its channel features start from what each company's work needs, and it can join your real work setup with no setup and still do well, instead of being one more app that nobody uses and that is hard to start with. And it ran in real business for a while before I cleaned it up and open-sourced it. The difference from Grok Bot is also exactly why I made Pots an open-source Grok Bot alternative. I have OpenAI and Claude subscriptions with plenty of quota, and my own servers, so I don't want an X subscription to limit me. I want to use whatever model I want and do whatever I want. I can even switch to an open model, and none of my data goes into anyone's pocket. Try it (Node 24+, macOS, Linux or Windows): the easiest way is to ask your coding agent (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor) to read docs/for-agents.md in the repo and set up Pots for you. Or by hand: npm install -g pi-durable-bot, then pots init. I'd love feedback, especially on how it decides when to act.

projects.title: Show HN: ApiClay – Turn a Website, Google Sheet or Database into a Paid API
projects.author: apiclay
projects.summary: Hi HN, I’m a reverse engineer, and I’ve seen the same problem repeatedly: people need data, but the path from “I need this” to “my app, agent, or workflow can use it” is messy. Vibe coders want a working endpoint in minutes. Developers want clean docs, predictable JSON, and no surprise integration work. Businesses want to enrich lists, monitor changes, and safely expose internal data. AI agents need APIs they can discover and call reliably. Sometimes, the API simply doesn't exist. ApiClay makes that whole loop easier. You can search a catalogue of APIs and datasets, inspect them in a playground, and copy ready-to-run JavaScript, Python, or cURL snippets into your app. Each API has its own reference, pricing, trials, and usage terms, so you can see what you’re calling before you go live. But ApiClay is not just an API marketplace. If the API you need does not exist, you can create one with Website to API: give it a page, map the fields you care about, and publish a stable JSON endpoint. It works with static and JavaScript-heavy pages, and can return clean Markdown, JSON, text, or links. You can also turn what you already have into an API: * MySQL, PostgreSQL, MongoDB, Google Sheets, Airtable, Excel/CSV, and HTTP services can become API endpoints. * Import an OpenAPI/Swagger file to get docs, a playground, and billing for an existing API. * Publish only the fields you choose, control access, set trials, plans, usage limits, and pricing. * Aggregate multiple providers into one tidy response for comparison-style products. For AI, ApiClay exposes an MCP endpoint so Claude, ChatGPT, or custom agents can search for an API, inspect it, and call it. The idea is simple: instead of an agent hallucinating a data source, it finds a real API and returns an answer backed by live data. There are also practical data tools beyond discovery: * Websets / enrichment: upload a list, enrich each row, set a spend cap, and export the result. * Monitors: watch an API or webpage and receive a signed webhook when something changes. * Cloud browser: automate a browser session for pages behind clicks or JavaScript rendering, then return the values your app needs. * Extraction: turn a page into clean Markdown, JSON, text, or links without maintaining your own scraper. For people publishing APIs, credentials stay encrypted on ApiClay and are not exposed to buyers; publishers control pricing, limits, trials, and access. For consumers, browsing and reading docs are free, while paid calls are charged per request and shown before use. *ApiClay is where you find the data API you need, build the one that is missing, let AI agents use it, and optionally sell it.* We’d love feedback from HN—especially from developers building data-heavy products, teams dealing with messy internal sources, and anyone experimenting with agent-driven workflows.

projects.title: Show HN: DBDelve – Open-Source DB Client Made with Rust and GPUI
projects.author: shayan_abbas
projects.summary: Hi HN, I’m Shayan and a few months ago I started building a DB Client DBDelve with a focus on performance and just making something that feels good to use (in the spirit of Zed, Ghostty, and other tools that just feel pleasant to use). For my workflow I’ve always looked for performance, especially since some time ago I had a really outdated machine and any kind of bloat was really noticeable, I remember using DBeaver and it just crashing on me multiple times, I also had to use postGIS which just made it worse. I migrated all my essential dev tools to use the ones with performance in mind (Zed, Ghostty etc) but the only thing that was missing was DB Client. The main choices everyone has are DBeaver which is a memory hog and an overkill for most of the tasks imo. The other options like Datagrid, Beekeeper, TablePlus are either electron based so bloated and memory hogs or paid and closed-source. DBDelve 0.3.6 against DBeaver 25.3.1 on the same Postgres table, median of 5 runs each (2026-10-11, M1 Pro, 32 GB). Times are from the action to the rows rendered. DBDelve DBeaver Launch 1.1 s 5.2 s Idle memory 133 MB 606 MB 1,000-row query 0.21 s 1.96 s 1M rows, time 56 s 208 s 1M rows, memory [1] 4.9 GB 17 GB [1] The whole 1M-row, 100-column table pulled into memory on purpose, with the row limit off. Not a normal use case; DBeaver's heap limit had to be raised manually for the benchmark. Scrolling perf with 1 million rows loaded with 100 columns each: https://youtu.be/V2MOhJYFqIE It has most of the features most devs would need for 90% of their workflow plus some more I thought would be a nice touch: Readonly, read-write and Full Access modes Glass themes (If you’re into them, I am) Keyboard focused with every keybinding customizable Organization of connections into projects Me and some other folks have been daily driving it for more than a month now and most good feedback comes on it having a really simple UI to navigate, very stable for its age and the performance of course. I’m also sharing here because those people tell me this has potential to grow so I’m trying my hand at distributing it. Just want to give a huge shoutout here to the Zed team for GPUI, it's a breeze to work with if you just get through them not updating the crate officially on crates.io but the community has found the solutions for it, you just have to dig deep for it. It performs extremely well and just the HTML-like structure of it, makes it easy to understand for someone from a web dev background and agents are very good at writing it too. GPUI component also solves a lot of problems with having a good component library we can use. I think for anyone starting a GPUI project now, GPUI-kit makes a lot of sense, it just bundles GPUI, GPUI-component together and has some optimizations adding retained mode which is experimental but could provide a lot of benefit, so think all things considered it should be the default way. The major optimization I did was just lowering the memory overhead by using packed rows which reduced the memory usage by 40% on large datasets (8.1GB to 4.9GB on a 4GB table loaded in app), everything else came bundled in with Rust and GPUI mostly or they just made it very easy. Limitations: It's not signed and notarized, identity verification from apple's side has been a nightmare but it should be signed soon. Don’t expect feature parity with more mature clients for now, the general direction of this right now is the zed way of adding features in but after making sure the core workflows are done with a high quality. Do give it a try, you can import your connections from dbeaver and tableplus. https://github.com/ShayanAbbas1/dbdelve

projects.title: Show HN: Aircad – Professional drafting and 3D modeling in the browser
projects.author: peetle
projects.summary: Aircad is a professional CAD system running in the browser with deep AI integration. It includes professional grade drafting and documentation tools, NURBS-based solid modeling, and a lot more. You can make professional quality design documents with it. It is all integrated behind a scripting API that can do anything you can do in the interface and also perform complex modeling operations efficiently. It reads and writes file formats like DXF, DWG, STEP, and 3DM. I built Aircad because I was frustrated with what was out there. Current CAD tools are expensive and slow to improve. New features barely move the needle. With Aircad, you have fast, powerful geometry tools for just about anything, from conceptual models to your final design. The newer generation of web-based CAD isn’t comprehensive enough to complete a project or is slower than existing desktop products because it sends performance-sensitive work to a server (OnShape), or isn’t designed to scale to real work in a collaborative setting (many "toy" CAD tools). Current CAD collaboration workflows are fragile, costly, and complex. They’re file-based and separate the design artifacts (eg PDFs) from the source. Collaboration is often an expensive add-on that raises your subscription, is hard to learn, and feels unnatural. Aircad builds it in: version history, drawing comparison, forking, and realtime collaboration. AI in most CAD tools is tacked on as a plug-in instead of being deeply integrated, and those plug-ins are often inefficient, hard to adopt, and costly. Aircad has a built-in AI agent and a comprehensive scripting API with a stage-and-commit workflow, so you know exactly what is happening during a complex change. You can use AI to write new scripts and commands that extend Aircad with repeatable, shareable workflows.

密码存在数据目录的 password 文件里（默认 ~/.oh-my-agent-web/password），不用系统变量；之后不管用 局域网 IP、外网 IP 还是域名访问，输密码就能进 —— 不需要再配 --allow-host。 密码只能在本机定：远程访问时若还没设密码，只会看到「请先在本机设置」（/setup、/api/auth/setup、/api/auth/password 对远程一律 403），否则谁先扫到端口谁就接管了。 反代 / 隧道请带上 X-Forwarded-For（来源校验会看它，否则分不清是本机还是外网）。 登录保护：同一个来源连续输错密码 3 次就暂停 30 分钟（锁定期内连密码都不比对），可在 设置 → 远程 里改次数 / 时长（1–20 次、1–1440 分钟）；策略和未过期的锁都存在 <数据目录>/login-guard.json，重启服务也不会解锁。「设置 → 远程」里还有一列登录活动（哪来的 IP、成功/错第几次/被暂停，最新在最前），存在 <数据目录>/login-activity.json（最近 200 条）。 在家目录直接敲 oh-my-agent-web 也能用，但家目录当工作区不安全（文件树 / 搜索 / agent 的 cwd 会是整个 home），这时会自动改用 <数据目录>/workspace 并打一行提示；想指定项目就用 AGENTWEBCWD=/path/to/project。 各引擎还有自己的逃生阀（都有默认值，通常不用配）：AGENTWEBCODEXBIN / HOME、AGENTWEBDSHBIN / HOME / MODEL / PATCH、AGENTWEBOPENCODEBIN / ARGS / MODEL、AGENTWEBCLAUDEBIN / ARGS / MODEL（默认自动探测 claude-code-acp / claude-agent-acp，没装就直说）。 它是什么，不是什么 是：一个把 agent 的「过程」摊开给你看的前端。思考块、工具调用、改动文件、token 与花费，都在对话流里；你能在回合中途插话、把某段话圈出来提意见、另开一条不落盘的临时对话问一句就走。 不是：不是新的 agent 引擎，也不是把会话搬到云上的 SaaS。它不重写 prompt、不接管工具实现 —— 你装的是 pi / Codex / Claude Code / opencode / DeepSeek Harness，工作台只是给它们配了一套能看的界面、能点的按钮和能落盘的会话列表。 三条硬纪律： 1. 不引数据库：会话就是引擎写的 JSONL / thread，网页只读它、改它的名字、必要时删它。 2. 不假装：引擎没有的能力就在界面上藏起来（能力矩阵），面板拿不到数据就说清楚，不拿别的引擎的配置冒充。 3. 不越界：默认只听 127.0.0.1；要远程就 -H 0.0.0.0 + 先在本机设好密码（或 -P）。 对话 流式正文 + 可折叠思考块 + 工具卡。工具卡上给参数、完整命令（可复制）、输出、耗时与成败；一次回合里的思考与工具调用跑的时候只显示最新一组里的那句说明（思考和命令卡都不画，正在跑的命令由最底下那行状态位实时报；顶上那行「N 段思考 · N 次工具 · 耗时」带秒表），跑完自动收成那一行（最后结论之前的一切都进折叠），点它看完整时间线。 每条回复的尾注是这一轮的用量：输入（未命中缓存）/ 输出 / 缓存命中 / 这类路径可直接点开预览。 插队、排队、停止 回合正在跑的时候，输入框不会锁死： | 动作 | 含义 | |---|---| | 插队（steer） | 立刻生效，作为下一条指令插进当前回合 | | 排队 | 排在本回合结束之后，队首是谁一目了然，随时可撤回 | | 停止 | 中断当前回合，保留已经产出的内容 | 插队只有 pi 引擎支持（它的 SDK 有 streamingBehavior: "steer"）；别的引擎没有这个语义，宿主会降级成排队，而不是硬发第二条把活跃回合冲掉。 注释：把一段话圈出来提意见 在对话里选中一段文字，会浮出一个小工具条：添加到会话 / 标注 / 在临时会话中提问。 「标注」给这段文字挂一条评论，正文上会留一个 ①②③ 编号徽标，输入框里多出一个「N 条注释」的胶囊 —— 点开能逐条看、改评论、删掉，或者「放进输入框」。 发送时会自动拼成这样的块（也可以手动「放进输入框」，那就只发你自己写的话）： 标注 1： 面板从 y=0 开始，但顶栏的 z-index 是 45 这里要再压缩一句 注释是本地锚点：按「原文 + 前后文」定位，所以正文重排、流式追加之后徽标仍能挂回原处；它存在当前浏览器的 localStorage（按会话隔离），不进服务端、不上云，换个设备看不到。 文件的行引用是另一条路：在预览里选中行（Shift+点 连选、Ctrl/Cmd+点 加选、右键出行菜单），「追加到对话」写进草稿的是 @web/src/App.tsx:120-138 这样的路径 + 行号，让 agent 自己去读。 临时对话：问一句就走 顶栏那颗「临时会话」（或右栏工作区落地页的第一张卡）会在右栏另开一条聊天： 不落盘：会话只存在内存里，关掉标签就销毁，不进侧栏、不留文件； 主对话照旧跑，两边互不打断； 想留下就点 保存为正式对话，此时才写出会话文件（临时会话没有的历史也能保住）； 可以同时开多条，每条一个独立通道、独立标签。 该能力依赖引擎的「内存会话」：pi 支持；Codex 的 thread 本身就在它自己的库里，所以没有「保存」按钮。它不是「换皮的新会话」，也不等于子代理 —— 临时对话是人开的窗口，子代理是 agent 派出去的子任务。 cwd>/<ISO><uuid>.jsonl（首行 {type:"session",id,timestamp,cwd}） | | Codex 会话 | Codex 自己的 thread 存储（thread/list \| resume \| delete） | | opencode / DSH / claude 会话 | 各自的数据目录（opencode 按 cwd session/list；DSH 读 ~/.dsh；claude 读 ~/.claude） | | 会话标题 | pi 取首条 user 消息（只读头 60 行）；改名 = 追加 sessioninfo.name | | 工作台状态 | ~/.agents/skills/、~/.pi/agent/agents/、~/.pi/agent/mcp.json | | 本机界面偏好 | 浏览器 localStorage（agent-web. 前缀：主题、字号、宽度、快捷键、注释、标签页） | 安全模型 默认只听 127.0.0.1；远程要显式 -H 0.0.0.0（或指定别的地址）。 身份判定：对端是回环且 Host 是回环 → 放行（本机不用密码）；其余一律要密码，未设密码时远程全拒。 密码只能在本机设 / 改（本机 设置 → 远程 的密码框、打开 /setup，或启动时 -P）：远程不能设第一个密码 —— 否则端口一暴露，谁先扫到谁接管。密码落盘在 <数据目录>/password（一行明文，0600），改完立即生效、不用重启；-P 给的也会写进去，下次重启不必再带。设了密码则走 cookie（agent-web-auth，7 天 HttpOnly）或 HTTP Basic；登录失败默认连续 3 次就暂停 30 分钟（次数与时长在 设置 → 远程 里改，范围 1–20 次 / 1–1440 分钟，锁会落盘、重启不解锁）。 域名 / 局域网 IP / 外网 IP 都不需要白名单：同源请求直接放行，远程来的请求一律交给密码那道门（--allow-host 一般用不上）。跨源门禁只保留给「真的是从本机来」的请求 —— 那才是 CSRF 的靶子（本机直连免密码）；判据用真实来源（X-Forwarded-For 已算过），所以反代把 Host 重写成 127.0.0.1 也不会误伤自己的域名。 工具与命令走审批：只读工具（read / grep / find / ls）与只读命令自动放行，其余按 scopeKey（工具 + 可执行名或目标目录）询问；点「总是允许」把规则写进 approval-rules.json（原子写，坏文件当空）。 回合结束时清掉该会话所有悬置审批，不会挂在那等下一个人点。 上传的临时文件、会话缓存都在数据目录里，不写进你的项目。 内置网页的代理不带 cookie、iframe 沙箱不含 allow-same-origin（否则远端 JS 能摸到 localStorage 与 RPC）。 远程暴露 = 两条：-H（让外面连得上）+ 密码（在本机 设置 → 远程 设一个，或 -P）。域名白名单不需要；域名 / 外网 IP / 局域网 IP 一视同仁。 开发 在仓库根目录先 npm install，然后： bash npm run dev # 一条命令起两个进程 对外仍然只有一个 25257（Vite 监听并反代），后端躲在内部 25258：开发和生产记同一个地址。 前端热更新走 Vite，后端 tsx --watch 自动重启。 手机调试：npm run dev -- --host 0.0.0.0。 | 命令 | 作用 | |---|---| | npm run typecheck | 服务端 + 前端两套 tsc --noEmit | | npm run lint | oxlint（server / web/src / scripts） | | npm run format | prettier 全仓格式化（format:check 只检查；.md 故意跳过） | | npm run build | 服务端 tsc + 前端 vite build 到 web/dist | | npm run icons | 用 playwright-core 重新生成 PWA 图标 | 两个工作流，没有单独的 ci.yml： .github/workflows/release.yml（v 标签或手动触发）：npm ci → typecheck → lint → build → npm pack --dry-run → npm publish（OIDC）。单测与 format:check 暂未进门禁。 .github/workflows/pages.yml（docs/site/ 变更时）：把 docs/site 原样发布到 GitHub Pages。 单测在本地跑：node --import tsx --test tests/unit/.test.ts。 排错 为什么用 npm ci 而不是 npm install：直接依赖普遍很新，npm install 会拿版本范围去 registry 重新解析，镜像源（公司 Nexus、npmmirror 等）没同步到那些版本就报 npm error notarget。npm ci 直接用锁文件里的精确版本。 1. npm error notarget No matching version found → 镜像没同步。先 npm config get registry，再临时用官方源：npm -g install oh-my-agent-web --registry= 2. EBADENGINE / 启动即报 Node 版本 → 需要 Node ≥ 22.19（node -v 确认）。 3. node-pty 编译失败（多见于 Linux）→ 先装 python3 / make / g++ 再 npm -g install，或用一行脚本的 --with-build-tools 让脚本代劳。 4. 起不来但 oh-my-agent-web status 说「陈旧锁」→ 之前进程没退干净，下次 start 会自动接管；确实僵着就删 <dataDir>/server.lock。 5. 端口被占 → oh-my-agent-web -p 25258，或先 oh-my-agent-web stop。 6. 内置网页一片空白 → 该站点重登录 / 重脚本，代理不隧道 cookie；点 ⧉ 用系统浏览器。 7. 界面报 engine.providererror: This operation was aborted（偶发）→ 这是传输层被打断（模型刚连上、代理换了条连接、请求体被回收），不是模型真的拒绝。现在遇到这类瞬时错误会自动重试 2 次（1s / 3s 退避，界面上只留一条「正在重试」的提示），重试成功就不报错；如果还是失败，去 <dataDir>/logs/agent-web.log 里搜 provider 报错 / 模型调用失败，每条都带 sessionId / attempt / code / 原始 message（以前这类错误只变成界面上一根红条，日志里一个字都没有）。点「停止」导致的中断不会重试，也不会报红条。 8. 想看引擎到底在干什么 → AGENTWEBLOG=info aw：pi 自动重试（SDK 自己那层）、自动重试成功、这一轮被中断 都记在日志里。 9. 界面报 请求失败：HTTP 502（或「后端正在重启或还没起来（HTTP 502）」）→ 这是前端到后端那条链路，不是模型报错：开发态 npm run dev 是 Vite(25257) 反代后端(25258)，改 server/ 下的文件就会重启后端，那一两秒的窗口里 POST /api/rpc 就会 502（终端里是 http proxy error: connect ECONNREFUSED 127.0.0.1:25258），正在跑的回合也会被抽掉（会话里最后一条是 toolUse、没有 errorMessage 就是这个特征）。现在开发态后端遇到端口没及时释放会在 6 秒内重试，红条也会在 SSE 重连后自动消失；跑长回合请用 aw（跑打包后的 dist，没有 watch 重启）。 Windows 上的 shell 解析、进程树回收、路径判断、权限与 CRLF 差异已全部收口在三个模块里：server/util/spawn-cli.ts（PATH/PATHEXT、.cmd 走 cmd.exe、killTree）、server/util/paths.ts 与 web/src/path-utils.ts（分隔符与绝对路径）、server/util/file-mode.ts（Windows 走 icacls）。改跨平台相关的代码先看这三个文件头。 License MIT

projects.summary: 阮老师好，自荐一个自己写的 macOS 应用，我是作者。 AgentHome：把 Claude Code、Codex、Gemini CLI 的会话收进本机归档，在同一块仪表盘上查看 token 用量、估算成本和剩余订阅额度。 做它有三个原因： 1. Claude Code 默认 30 天后删除会话记录，几个月前解决某个难题的那次对话，到时候就找不回来了。 2. 长会话每一轮都会从缓存重读一遍上下文，token 数字大得吓人，却和实际花费对不上。 3. 各家的 5 小时 / 7 天额度窗口分散在不同地方。 比 agent 清理活得久的归档：每份会话记录入库前先逐字节拷贝（zstd 压缩）到 ~/AgentHome/raw/，agent 删掉自己的文件后，副本还在。只拷贝，不改动 agent 的目录。 成本算得清：直接从会话记录里算 token，按模型、缓存档位分别计价，分项目、分模型统计，有 30 / 90 天趋势。 额度一眼看到：Claude 额度通过官方 claude CLI 的 /usage 读取，Codex 额度读它自己写进会话文件的快照。不读任何凭据，不调私有接口。 全文搜索：⌘K 跨全部消息搜索，支持中文子串，回车直接跳到那条消息。 菜单栏面板：点菜单栏的像素小屋，不用开主窗口就能看到今日成本、各家剩余额度和重置倒计时。 像素栖息地：左栏小屋里住着 Claude（狐狸）、Codex（企鹅）、Gemini（猫），会随真实的活动和额度工作、思考、疲惫或睡觉。 实时同步、中英双语界面，另附命令行工具；没有统计上报，数据不离开本机。 | 归档 | 会话详情 | |---|---| | | | 技术栈：Rust + GPUI Kit（Zed 编辑器的 GPUI 框架），原生 macOS 应用，Apache-2.0 许可证。

Some background on the development process: AppTraction started as a straight port of the App Store Connect website to a native Mac app, and for about two months that’s all it was. Right away it caught that Apple had featured my apps in Australia and the UK, which I’d been totally oblivious to. It also explained that my bread baking app’s sales decline (which I knew about) wasn’t a problem with the app at all, but a recurring seasonal slump, which is evidently typical for baking apps in the summer. projects.title: Show HN: Git-dupe – plain Git per-project private versioning for agent files
projects.author: WayHow
projects.summary: Hi HN! Suppose you have notes, skills, and agent instructions that are part of your personal workflow, so you do not want them committed to the public repo, but at the same time, you want them to be in the workspace at the correct locations (e.g., AGENTS.md file locations matter), and these files cannot be simply gitignored because you also want versioning for them. The solution to this is actually just a bit more plain Git. $ git status --short # public repo ?? AGENTS.md ?? notes/ $ git dupe init # private repo Initialized empty Git repository in /home/brian/code/project/.git/dupe/ $ git dupe add notes/ AGENTS.md # private repo hint: notes is now hidden from the project's Git; run from the root, 'git dupe unhide -- notes' stops hiding it $ git dupe commit -m "Notes and agent instructions" # private repo [main (root-commit) 3eb3af9] Notes and agent instructions 3 files changed, 3 insertions(+) create mode 100644 .gitdupe create mode 100644 AGENTS.md create mode 100644 notes/todo.md $ git status --short # public repo: nothing $ git dupe log --oneline # private repo: your files 3eb3af9 Notes and agent instructions The solution, in short, is versioning those agent files in a repo, say <private-repo> (this repo is private to you and holds the history for your agent files), and that repo shares the same worktree as the public repo <public-repo>. You essentially overlap the two, with <private-repo> put in .git/ (and .git/ is that of the public repo) for a convenient solution. If you want to read more about the strategy used, there is more comprehensive documentation in the repo. git-dupe supports macOS, Linux, and Windows and is under the MIT License.

projects.title: Show HN: Natel, a self-hosted contacts editor for CardDAV servers in 20MB of RAM
projects.author: Protectator
projects.summary: Hi HN, I decided to move away from Google Contacts and self-host my contacts two months ago. After installing a Radicale server, I was really missing a way to edit my contacts on the desktop. Nextcloud is overkilled for my needs, and InfCloud is the only other web contacts editor but it hasn't had a release in more than 10 years. So I built what was the missing piece in my setup : Natel, a lightweight self-hosted contacts editor for a CardDAV server. The goal is to edit your contacts on the web, be robust enough to not make you lose anything when there's an edit conflict with the server, and be super light in resources on the server. I came up with building a docker image of just a proxy caddy server and a go process that stores your credentials only in-memory, for a compressed image of less than 30MB and it uses less than 20MB of RAM when idle. Tested against four CardDAV servers : Nextcloud, Radicale, Baïkal and Xandikos. I already use it myself and it syncs with my server and DAVx5 back-and-forth, but I consider it still in beta and want to add more testing to prove compatibility for features I don't (yet ?) use. Note that any field that isn't displayed is never lost, it's just written back as-is. Demo: https://demo.natel.app/contacts Website: https://natel.app I wouldn't have done this side-project if I couldn't delegate writing the code to agents. We iterate on architectural decisions together, and once I'm satisfied with the direction, they write the result in a file (find it in docs/DECISIONS.md in the repo), then write the code to meet the expectations and independently review each other's iterations. I drive the project's direction and decisions, but I don't review the code myself. I keep an eye on the tests to know what's covered, and will read and review code when an agent draws my attention to it. The e2e tests were able to find a bug in SoGO, a CardDAV server : https://bugs.sogo.nu/view.php?id=6269 (and I didn't add that server in the compatilibity list yet because that bug breaks one the promises of the app, which is to be warned if we're trying to delete a contact that is modified elsewhere ; the server doesn't correctly enfore the If-Match instruction) As I don't have that many users yet, I welcome feedback on any part of the project but especially the parts that I have not yet tested like Contacts on a Mac !

projects.title: 【开源自荐】vmr：Rust 重写后，一个命令管理 80+ 种 SDK，还能装 conda-forge 的 3 万多个包

github.name: gvcgo/version-manager
github.description: 🔥 A general version manager for thousands of SDKs.

projects.summary: 最新版本：v0.8.1（2026-11-08） 收录说明：2024 年第 299 期收录过本项目的 Go 版本（当时支持 40 多种语言）。2026 年 11 月发布 Rust 重写版 v0.8，命令和磁盘布局保持兼容，但安装后端换成 pixi 的 Rust 组件（rattler），并新增了下面这些能力，故再次自荐。 一句话：一个命令行工具，同时管理 80+ 种语言和工具的版本，还能直接安装 conda-forge 上的 3 万多个包。 为什么需要它 nvm、pyenv、sdkman、rustup 各管一摊；想装 ffmpeg、cmake、ripgrep 之类的工具又要另找包管理器；conda 则是另一套几百 MB 的体系。vmr 把这些收进一个二进制：不需要管理员权限，所有版本放在 ~/.vmr 下，切换版本只是换一个软链接。 亮点 80+ 种语言和工具：Go、Node.js、Python、JDK、Rust、Zig、Bun、Deno、dotnet、PHP、R、Lua……以及 ripgrep、fzf、lazygit、neovim、ffmpeg、cmake 等常用 CLI 工具，共 82 个插件。 背靠 conda-forge：内置 pixi 同源的 rattler 后端，直接读取 conda-forge 的 repodata（linux-64 子目录压缩后约 60 MB），本地 zstd 缓存后用求解器装完整依赖闭包，不需要预装 conda/miniconda。按 2026-11 抓取的 repodata 统计，linux-64 + noarch 去重后共 34,598 个包名、约 120 万条构建记录；VMRPIXICHANNEL 可换清华等镜像。 项目级版本锁定：在项目里执行 vmr use -l node@20.11.0，会写入 .vmr.lock；之后 cd 进目录自动切到锁定版本，离开自动还原。lock 文件提交进仓库，队友进入目录即对齐版本。 切换立即生效，也能隔离：shell 集成让 vmr use 后的版本在当前终端马上可用，不用新开窗口；vmr use -s 只对当前子 shell 生效，退出自动恢复；vmr freeze 导出清单，新机器 vmr use -f 批量装回。 Rust 重写，下载更稳：单一可执行文件，多线程分块下载 + SHA256 校验，支持反向代理、本地代理与 HTTP(S)PROXY。Linux、macOS、Windows 的 x8664 与 aarch64 都有预编译包，Homebrew、Scoop、APT、pacman 可直接装。 vmr mcp：以 MCP 服务把「查版本、装版本、取 PATH / GOROOT」交给 AI 客户端调用。 快速上手 bash macOS / Linux brew install gvcgo/tap/vmr Windows: scoop bucket add gvcgo && scoop install gvcgo/vmr eval "$(vmr init zsh)" # 启用 cd 钩子，切换立即生效 vmr plugins # 支持的 SDK vmr search go && vmr use go@1.22.0 vmr use -l node@20.11.0 # 项目内锁定版本 vmr use -s python@3.12 # 只对当前会话生效 vmr search -p lua # 查 conda-forge vmr use -p lua@5.4.6 # 安装任意 conda-forge 包，无需装 conda
